News.title: Child who died in UK woodland was three-month-old baby girl & had been ‘camping with family’ before ‘unexplained’ death
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

DEATH PROBE Child who died in UK woodland was three-month-old baby girl & had been ‘camping with family’ before ‘unexplained’ death

COPS have confirmed that a three-month-old girl died in a woodland while camping with her family.

Emergency services rushed to Strawberry Lane, Great Wyrley in Staffordshire at 8.45am yesterday following reports of a child in cardiac arrest.



Midlands Air Ambulance attended the scene but sadly the child was pronounced dead by paramedics.

Roads around the area were closed throughout the day as detectives began piecing together what had happened.



Cops are still in the area today, carrying out enquiries to understand more about what happened.

The child’s tragic death is currently being treated as “unexplained” and a probe continues.



Detective Inspector Katie Gregory said: “While the investigation remains at an early stage, this is an isolated incident and we understand that the child’s family was camping in the area.

“The death is being treated as unexplained at this time.”

News.title: Driver who killed my brother fled UK & hasn’t spent a DAY in jail… now he’s flaunting his glam life online
News.content:
JACK Ryan’s sister went to court for every one of the nine days that the speeding driver who killed her brother was meant to be on trial – and every day she faced an empty dock.

Ciara Ryan, 34, along with the rest of her family listened as Rashid Ali’s barrister offered various excuses for why he could not attend from “stress” to visa issues.



On September 13, 2024, Ali was sentenced in his absence to five years for causing death by dangerous driving.

He is still to serve any of his sentence after he absconded to Pakistan before his trial, leaving Jack’s family without justice for his death.



The judge said he would be jailed should he return to the UK – but he never has, and has instead been living a globe-trotting life.

Heartbroken Ciara told The Sun she is “taunted” by Ali appearing to show off his “luxurious life” on social media.



And this includes trips to Dubai where he stayed in a hotel in the Burj Khalifa – all while claiming he is terminally ill and can’t return to the UK.

Jack’s family are now calling for a change in law which would make handing over your passport mandatory in a campaign called Justice for Jack Ryan.

Ali has previously insisted he would return to the UK – and said he could return in 2027, shamelessly adding he felt “sorry” for the family when confronted over a phone call.

Ciara told The Sun: ” In an ideal world, justice would be Mr Ali doing the moral thing and coming back and and serving time for his sentence, failing that, it would look like the measures being taken to extradite him and to bring him to the UK to to face his sentence.”

Jack was out for a run near his home in London at around 6pm on January 13, 2021.



While crossing the road by Battersea Bridge he was hit by Ali’s Range Rover and thrown into the air before landing in front of the car.

Ali called the emergency services but despite best efforts, Jack could not be saved and was declared dead at the scene at 6.36pm.

Ali – aged 26 at the time – and in the UK on a student visa – had driven through the traffic lights at 42mph while they were amber, despite them changing when he was 50 metres from the junction.

This was twice the area’s 20mph speed limit – and Ali originally told cops he was doing 30mph and had passed the light when it was green.

It took more than a year for Ali to be charged over Jack’s death Ciara said and due to delays from the pandemic, the trial at the Old Bailey did not begin in his absence until July 30, 2024.



Two days before the trial opened, Ciara said the police called her family with “good news and bad news” – telling them the while the trial was going ahead, Ali was not in the UK.

One of his reasons was said to be “stress”.

Ciara said: “It felt, pretty unbelievable that that was the reason.

“And look, I can also appreciate the amount of stress that he would have been under, and I also wanna say I know that he didn’t go out that day with the intention of killing somebody, and I’ve always said that.

“But I think there’s a selfishness that he has approached this with, which is thinking about himself and not thinking about us in any way, because, whatever stress he feels is nothing compared to what we’ve been through.”



What followed was a “farce” Ciara said, as the trial continued with no defendant and the jury could not be told the reason for his absence.

She said: “It feels again out of balance and that it’s almost balanced in the defendant’s favour, because the real reason that he’s not there is that he was too cowardly to attend his trial, but if you’re a jury and you don’t know that.”

Ciara said the delays gave Ali “confidence” and “gave him a period of time to live freely and to obviously think about what it would be like to continue living like that.”



She added: “I think the moment I knew that he wasn’t coming to court, that he wouldn’t be coming back at all.”

After the court proceedings, the Crown Prosecution Service barrister wished the family good luck with getting Ali back to the UK.

Ciara said “I had assumed that they would be helping us, so that made us feel very on our own.”

The constant updates and support stopped Ciara said and her family were left to navigate an “absolute minefield”.

“We have no real insight into what’s happening, no real sense of progress” she added.



Instead Jack’s family were left watching Ali’s movements on social media and reading his comments on news about the case in what feels like “a slap in the face”.

Ciara said she has even shown some of the posts to the CPS – in bid to spark them into action.

A Channel 4 Dispatches documentary broadcast in June found Ali had since travelled from Pakistan to Saudi Arabia, got married and even allegedly returned to the UK since being charged.



When the programme’s host Matt Shea managed to speak to Ali on the phone he claimed he was terminally ill with “tuberculosis and some other health issues.”

This, Ciara said she “found hard to believe” having seen “the social media of him living a very free and luxurious life.”

Ali said he had travelled to Saudi Arabia to complete the Islamic pilgrimage Umrah.

He told the programme that he “feels sorry” for Jack’s family and has informed the authorities he will “definitely” return in 2027.

While the family wanted to give the CPS and the police time to bring Ali back, after two years, Ciara said “that’s not happening, hence the need for us to try and take matters into our own hands.”



She added: “If his conscience is not weighing on him, then, nothing else is putting pressure on him at the moment.”

“The more that has been revealed around like Mr Ali and the life that he’s like living quite freely, the more I feel that sense of I need to do something because it just feels so unfair and so unjust.”

Ciara added that the current justice system is not working for victims and their families.



She said: “I’m frustrated by the fact that as loudly as I shout, no, no one is able to help.”

Having never interacted with the justice system before, Ciara trusted it would have all the correct measures in place but her experience has left her feeling failed.

Jack’s family are now campaigning for a change in law which would make handing over your passport mandatory.

The petition was launched alongside The Chelsea Citizen, after editor Rob McGibbon witnessed the aftermath of the collision, and calls for passport surrender to be an automatic bail condition.

The amendments have since gained support from Lord Michael Howard, who was home secretary when the 1993 Bail Act was passed.



In a letter to Shabana Mahmood, he asked: “The loophole is obviously something I should have thought of when I took the 1994 (sic) legislation through Parliament and much regret that I didn’t. Can you remedy my oversight.”

Gemma Davies Associate Professor in Criminal Law at Durham University said Pakistan can feel like a “safe haven” as there is no extradition treaty with the UK.

She added that “the more serious the offence the more likely someone would consider absconding to avoid a prison sentence”.

To prevent this “prosecutors need to ensure they have the right information about the Defendant” when bail conditions are set.

Jack, who now would be 34, and his partner Liz Austin were just one week from their first embryo transfer appointment when he was killed.



Liz gave birth to a daughter using embryos from before Jack’s death, in December 2021.

A Crown Prosecution Service spokesperson said: “The death of Jack Ryan was a wholly avoidable tragedy, and we ensured Rashid Ali was convicted in his absence for causing death by dangerous driving.

“The basis for applying for particular bail conditions is set out in the Bail Act which we considered carefully – this included taking into account Ali’s attendance at his previous court hearings – but final decisions about bail are ultimately a matter for the court.

“Our thoughts remain with Jack Ryan’s friends and family for their loss.”

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “Our thoughts remain with Jack’s family who are understandably still coming to terms with their loss. A specialist officer remains in place to provide them with support, as well as any relevant investigative updates.



“We understand the frustration when a defendant flees the country while on bail, and the distressing impact on the victim’s family.

“We continue to work closely with the Crown Prosecution Service and Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

“We cannot comment on extradition proceedings.”

The Sun reached out to the solicitor who represented Ali during the trial – and attempted to contact him via friends on social media, with his personal accounts now hidden.

The Sun has also reached out to Pakistan’s Ministry of Interior for comment.

News.title: Married couple arrested after living with dead body of elderly dad in ‘sick plot to keep claiming his pension’
News.content:
HAUNTING 'PLAN' Married couple arrested after living with dead body of elderly dad in ‘sick plot to keep claiming his pension’

A MARRIED couple have been arrested for living with the dead body of an elderly man in a sick plot to claim his pension, it is alleged.

The woman, 50, believed to be the man’s daughter, and her partner, 60, allegedly kept the corpse in a locked room in their Spanish home.



Police discovered the 88-year-old man’s body in an advanced state of decomposition after a tip-off from a neighbour.

Social services had raised the alarm after locals reported a foul smell coming from the property in Torrelavega, near the Cantabrian Coast.



Officers reportedly found the man’s body in a locked room with the entrance blocked.

Torrelavega councillor Pedro Perez Noriega described the condition of the home “deplorable”.

He said: “What we know for now is that the couple has been arrested and that they are also considering whether they suffer from some kind of mental disorder, because the truth is that the home was in a deplorable condition.”

At this stage there is no evidence to suggest the pensioner suffered a violent death, Spain’s National Police force said.

Investigators are probing how long the deceased man was kept inside the home.

The couple are set to appear in court on Monday.



They are likely to face charges of abandoning a person in an at-risk situation as well as Social Security fraud.

The pair also face a charge of misappropriation of assets.

A source close to the ongoing inquiry told a local paper the couple had confessed to hiding the OAP’s body after he died of “natural causes”.

They also reportedly admitted to keeping the body so they could carry on claiming his pension, it is alleged.

The source said: “The conditions they lived in were not those of normal people, and the possibility that there may be something more is being considered, which is why they want to rule out other issues with an psychiatric examination.”



It remains unclear how much pension money the pair allegedly claimed before cops discovered the OAP’s body.

The dead man was a former worker at the Reocin Mine in Cantabria – once the largest zinc deposit in Europe.

The shocking case comes after an Italian man was accused of dressing up as his dead mother to fraudulently claim her pension.

The 56-year-old successfully pocketed thousands in pension payments before he was eventually exposed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His mother, Graziella Dall’Oglio, died three years earlier at the age of 82.



When she passed away, her son wrapped her body in a bed sheet, stuffed it in a sleeping bag and hid it away in his house.

News.title: Do you care about the Reform UK donations row? VOTE NOW
News.content:
NIGEL Farage has found himself at the heart of another dodgy donations scandal following an undercover sting operation.

An undercover Channel 4 report appears to show two senior Reform figures arranging for a US firm to fund three polls earlier this year, costing £32,500.



James Orr, head of policy, and Dan Jukes, a senior aide to Mr Farage, have both stepped back amid an internal investigation.

Mr Farage has insisted: “The party has done nothing wrong, taken no illegal money. In fact no money was taken at all.”



Speaking at his party conference this weekend, he dismissed the allegations as “a little local difficulty” and described the reports as “an exercise in entrapment”.

He added the row was built on nothing but “loose pub talk” – but it follows other probes including questions over a £5million gift which led to his resignation and re-election as an MP.

News.title: Trump’s peace envoys race to Kyiv after ‘constructive & useful’ talks with Putin as 3-day capital truce hangs in balance
News.content:
DONALD Trump’s peace envoys have raced to Kyiv just 24 hours after holding “constructive and useful” talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

The crunch diplomatic negotiations come during a fragile three-day truce between Russia and Ukraine in which both sides have promised not to attack each other’s capitals.



A smiling Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv this morning to hold talks with Ukraine’s top officials over the war just hours after departing Moscow following “substantive” talks in the Kremlin.

Volodymyr Zelensky said he and his aides were preparing to have a “meaningful conversation”.



The trip marks the first official visit to Ukraine for the two close Trump aides as they arrived after a mammoth 11-hour train journey from Rzeszów in Poland.

The US officials had wanted to fly from Moscow but were forced to make the gruelling train journey out of fear of a Russian aerial attack.

Zelensky said: “Unfortunately, through their strikes, the Russians demonstrated that [the visitors] could not land and use an aircraft, although our airports remain operational.”

They said they hoped for “equally productive meetings” in Ukraine today.



A Putin aide described the three-hour talks on Saturday as “timely and highly useful” as the tyrant himself praised Trump’s peace efforts on state TV.

It comes as Moscow officials hinted that a meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and China’s tyrant ruler Xi Jinping may be on the cards soon.

Donald Trump previously claimed that Witkoff and Kushner – who is also his son in law – are bringing with them “a proposal to end the war”.



But a Kremlin insider said Putin was desperate to capture more territory before any peace deal could be struck.

He said: “There is no chance of reaching an agreement regarding the frontline until Putin finishes securing the remaining part of the Donetsk region.”

It comes after Zelensky declared a three-day ceasefire on Friday – which Putin swiftly violated by launching drone strikes mere hours later.

An 11-year-old child was among those killed in a strike on Saturday night during the time US envoys were being hosted by the Kremlin.

The Ukrainian president also accused Putin of drone-bombing two Kyiv airports on Friday to prevent Trump’s envoys from landing.



Zelensky said: “It is clear that these Russian strikes on airports are a reaction to discussions and preparations regarding the possibility of the American side using an aircraft to arrive in Ukraine and land at either Kyiv or Boryspil airport.”

On Thursday Putin told an international economic forum that “there are chances” a peace deal could be reached.

But the Russian tyrant showed no sign of backing down from his territorial demands in Ukraine – which have previously stunted peace negotiations.

After Zelensky’s first ceasefire lay violated, the leaders struck a new deal not to bomb one another’s capital cities ahead of the talks.



Bloodthirsty Putin snubbed the second deal – and rained down drones on the headquarters of Ukraine’s state security service (SBU) on Friday.

At least seven people were injured in the attack on the building in Kyiv, across from the historic St Sophia Cathedral.

Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the attack a “major escalation” that came as potential peace talks were gaining momentum.

“Moscow launched this strike during a renewed push for peace – laying bare its true rejection of diplomacy,” he said in a post on X.



More than 1.5million people have so far been killed in the war as the wail of air-raid sirens become a part of daily life in Kyiv.

On the frontline, Russia is struggling to capture new territory and Ukraine is standing strong in its fortress cities of Kramatorsk, Sloviansk and Kostiantynivka.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Putin’s war machine continues to churn – as nearly 250 smaller combat battles have been recorded in the last 24 hours.

Mad Vlad’s armies reportedly dropped 288 guided bombs, launched 87 air strikes and deployed more than 8,000 drones during this period.

News.title: Iran ‘plotting October 7-style attack on Israel alongside terror proxies Hezbollah, Hamas & Houthis’ as US war rages on
News.content:
IRAN is plotting a terrifying October 7-style attack on Israel using its sprawling network of terror proxies, intelligence in Tel Aviv has claimed.

The Islamic Republic has allegedly held meetings and training exercises with terrorist groups to prepare for a repeat of the horror Hamas’ attacks in 2023.



Hezbollah in Lebanon, Hamas, the Houthis in Yemen and regional militias will join forces with Iran’s army under the plans, the Jerusalem Post reports.

Iran’s alleged plot comes as the regime’s war with the US continues to spiral out of control.



The reeling regime is now looking to its regional allies to bolster its forces and weapon stockpiles.

Israeli intelligence claims Iran has hosted multiple meetings with Hezbollah, Houthi and Iraqi militia leaders about an escalation against Israel.



The terrorist proxies have also reportedly taken part in joint training exercises with Iranian forces.

Meanwhile the Islamic Regime has ramped up drone and missile production to replenish its dwindling reserves, the outlet reports.



Hamas documents seized in the Gaza Strip after the attack on October 7, 2023, reportedly suggest plans sought to expand the confrontation after the initial attack.

But Hamas launched its murderous rampage without the other fronts opening, the outlet reports.

The attacks killed 1,200 Israelis, kidnapped 250, and left thousands of others wounded, sparking the ongoing Israeli-Palestinian war.

One of the planning documents allegedly stressed the need to “connect and prepare the external fronts”.

The document also discussed the need to agree on communication mechanisms for the allies in wartime, the outlet reported.



The chilling warning comes as Iran said its forces struck an unmanned US vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday.

The history of Israel and Iran's relationship THERE'S been an ongoing conflict between Israel (left) and Iran (right). In 1947, Iran was among 13 countries that voted against the United Nations Partition Plan for the British Mandate of Palestine. Two years later, Iran also voted against Israel’s admission to the United Nations. After the 1979 Islamic Revolution, Iran severed all diplomatic and commercial ties with Israel, and its theocratic government does not recognise the legitimacy of Israel as a state. The turn from cold peace to open hostility began in the early 1990s, shortly after the collapse of the Soviet Union and the defeat of Iraq in the Gulf War, after which relative power in the Middle East shifted to Iran and Israel. CONFLICT ‘HEATS UP’ The conflict escalated in the early 1990s, as Yitzhak Rabin’s government adopted a more aggressive posture on Iran. Rhetorical conflict heated up during the presidency of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, who made inflammatory statements against Israel. Other factors that have contributed to the escalation of bilateral tensions include Iran’s development of nuclear technology relative to Israel’s long-stated Begin Doctrine, Iran’s funding of Islamist groups such as Hezbollah, Palestinian Islamic Jihad and Hamas, as well as alleged involvement in terrorist attacks such as the 1992 attack on Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires and the 1994 AMIA bombing, and Israel’s alleged support for militant groups such as the People’s Mujahedin of Iran and Jundallah as well as alleged covert Israeli operations in Iran including multiple assassinations and bombings. ‘COMPLEX AND ONGOING’ Since 1985, Iran and Israel have been engaged in an ongoing proxy conflict that has greatly affected the geopolitics of the Middle East, and has included direct military confrontations between Iranian and Israeli organisations, such as in the 2006 Lebanon War. The conflict has played out in various ways, including through support for opposing factions in conflicts in Syria and Yemen. Iran has provided support to the Syrian government, while Israel has supported opposition groups. In Yemen, Iran has provided support to the Houthi rebels, while Israel has provided support to the Saudi-led coalition fighting the rebels. The conflict has also involved cyber attacks and sabotage against each other’s infrastructure, including attacks on nuclear facilities and oil tankers. Overall, the Iran-Israel proxy conflict is a complex and ongoing conflict that has had a significant impact on the political and security dynamics of the Middle East. INSIDE THE WAR In the Israeli–Lebanese conflict, Iran has supported Lebanese Shia militias, most notably Hezbollah. In the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Iran has backed Palestinian groups such as Hamas. Israel has supported Iranian rebels, such as the People’s Mujahedin of Iran, conducted airstrikes against Iranian allies in Syria and assassinated Iranian nuclear scientists. In 2018, Israeli forces directly attacked Iranian forces in Syria. Iranian Islamists have long championed the Palestinian people, whom they perceive as “oppressed”. Scholars believe that by supporting the Palestinians, Iran seeks greater acceptance among Sunnis and Arabs, both of whom dominate the Middle East. Ideologically, Iran seeks to replace Israel with a one-state solution and has predicted Israel’s demise. Israel sees Iran as an existential threat, and accuses its regime of harbouring genocidal intentions. Consequently, Israel has sought sanctions and military action against Iran to stop it from acquiring nuclear weapons.

Hours earlier, the US military said its forces blasted three Iranian oil tankers in response to a missile attack on Navy warships.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) said the tankers were part of a shadow network funding Iran’s Revolutionary Guard and its armed proxies.

The strikes came nearly a week after the US and Iran resumed attacks following a month of relative calm.



As tensions flare, US President Donald Trump declared he may strike Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site.

Iran’s nuclear programme, the issue that sparked the war in February, was meant to be addressed in negotiations.

But talks fell apart soon after the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Instead, Tehran’s new leverage focuses on the Strait of Hormuz – a crucial waterway used to transport oil and natural gas.

The US military has been helping guide ships through the strait as Tehran continues to assert its control and targets vessels.

News.title: Lamborghini worth £240k seized by cops after being ‘driven 80mph in a 30mph zone’ by idiot driver
News.content:
A LAMBORGHINI worth over £200,000 has been seized by cops after it was caught driving at speeds suspected to be more than twice the limit.

Shocked residents in Southend made multiple calls to Essex Police on Saturday afternoon after reports of the supercar speeding in the area.



It is understood the Lamborghini Huracan was being driven at about 80mph in a 30mph zone.

Officers then seized the supercar from the reckless driver under tougher laws introduced to crack down on dangerous driving.



The Lamborghini Huracan has an on-the-road recommended retail price of £238,195, depending on the version, according to Autotrader.

It was seized under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, which was strengthened earlier this year to give police more seizure powers.

Drivers who drive their cars in a reckless way by wheel-spinning and causing burnouts, drifting in public places, racing in residential areas or repeatedly revving their engines could have their vehicle seized.

Before the changes, drivers could only have their car confiscated if they were involved in another antisocial driving incident within the past 12 months.

Officers can still choose to give a warning to motorists at their discretion.

A spokesman for Essex Police said: “Antisocial driving can pose a danger to other people using the road and cause misery to residents.



“The safety of our communities will always be our priority and we’ll take action against those who risk the safety of others.”

According to Essex Police’s website, under the new legislation, the owner of a seized vehicle has to attend the car pound within seven working days and with the correct documentation.

It comes after a number of luxury motors were seized by cops after they were caught wheel-spinning, weaving and slowing down to speeds of 17mph on a major motorway.



One clip shows Lamborghinis and a Mercedes G-Wagon being stopped by police in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, on Wednesday evening.

Cops shared the footage, which was captured just before 7pm, on social media after a number of people were prosecuted for driving dangerously on the M66 and M62.

The high-powered supercars were first spotted speeding on the M66 motorway.

Police said the cars were seen weaving across lanes, wheel spinning and slowing down to speeds of around 17mph on the motorway.

The vehicles were then spotted on the M62, with officers deployed to bring them to a stop.



Two Lamborghinis were stopped as they came off the motorway.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Officers then brought the remaining vehicles to a stop on Edinburgh Way in Rochdale.

Five Lamborghini’s and a Mercedes G-Wagon were seized and police prosecuted the drivers for a number of driving offences.

News.title: Bodies found of two missing fishermen who vanished when trawler sank in English Channel eight days ago
News.content:
CHANNEL TRAGEDY Bodies found of two missing fishermen who vanished when trawler sank in English Channel eight days ago

THE bodies of two French fishermen who went missing after a French fishing boat sank in the English Channel have been recovered.

The vessel, which was carrying five people, had reported a problem with its fishing gear and run into trouble off the coast of Plymouth, Devon, on August 29.

Three of the five crew members were rescued by a nearby vessel and a major search operation was launched for the other two but suspended after two days.

Alex Dehays, deputy prosecutor in Saint-Brieuc, said the bodies were found yesterday after weather conditions cleared up allowing divers to resume.





A coastguard helicopter, fixed wing aircraft and two RNLI lifeboats began the “extensive search” near Eddystone lighthouse at around 6pm on August 29.

The huge rescue effort continued through the night, with more than 15 lifeboats and a French warship drafted in.

A large number of civilian boats, including fishing vessels also joined the efforts – and the French Navy’s Falcon 50 was deployed to the scene.

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency said in an earlier statement: “HM Coastguard maintained the intensive search during the night and it is continuing today with multiple assets sent to help with the search.



“Three people were rescued last evening from the French-registered fishing vessel which had made the call for help.

“They were taken to hospital for further care. The search is continuing for two further people who remain unaccounted for.

“The vessel has sunk.”

News.title: Boy, two, killed in horror hit-and-run near his Limerick home as he played on toy tractor
News.content:
Boy, two, killed in horror hit-and-run near his Limerick home as he played on toy tractor

Peter Mulcaire was tragically pronounced dead after he suffered catastrophic injuries when he was struck by a Jeep in Rathkeale, Co Limerick

View Image Gardaí rushed to the scene in Limerick (stock image) (Image: PA)

A two-year-old boy has died after being struck by a car in a horror hit-and-run.

Little Peter Mulcaire had been playing on a toy tractor when he was struck by a Jeep near his home in Rathkeale, Co Limerick, the Irish Mirror reports. Gardaí (Irish Police) said the vehicle involved did not remain at the scene after the collision at 4pm on Saturday.

The boy was flown by air ambulance to University Hospital Limerick with serious injuries but was later pronounced dead.

A male driver of the vehicle, aged in his 30s, was arrested at a different location by Gardaí on suspicion of driving under the influence of an intoxicant.

He was taken to a Garda Station in County Limerick to provide a blood/urine sample and was later released pending analysis of that test.

A Rathkeale community fun day, which had been scheduled for Sunday, was cancelled by the organisers "out of respect" to the boy and his family and the "tragic circumstances" of his death.

Friends and relatives of the boy posted photographs of him on social media and shared their sympathies and shock with his family.

"Never in my life seen sadder, may u get best bed Peter only a baby…heartbreaking," stated a relative. Another stated: "Heartbreaking…rest in peace baby Peter."

Article continues below

A neighbour of the boy’s family, wrote: "l've never see sadder, rest in peace to our little neighbour Peter, may God comfort his family tonight. I'm so sorry for year loss, my heart breaks for his family, a little angel."

News.title: Nigel Farage accused of 'laughing off' dodgy donations allegations in car crash TV interview
News.content:
Nigel Farage accused of 'laughing off' dodgy donations allegations in car crash TV interview

Nigel Farage has been forced to deny he is 'laughing' off an alleged dodgy donations scandal that saw two senior Reform figures step down from their posts

Nigel Farage laughs off questions about donations scandal

Nigel Farage has been forced to deny he is “laughing” off an alleged dodgy donations scandal that saw two senior Reform figures step down from their posts.

‌



The Reform UK leader gave a hearty laugh as he said Reform had “a few little local difficulties” during its annual conference.

‌



During the three-day gathering in Birmingham, which came to an end on Saturday, long-standing aide Dan Jukes and policy chief James Orr left their posts after an undercover sting appeared to show the pair discussing how to disguise donations from foreign donors. Scotland Yard has said it is assessing reports that senior figures sought to evade electoral law over donations.

‌



In an interview with the BBC, Mr Farage laughed after he said: "It's a big conference, energetic conference. We had a bad start with a few little local difficulties." BBC host Laura Kuenssberg snapped back: “It’s a bit more than a few little local difficulties, isn’t it? You've lost two of your most senior people. You can't just laugh it off.”

He replied: “I’m not laughing it off. You lose people in life, in business, in politics. It happens for all sorts of reasons.” It followed him claiming he "wasn't listening" during the meeting that sparked the party's donor drama, as well as dismissing it as "loose pub talk".

8 weird and sinister moments from Reform conference - from free speech to flags READ MORE :

View Image Nigel Farage - who lapped up the attention at Reform conference - dismissed an alleged donations scandal as 'loose pub talk' (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



During the interview, Mr Farage was torn apart after moaning that questions being asked about Reform’s finances are a "tactic" used against the party. He was asked what “evidence” he has that Reform is being unfairly treated and it was pointed out that those in power all undergo intense scrutiny, such as Keir Starmer facing questions about a field for donkeys that he bought for his parents in 1996 or Zack Polanski being scrutinised over whether he should have paid council tax on a house boat.

But Mr Farage said other politicians have not faced “an attempt to wipe them out of society” and referred to claims of Reform politicians being "debanked". A probe in 2023 criticised NatWest Group's decision to shut down Mr Farage's bank account.

He added: "There is no doubt there is huge political prejudice against Reform right across the corporate world and right across the establishment. And that is a simple fact of life. And why? Because we're the disruptors and that's the way it works."

‌



Asked about the investigation into a £5million gift he received shortly before the 2024 general election, Mr Farage complained: "We will be investigated every week between now and the next election. That is the tactic that is being used against us."

Told there appeared to be a pattern of serious questions about how Reform handles its finance, the Clacton MP said Britain is a "complainant society", adding: "It will never end. This has been a deliberate attempt to do this to us. If we get things wrong, if we make mistakes and do things that are wrong, I will hold my hands up and admit that. But frankly, the other things that have been talked about, I don’t believe we have any guilt at all. None whatsoever. Absolutely none."

Robert Jenrick, Reform's Treasury spokesman, on Sunday said "lessons need to be learnt" from the donations row. The Tory turncoat said: " We're going to investigate exactly what happened. It's right to have due process. But this is not the way that Reform conducts itself. Like any political party, we seek to abide by the law at all times, and we believe we have in this case.

‌



"In fact, I've reviewed the legal advice from the KC who's advised the party in the last 48 hours, and it shows that, yeah, we did. But do we want to be the best version of ourselves. Yes, absolutely. And no doubt there will be lessons to be learnt from this. But we do have a strong compliance department and in fact we turn away donations all the time from people who are impermissible."

Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said: "Nigel Farage will blame anyone apart from himself. Sooner or later he needs to wake up and realise the buck stops with him. It's time he stopped the desperate deflection tactics and took responsibility for the many scandals he and Reform are now drowning in.

"Reform wanted the past few days to show Farage was ready to be Prime Minister. In reality they've exposed how completely unfit he is for office.

Article continues below

“While Reform is consumed by chaos and scandal, Andy Burnham is focused on what matters: easing the cost of living and driving growth in every postcode across Britain."

News.title: Strictly rehearsals suffer setback as two stars forced to pull out
News.content:
Strictly rehearsals suffer setback as two stars forced to pull out

Strictly stars Katya Jones, 37, and ex-husband Neil, 44, were both injured and forced to pull out of rehearsals

View 3 Images Katya Jones was injured and forced to pull out of rehearsals (Image: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire)

Rehearsals for the new Strictly series didn't get off to the best start last week after two fan favourites were unable to take part.

‌



Katya Jones, 37, and ex-husband Neil, 44, were both injured and forced to pull out of rehearsals, it has been reported.

‌



It came at the worst time for the former couple, as it also meant that they missed out on a number of pre-recorded group routines.

‌



While they both returned to dancing on Friday, the damage could have already been done as it may jeopardise their chances of being paired with a celebrity. This will be particularly devastating for Neil, who didn't get a partner last year.

A source told The Sun: "There was a real crisis on set when both Neil and Katya were injured at the same time and there were concerns they wouldn’t be able to recover in time for the series start in two weeks."

First Strictly 2026 trailer introduces new hosts and teases glitzy revamp READ MORE :

View 3 Images Neil won't feature in as many group numbers (Image: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire)

‌



They added that Katya and Neil were "gutted" to miss out on the group dances as it "guarantees screen time if they don't get a partner, which Neil often doesn't".

The Mirror has reached out to the BBC for comment.

It comes after Strictly released its very first trailer on Saturday introducing the new hosts with as much glitz and glamour as expected.

‌



High-octane from the off, fans were treated to energetic performances by the pro dancers down the backstage of Elstree as glitter was thrown in the air and chandeliers rolled into shot. The infamous Glitterball also made an appearance, with judge Craig Revel Horwood attempting to smash it with a sledge hammer while co-stars Shirley Ballas and Anton Du Beke showed off their dance skills.

View 3 Images Strictly released their new trailer on Saturday (Image: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire)

The trailer concluded by introducing its brand news hosts Johannes Radebe, Emma Willis and Josh Widdicombe, who held hands as they made their way down the brightly lit stairs. The trio are taking over from Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman after they quit the BBC show last year.

‌



As part of a huge revamp, bosses also axed long-standing professionals, Karen Hauer, Gorka Márquez, Nadiya Bychkova, Luba Mushtuk, and Michelle Tsiakkas in favour of new talent. While former Strictly contestant Ellie Taylor replaces Janette Manrara and Fleur East.

Sharing the trailer online, Strictly declared: "Let's get this party started!"

Fans were ecstatic, flocking to the comments to share their thoughts, with one writing: "So, so excited for this to start, I literally look forward to strictly every year.." While another commented: "YES YES YES WE ARE SO BACK."

Article continues below

The BBC competition kicks off with a pre-recorded show on September 19 with the star-studded line-up - including EastEnders’ Lacey Turner, Love Island winner Dani Dyer and singer Delta Goodrem - learning who they will be partnered up with.

News.title: Woman who won £115million on lottery has given half of it away
News.content:
Woman who won £115million on lottery has given half of it away

The money is supporting good causes near where she lives

View 5 Images Frances Connolly, who won £115m on the lottery in 2019, as she launches her latest charity venture

A National Lottery winner who has given away half of her £115 million winnings has said it is human nature to help others. Frances Connolly has set up a charitable trust to support good causes since winning the enormous EuroMillions jackpot with husband Paddy in 2019.

‌



In honour of her 60th birthday, seven athletes who appreciated her support for young sporting talent will undertake a series of gruelling challenges to raise money for the couple’s PFC Trust, which funds good causes in the North East of England. Frances, who was a social worker and teacher, helped others from a young age while she was growing up in Northern Ireland, well before the life-changing lottery win.

‌



Her father was a fan of country and western music, with Dolly Parton a favourite. Frances described the singer, who died last month aged 80, as an “inspiration” for her philanthropy. After Parton’s death, it was said she could have been a billionaire had she not given so much of her wealth away to causes such as child literacy.

‌



View 5 Images Frances Connolly at Middlesbrough Velodrome.

Frances and Paddy estimate they have given away half of their lottery winnings over the years. Frances, a grandmother who has three daughters, told the PA news agency: “It depends on what you want in life. If your ambition is to be the richest person in the world and be influencing presidents, then you need to keep all your money, or you need to keep a lot of your money.

“But I don’t know anybody who doesn’t share something. I think it’s in mankind to share when you get to a level where you’ve got enough. ’Enough’ is a different level for everybody.

‌



“Maybe if we had been younger I’d have kept more, maybe you’d be a bit more nervous about how much you could give away, but unless I intended to live forever – I was 50-whatever when I won it – so even being generous, I was well over half-way through. So as long as the kids are sorted and they had enough to live comfortable, nice lives, I didn’t see the point.”

View 5 Images Frances Connolly has set up a charitable trust to support good causes since winning the enormous EuroMillions jackpot

Paddy continues to run plastics businesses and the couple enjoy good holidays and have a large house on Teesside, but they remain aware of value for money, buying a second hand Cartier watch or a used Aston Martin. She said: “We have a lovely life. I always tell people, we have the same life, we just live it bigger. You know, we haven’t particularly changed, if you talk to my friends.”

‌



Frances was delighted with the support of the athletes taking part in the 60 for 60 Challenge, where the team will run, swim or cycle a total of 60 miles. Starting with a family fun day at Middlesbrough Velodrome on Sunday, there will be a series of tough events, culminating in a team taking on the Great North Run for the trust.

She said: “They wanted to put something back into the community, and I’m delighted, I couldn’t have been given a better present. I am at pains to explain to people that despite being a millionaire, I can’t cure poverty, and I certainly can’t do everything that’s needed to be done on my own.

View 5 Images Seven athletes who appreciated her support for young sporting talent will undertake a series of gruelling challenges

‌



“I have a team of hundreds of people who work with me all the time. I put a message out – ‘we’re having a fun day on Sunday’ – there’s people baking cakes for us, people turning up to sell raffle tickets. We have 50 volunteers that come on the night of our ball.

“I get help and support every single day. I think people just need to be asked, and they just need to have that opportunity to do exactly what I do and change lives.”

View 5 Images Frances Connolly

Article continues below

The trust has bought respite caravans so young carers can take a proper break, funded loneliness projects and digital tech for older people, delivered emergency food parcels, and put defibrillators into local sports clubs. Paul Hewitson, who will take on the Great North Run for the trust, said: “She has set such an example, and we wanted to help through sport, as we all know how vital it is for young people to live healthier lives.”

To donate, visit justgiving.com/campaign/60for60challenge

News.title: Brit dad who killed Airbnb host before setting her Australia home on fire asked police odd question
News.content:
Brit dad who killed Airbnb host before setting her Australia home on fire asked police odd question

Mother-of-Maree Vermont, 60, three was killed inside the home she had designed and built over decades, with the fire causing such extensive damage that experts could not determine her cause of death

View 3 Images Timothy Loosemore was convicted over manslaughter (Image: Darcy Vermont)

A British man convicted of killing his Australian Airbnb host showed little concern for her when questioned by the police - instead asking a bizarre question.

‌



Timothy Loosemore, 63, killed mother-of-three Maree Vermont, 60, at her rural Victorian home before the property was destroyed by fire. The Somerset man was cleared of murder but convicted of manslaughter and is now awaiting sentence over Maree’s death at her home in Goldie, north of Melbourne.

‌



Loosemore had initially arrived as a guest while cycling around Australia before he and Maree became involved in what the court heard was a casual relationship. But prosecutors said he wanted the relationship to become more serious and “snapped” after Maree repeatedly rejected his advances, they said he had violently attacked Maree before setting fire to the property in an attempt to conceal what had happened.

‌



Her body was burned beyond recognition in the blaze, making it impossible for forensic experts to determine her cause of death.

View 3 Images Maree was remembered by her family as "peaceful and loving" (Image: Darcy Vermont)

Crocodile handler dies after being brutally mauled at Papua New Guinea wildlife park READ MORE :

In the hours after the fire, Loosemore was taken to Royal Melbourne Hospital, where officers arrived to question him about what had happened, he showed little to no concern about Maree. Body-worn camera footage later played in court showed his first question was about Maree’s 14-year-old dog Maxie. Loosemore asked: “Who’s looking after Maxie?”

‌



An officer replied: “I don’t know. Who normally looks after him?” Loosemore said: “Normally Maree. He’s 14 years old so he’s got some dental problems so he’s not a well dog … I suppose Maree’s looking after him?” Only afterwards did he ask: “Is Maree all right? Is she?”

His behaviour following the blaze was later raised during a pre-sentence hearing, where the court heard Loosemore had also appeared concerned about his bicycle and other possessions. Justice Tinney said: “His only concern was for himself and his bicycle and his other possessions. That struck me as being somewhat unnerving.

“Here he was, a person who claimed to be innocent, who had been involved in a relationship of sorts with Ms Vermont, and he knew that the house was on fire and that she was inside the house.”

‌



Crown prosecutor Mark Gibson, KC, said: “He did something horrific to Maree Vermont. Something he needed to conceal from the world. That something was him physically attacking Maree inside that house during which he killed Maree Vermont. An attack with murderous intent.”

Maree’s blood was later discovered across Loosemore’s trousers and T-shirt, while evidence heard during the trial suggested she had fought back. Her body was found face down in the living room, where three kitchen knives were also discovered. But the extent of the fire meant forensic experts were unable to establish precisely how Maree died, leaving jurors unable to find Loosemore guilty of murder.

View 3 Images Maree had only recently finished work on parts of her beloved home (Image: Darcy Vermont)

‌



Justice Tinney said: “Because he has never told the truth about what occurred, the mechanism of the actual death will remain unclear to everyone other than Mr Loosemore.”

The fire also destroyed a home which had been a huge part of Maree’s life. A surveyor by profession, she had moved to the property with her then-husband in her 20s and raised their three sons there. The family spent more than 30 years creating the stone house using salvaged materials, with Maree reportedly putting the finishing touches to its lead-light window trims just a week before her death.

Her son Darcy Vermont said: “She adored the house and it was beautiful. She was really proud of her work.”

‌



Loosemore has maintained he cannot remember killing Maree, although the court heard he gave several different accounts of what happened around the time of the blaze. He told neighbour Peter Greenham that he and Maree had a “small argument” before he went outside to collect wood and returned to find the property burning. Another neighbour, Kynan Share was given a similar account.

But on another occasion he claimed he had been upstairs asleep before getting up to put wood on the fire and discovering the house engulfed in flames when he returned. His barrister Christopher Farrington told the court Loosemore had consistently maintained that he had “no memory of what took place”, which was why he had not accepted responsibility or expressed remorse. Justice Tinney asked Mr Farrington: “Isn’t it all much more consistent with a person who has simply been refusing to tell the truth about what occurred?”

Loosemore had no previous criminal history and people who knew him before Maree’s death, including some of her friends and relatives, described him as polite, calm and helpful. Originally from a rural community in Somerset, he previously ran a civil construction business in Britain. His family had lived in Western Australia from 2004 to 2007 and became Australian citizens before returning to the UK.

‌



He returned to Australia with his son in September 2022 for a cycling trip. After his son left, Loosemore continued travelling alone and stayed at properties where he carried out work in return for accommodation and food - like the arrangement he had at Maree's.

Maree’s loved ones have since spoken about the devastating loss of the woman they described as peaceful, loving and caring. Her son Darcy said outside court: “It’s a very hard day. But it’s bringing some sense of closure to be able to get up in court and have our voices heard.”

Darcy previously said the manslaughter verdict had been “upsetting and distressing”. He said: “It was an unlawful, violent assault that killed her, and then burning of the house meant there was not enough evidence to suffice intent of murder. We have to accept what we can get.”

Article continues below

Maree’s son Harrison said the destruction of so many family photographs in the fire had made reflecting on their mother’s life and work even more important. He said: “The loss is just devastating, especially to us kids. She was just … she was our mum. She was beautiful.”

News.title: Man ordered to demolish 'summer house' built in back garden
News.content:
Man ordered to demolish 'summer house' built in back garden

The council has refused to grant permission for the building

View 4 Images A man has been told to demolish an “inappropriate” annexe built without permission in the garden of a city home

A man has been ordered to demolish the summer house built in his back garden after planners said it detracted from the 'pattern of development' in the local area.

‌



Aron Davis, 36, erected the L-shaped one-storey building behind his four-bedroom end-terrace home in Warndon, Worcester, without planning permission. He described it as a summer house but the council says it is "self-contained residential accommodation".

‌



The building comprises a bedroom and a kitchen/lounge with wet room. Worcester City Council rejected a retrospective application and launched enforcement action demanding the building be torn down.

‌



View 4 Images City planners rejected retrospective plans for the annexe, built at the back of the property

Planners said the development "reduces the amount of space available for soft landscaping and detracts from the established pattern of development in the area."

They also raised concerns over its proximity to a mature oak tree protected by a Tree Preservation Order in the grounds of neighbouring Oasis Academy Warndon. Planning officers said: "This tree is substantial in size and is highly visible within the public realm. It thus makes an important and positive contribution to the visual amenity and character of the area."

‌



Mr Davis, director of a civil engineering company, built a two-storey extension at the side of his property in 2023 which was granted planning permission. But he fell foul of planners when he built the large annexe in his back garden which he claimed was a "summer house".

View 4 Images The development can be seen in the back garden

He appealed after the council refused permission, but planning inspector S Edwards dismissed the challenge in 2024. A second appeal against the enforcement notice has now also been rejected by planning inspector SA Hanson.

‌



The inspector ruled on August 28 that the council's six-month deadline to demolish the building was "reasonable and proportionate". In the decision notice, the inspector said: "The appellant seeks a compliance period of between six and nine months.

"It is argued that additional time is required to design and implement revised works, engage contractors, arrange lawful removal of materials and ensure that any demolition works are undertaken carefully to avoid harm to the nearby protected tree. The appellant has not demonstrated why this period would be insufficient to undertake the demolition, site clearance and lawful disposal of materials required by the notice.

"While I acknowledge that appropriate care may be required when carrying out works in proximity to the protected tree, I have seen no substantial evidence that a longer period is necessary."

‌



View 4 Images Aron Davis says it is not worth fighting

Mr Davis said he had originally planned to rent out the annexe while using a summer house in the garden for leisure and entertaining. He said: "I bought the property and developed with a view to letting it out with a summer house in the back to use for leisure and an entertaining space but that has not happened. I'm not going to fight it [the council] any more, it's not worth it so that's that."

Article continues below

When planners first threw out the scheme in 2023, they concluded the annexe was effectively a separate house because it was detached from the main property, had its own power supply and could potentially have separate access.

The council said: "The proposed works, which are largely complete, result in the creation of an additional independent residential unit which is considered inappropriate in terms of the detriment caused to the amenities of the surrounding residents with regard to additional noise and general disturbance.

"The development results in overdevelopment of the site and this is clear by the lack of private amenity space which can be accommodated on the size of the plot for both existing and potential residents."

News.title: Bride and groom end up in river after accident taking wedding photographs
News.content:
Bride and groom end up in river after accident taking wedding photographs

The wedding day also featured a forgotten bouquet, torrential rain, a burnt foot and a broken leg

Bride and groom end up in river after accident taking wedding photographs

A bride and groom accidentally fell into a river in full wedding attire while having their photos taken standing on a canoe.

‌



Jamie Wade, 46, and his new bride Michelle, also 46, were posing for wedding photos along the River Bure in Norfolk when they stood in a canoe. But the newlyweds, from Horstead in Norfolk, "went down like the Titanic" after losing their balance and tumbled into the water together.

‌



Jamie and Michelle, who was wearing a £1,800 gown, said the incident was part of a string of mishaps on their big day - but said they wouldn't let it leave a damper on the event. Phlebotomist Michelle said: "I can just remember, as we were sinking, thinking I can't go in - I've got a wedding dress on, I've had my hair done. I'd only had that dress on two hours. We went down like the Titanic. We like the River Bure but I never thought I'd end up in it.

‌



View 5 Images It wasn't the only accident on the day (Wild Daisy Photography / SWNS)

"Not exactly the elegant newlywed photo we had imagined, but somehow it sums up our day perfectly - completely unexpected, slightly chaotic, soaking wet, absolutely hilarious, and filled with love."

Michelle and Jamie, a builder, first met at school in 1993 and started a relationship before splitting as they went their separate ways as adults. It was a chance meeting in a Tesco car park in 2016 when they met again and became engaged in May 2021 - on a boat.

‌



Jamie said: "I'd moved back to Norfolk and went to Tesco one day when I saw Michelle walking through the car park. I had that panic moment that comes from childhood dreams and I thought 'if I don't talk to her now, I never will again'.

"We got engaged in 2021 on a boat and we've been inseparable ever since. We've never spent more than a day apart."

View 5 Images They ended up in the water (Wild Daisy Photography / SWNS)

‌



Their journey to the altar wasn't easy as Michelle had suffered several miscarriages and an ectopic pregnancy. The couple planned to marry in 2025 but postponed following the heart breaking loss of Jamie's dad and Michelle's mum.

But despite everything the couple battled the odds to marry at Norwich Castle Museum on August 29 - with more hiccups than just the unexpected swim. Jamie said: "First, Michelle forgot her bouquet and had to turn back, passing me on the road after we'd carefully avoided seeing each other all the night before.

"Then, as I cried my way through an emotional ceremony at Norwich Castle Museum, torrential rain caused the confetti to stick to all our guests as they threw it over us. It doesn't rain for months and then the day you want to get married, the heavens open."

‌



View 5 Images The shoot ended in disaster (Wild Daisy Photography / SWNS)

Following the 50-guest wedding at Norwich Castle Museum, the couple held their reception at the Grade-II listed pub The King's Head in Coltishall, Norfolk. It was on the nearby Coltishall Common that their newlywed shoot began.

Michelle said: "All morning we thought the weather looked okay and then suddenly, rain, thunder, everything. Our photographer told us we weren't going to get our sunset picture but we [Jamie and Michelle] knew we had to get creative. I'd waited since I was 13 for this moment."

‌



It was then the couple tentatively got into the canoe - before overbalancing and spilling into the river. To make matters worse, another wedding guest had rushed to see if they were okay and slipped - breaking their leg.

View 5 Images Jamie Wade and Michelle

The pair went back to their 120-strong wedding reception to the shock of their guests. Jamie said: "We took it entirely in our stride. Michelle looked absolutely stunning before and after the dunk. She just shook out her drenched hair, straightened her dress, and gave me a big hug.

‌



"I was tipping water out of my boots all night - every time I emptied them, a little while later they were full again. To top it off, Michelle accidentally put her foot in the fireworks machine and burnt her toe. If she hadn't been wet, she would have gone up.

View 5 Images Jamie Wade and his new bride Michelle (Wild Daisy Photography / SWNS)

"We'd worked so hard to get to our wedding day and the powers that be had one last test for us."

Article continues below

The couple are due to go to Corfu on their honeymoon this month but Michelle added: "I think we should probably take a paramedic."
