Sports.title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.

Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.

“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”

Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”

The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. The Spurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.

Sports.title: High-flying Hull stay unbeaten by holding off Aston Villa in stalemate
Sports.content:
It’s never dull in Hull, as the saying goes in these parts, and after just three games the Premier League is proving to be quite some ride for Hull City supporters.

Having embarrassed Manchester United here on the opening day and won at Coventry last weekend, this deserved point and third successive clean sheet merely reinforced Sergej Jakirovic’s belief that his men can beat the drop.

You have to go back to Bolton’s excellent start in 2001-02 to find a promoted side who began the season with three straight victories. The Tigers failed to emulate Sam Allardyce’s team, but they came closest to a winner as the Algeria winger Mohamed Belloumi hit the crossbar with a stunning second-half shot before the substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho and Oli McBurnie threatened late on.

“We could have won, but they also had a few chances in the second half,” said Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday. “We won’t be ungrateful for seven points after three games and another clean sheet. It’s a great result for us and we showed we can compete at this level.”

For Aston Villa, it was another largely impotent display which saw them fail to score for the third match running as the captain, John McGinn, and Emiliano Buendía spurned decent second-half opportunities.

Villa failed to manage a shot on target when being hammered 4-0 at Brighton and losing 1-0 at home to Arsenal; here they managed just one, a tame shot by George Hemmings early on.

Unai Emery chose to take the positives from Villa’s display as he patiently rebuilds the club after a summer of major upheaval which saw a number of key players leave and 10 new faces arrive.

View image in fullscreen George Hemmings had Aston Villa’s first shot on target of the Premier League season, 13 minutes into their third game. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

“The result is not enough, but I think we deserved more,” he said. “We weren’t clinical but of course to win matches, you need goals. We created chances today to score and we must improve but we are rebuilding.”

Ambition pulsed loudly at a sold-out MKM Stadium before kick-off as a huge amber banner inscribed with the words “One family, one dream” was paraded on the pitch. It said much for the togetherness that Jakirovic has fashioned within his squad and the connection with the club’s supporters during a remarkable few months in the Tigers’ history.

Desire was visible and audible in the stands and on the pitch, but Villa almost led inside the second minute when Nicolas Jackson headed Ian Maatsen’s teasing left-wing cross wastefully wide.

Hull were unfazed and Belloumi beat Ross Barkley twice, including with a delightful nutmeg, before breaking clear down the right flank. His low cross was cleared, but it hinted at the possibilities on offer for the hosts.

In the 13th minute, Villa finally fashioned their only effort on target this season as Hemmings’s low shot was comfortably saved by Konstantinos Tzolakis.

If Villa could not see off a promoted side widely tipped for an immediate relegation this season, could they really consider themselves ready to start climbing the table? A neat passing sequence should have brought a Villa goal in the 50th minute but McGinn could only lift the ball harmlessly over Tzolakis’s crossbar from less than 12 yards out.

Three minutes later, Villa went even closer as Hemmings outstripped the Hull captain, Lewie Coyle, down the left flank and showed intelligence to pick out Buendía with a neat cut-back. Buendía should have buried the chance but he blazed wildly over, much to his disgust.

In the 65th minute, Hull went agonisingly close to scoring when Belloumi collected possession from a short corner and curled a stunning left-foot shot against the bar. There was a resilience to the hosts, and the collective desire that carried them to promotion last season will be needed over the next 35 games if they are to defy the odds and beat the drop.

It was evident again late on when the Hull substitute Lucas Herrington – on his 19th birthday – produced a vital block to repel Tyrone Mings’s shot. Cho’s close-range effort was then repelled by Zion Suzuki before McBurnie failed to properly connect with Giles’s cross as Hull looked likeliest to nick a late winner.

Sports.title: Haaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debut
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernández started for Manchester City after Nico O’Reilly’s back injury during the warm-up and sparkled, showing why the club paid a British-record-equalling £125m for the midfielder. The winner came courtesy of Erling Haaland’s 300th goal in club football and Fernández had a key part, feeding Antoine Semenyo, whose cross from the right was crashed home.

In the second half Coventry hammered away, but their wait for a first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji’s second in a 3-2 defeat at Aston Villa on 5 May 2001 goes on. The visitors did not like losing, but were heartened by holding the star-studded hosts to a slender win, though the bottom line is all three of their Premier League outings on their return have been defeats.

Frank Lampard said: “I don’t think we deserved to lose. I’m disappointed we didn’t get what we deserved – which was a point. We can walk out of here with our heads held extremely high.”

Enzo Maresca’s men have a maximum nine points so can be supremely satisfied. “Today was not a nice win, a bit ugly,” he said. “In the first half we deserved more goals – we scored one but could have scored one or two more.”

The manager said of Fernández: “The reason Enzo was on the bench [initially] was because he arrived only a few days ago. I know how frustrating it was for him in the last weeks but in the end he played some minutes and was quite good. Nico felt something in his back – not serious.”

Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought for £85m, was on the bench for the hosts, as Fernández lined up alongside Rayan Cherki in a 4-1-2–2-1 that had Semenyo and Iliman Ndiaye, another new home signing, stationed behind Haaland.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández shoots on his Manchester City debut. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Coventry, with Ethan Pinnock and Frank Onyeka replacing Caleb Yirenkyi and Loum Tchaouna from the XI that lost at home to Hull, could have taken the lead when Abdukodir Khusanov played the ball back to Gianluigi Donnarumma and it slipped under the goalkeeper’s boot, but the Italian scrambled it clear. The visitors should then have bridged the 25 years to Hadji when a Semenyo pass meant for Rúben Dias was intercepted by Taiwo Awoniyi. But when the striker ran in his radar failed, and the shot was pulled wide.

The longer Coventry stayed level the better their prospects. Cherki fed a galloping Haaland and he twisted and let fly, but Carl Rushworth’s save was equal to the shot. Then, dazzling Cherki footwork – after a pass from Fernández – was followed by an effort that struck a post.

The frame of the goal and Rushworth could do nothing to stop Haaland’s opener. This time Fernández curved a pass in behind for Semenyo, the right-winger spun the ball over, and Haaland did the rest.

This was 26 minutes in and Coventry were under siege. Fernández collected the ball along the right, looked up and aimed a cross for Haaland but it failed to beat the first man. Then Cherki, again in Fred Astaire mode, made space and saw an effort blocked.

Maresca wants his wingers to be more direct – utilising the pace of Ndiaye and Semenyo – and the tactic spun Coventry. So, too, did an impish Cherki flick which put Haaland in again: he rode a challenge when going down might have brought a penalty, before shooting. Rushworth once more thwarted the Norwegian.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard and the Coventry players applaud their fans but their wait for a Premier League goal goes on. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

For Coventry, Jack Rudoni did better than Awoniyi with a header at close range, but Donnarumma flew to his left to prevent an equaliser. This showed the hope Lampard’s men carried but they had to finish any chance as these were scarce.

Ndiaye was fairly quiet on debut and when Cherki’s work took the ball to him in the area he should have pulled the trigger but refused.

Maresca said of the Senegalese: “Ili just had two sessions with us – most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, he needs to learn. When Marc Guéhi has the ball [at centre-back] he was dropping a lot – we didn’t need that, we needed him in the final third, that space was for Josko [Gvardiol, the left-back].”

The manager was more enthused about Elliot Anderson. “Really impressed not just today, he was very good against Palace, and against Bournemouth,” said Maresca. “The best thing with Elliot is day by day he wants to be better.”

Bouaddi’s home debut came on 75 minutes for Fernández and the 18-year-old showed composure during Coventry’s late-game bombardment, which included Ellis Sims forcing a point-blank save from Donnarumma.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren
Sports.content:
Yang Hyun-jun scored the winner as Celtic came from behind to beat an impressive St Mirren side 2-1. St Mirren were heading for the top of the Premiership when Nikolas Agrafiotis netted from the spot midway through the first half.

Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.

The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.

O’Neill later lamented the unavailability of Yang for some crucial games – the 24-year-old will now fly to Japan for the Asian Games and miss the midweek trip to St Johnstone and two games against Rangers, plus the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros.

“We are going to miss him. He’s in really fine form at the moment,” the manager said. “But he’s signed off with a brilliant goal. He’s in great form and he’ll work for you going backwards. He doesn’t mind doing the hard graft.”

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi accepted a gift to score the only goal against Motherwell at Ibrox, but they fear their captain Lawrence Shankland faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a hamstring injury suffered early on in the game.

Naderi, who came on for Shankland in the eighth minute, dispossessed Alex Paulsen as the Motherwell goalkeeper attempted to dribble the ball past him outside his box and the German had the simple task of rolling the ball into the net to score what proved to be a 12th-minute winner.

Motherwell dominated possession and created several chances but Rangers were more effective in the final third and should have added to their lead. Kim Min-su missed a first-half penalty and the debutant striker Kevin Kelsy was among those to pass up good opportunities after he came off the bench.

View image in fullscreen Lawrence Shankland leaves the pitch unaided but his manager later revealed the club fear his hamstring injury is significant. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

Rangers ultimately saw out the game without any late scares as they recorded a third consecutive Premiership victory.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Of Shankland, the Rangers manager, Derek McInnes, said he fears the injury is similarly significant to the one that kept him out for two months early in 2026. McInnes said: “He has a similar feeling to the hamstring injury he had at Hearts last January. We don’t want to speculate too much but he says it feels similar, in the same area, so we’ll get him scanned on Monday.

“He says he felt fine going into the game and there was nothing really that he did in the game that he was aware of, he just felt it pull up. It’s a shame for the boy because he was obviously in good form, getting himself moving and enjoying some of that attacking threat we’ve had over the last few games, and we’ve waited long and hard for that.”

Michael Forbes scored an added-time equaliser for Dundee United against Falkirk, who had led at Tannadice thanks to Jacob Murrell’s fourth-minute opener, while Kilmarnock picked up their first point but are still waiting for a first Premiership win of the season after a 0-0 draw at Aberdeen. Kilmarnock’s Aaron Tshibola was sent off for a second yellow card after 83 minutes but the hosts could not find a way past the 10 men.

Sports.title: European football: Martínez seals thrilling comeback for unbeaten Inter
Sports.content:
Lautaro Martínez scored in the 91st minute as Inter rallied from two goals down ⁠to secure a stunning 3-2 home victory over Napoli, continuing their 100% start to their ⁠Serie A title defence.

Napoli looked ⁠to be ​on course for victory when Matteo Politano and Rasmus Højlund put them 2-0 up after 53 minutes, but Martínez’s ⁠first goal halved the deficit and Marcus Thuram equalised eight minutes from the end. Both sides had excellent chances to win ⁠it after that but it was Inter who took theirs when the Argentinian stabbed ​home the ball at the back ‌post from a corner.

After ‌no goals in the first half, the game burst into life on 50 ‌minutes when Politano finished from a rebound. Three minutes after that Højlund collected Giovanni di Lorenzo’s pass and scored with a shot that arrowed in from the edge of the box.

Inter hit back three minutes later though as Martínez provided a clinical finish, and Thuram’s header from Carlos Augusto’s pass ‌levelled the scores.

It was anybody’s game from there as the action went back and forth between the two boxes, but Inter ​found the momentum they needed to take the points.

Roma scored twice past the 90th minute to claim a 2-1 ​victory over Atalanta and move to the top following a dramatic clash at the Stadio Olimpico.

Éderson’s opener for Atalanta looked to be steering them to victory, but Roma equalised through Mario Hermoso’s looping header.

They were not content with the point though and continued to push forward, allowing Matías Soulé to score via a loose ball in the box in ⁠the 93rd minute to snatch all three points.

Torino claimed a first win under Ignazio Abate when they came from behind to win 2-1 at Fiorentina.

Fiorentina took the lead when Mateo Pellegrino tried a shot from range that should have been a comfortable ⁠stop for Lucas Perri, but the Torino goalkeeper allowed the ball ​to squirm beyond ​him.

Perri later made several good ​saves to keep his side in the contest, before the ​visitors turned the ‌game on its ​head. Rolando Mandragora drilled ​the ball into the Fiorentina net from outside the box to level the score at 1-1, before Ché Adams poked home from close range on 82 minutes to secure all three points for the away side.

Later on Saturday, Gian Piero Gasperini faces his former club Atalanta when they visit Roma.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane and Bayern Munich were held to a rare goalless draw in the Bundesliga at Schalke. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

In the Bundesliga, Bayern Munich were left to rue several missed chances in the second half by Harry Kane and Luiz Díaz in their stalemate at Schalke. Loris Karius made several outstanding saves as the visitors failed to score in a Bundesliga game for the first time since a draw at Bayer Leverkusen in February 2025.

Kane and Michael Olise started on the bench, Bayern dominated the ball but created few clear chances, and stubborn Schalke dug deep to pick up their first point of the season.

Jamal Musiala played his first league minutes of the season after the Bayern midfielder collapsed in two pre-season games due to a neurological issue which causes seizures.

The Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri caused a late own goal in Borussia Dortmund’s favour, as his side came from two down to win 3-2 at Hoffenheim in a topsy-turvy clash.

Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes.

Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle. Nwaneri, who became the youngest player in Premier League history in 2024, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played after an injury for Filippo Mane.

Serhou Guirassy gave the hosts hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fábio Silva five minutes later.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With just four minutes of regular time remaining, Nwaneri cut down the left and shot centrally, but his effort took a big deflection off the home defender Albian Hajdari and into the goal.

The Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg continued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win at Borussia Mönchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season.

Gladbach took the lead twice and were 3-1 up midway through the second-half, but Elversberg fought back despite losing manager Vincent Wagner to a second yellow card just before the break.

With 10 minutes left, Felix Keidel levelled the scores at 3-3 and Maurice Krattenmacher put the visitors in front in stoppage time with his second goal of the match.

Bayer Leverkusen rebounded from their loss to Elversberg last Saturday by putting sorry Union Berlin to the sword in a 4-0 home victory.

Argentina internationals Equi Fernández and Facundo Medina had Leverkusen 2-0 up at half-time. The England centre-back Jarell Quansah set up Patrik Schick for Leverkusen’s third before Ibrahim Maza added a stylish fourth late on.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to help Werder Bremen win at home 3-1 against RB Leipzig. The Germany striker scored a long-range header, with Eren Dinkci and Marco Grüll also getting on the scoresheet.

Last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg continued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win at promoted Paderborn.

View image in fullscreen Oihan Sancet roars with delight after scoring Athletic Bilbao’s third goal. Photograph: Vincent West/Reuters

In Spain, Athletic Bilbao thumped Atlético Madrid 3-0 on a miserable afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side. Nico Williams, Robert Navarro and Oihan Sancet’s goals gave the Basque hosts a resounding victory at San Mames.

Athletic secured back-to-back wins under former Borussia Dortmund coach Edin Terzic, after losing their first two matches of the campaign.

Julián Álvarez, who tried to leave Atlético to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness but the striker was ineffective in his second-half appearance.

On Sunday La Liga leaders Barcelona visit Valencia looking to move clear of Real Madrid, who lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.

In the big game in the Eredivisie, Ajax fell to a 3-1 home defeat by PSV. Ricardo Pepi had opened the scoring early on for the visitors, before Tolu Arokodare’s 23rd-minute leveller. Goals in stoppage time in either half, from Lutsharel Geertruida and Esmir Bajraktarevic respectively, then gave PSV the win.

Sports.title: Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at Fulham
Sports.content:
The managers may have changed but the result stays the same. For the fourth successive trip to this part of west London, Crystal Palace returned over the river with a win as Pierre Sage got his reign off the mark in dramatic style. Their hero was Ben Chilwell, the former England left-back who was signed on deadline day from Strasbourg – this time permanently, after a loan spell in which he helped Palace win the FA Cup – after he came off the bench to volley home the winner.

It was a bitter blow for Fulham’s new manager Álvaro Arbeloa, who had seen his side lead twice through the impressive Josh King – who showed his potential in front of the watching England manager, Thomas Tuchel – and César Palacios before being pegged back twice by Tyrick Mitchell, the second in a moment of pure slapstick. Arbeloa and his side left the pitch to boos from some supporters and remain pointless after three matches. But having won here three times in 2025 under Oliver Glasner, this has been a happy hunting ground for Palace and Chilwell could not contain his delight as he celebrated with Sage and the travelling fans at the full-time whistle.

“Today’s lesson was free because we won but we were inefficient in buildup during the first half,” said Sage, who maintained his record of never losing three games in a row as a manager. “It’s really a difficult period for me because I don’t like the mindset of the team and the club in this moment because [the transfer market] is always open. I like to know who I will work with.”

View image in fullscreen Tyrick Mitchell equalised twice for Palace. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Fulham, who had almost 65% possession and racked up 25 shots in total, had looked more likely to end their winless start until Mitchell’s second goal swung the momentum decisively in Palace’s favour. They have now conceded seven goals in their first three league matches and Arbeloa – who was managing Real Madrid a few months ago – knows they must improve before next week’s game to face Liverpool at Anfield.

“We lost a game that we didn’t deserve to lose. But in football you need to take your chances and they did that better than us,” he said. “We need to learn quickly because things can change when you concede a goal.”

It didn’t take long for Alex Iwobi – the 30-year-old who has become only the fifth player in Premier League history to play 100 or more games for three clubs – to start pulling the strings for Fulham in midfield alongside the new £30m signing from Southampton, Shea Charles. A sloppy early pass from Jaydee Canvot inside the first minute that almost handed Palacios an opportunity betrayed the nerves of a Palace defence that had the Chelsea loanee, Axel Disasi, in the centre of the back three also favoured by Sage’s predecessor.

View image in fullscreen César Palacios scored his first goal for Fulham to put them back in front before half-time. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Fulham took the lead when Adam Wharton failed to clear a cross from Oscar Bobb and it fell straight into the path of King, whose shot took a big deflection to deceive Dean Henderson. It was typical of Sage’s luck in his first month at the helm that a superb apparent Palace equaliser less than two minutes later was chalked off. Daichi Kamada had strayed millimetres offside before volleying in a brilliant cross with the outside of his boot from Yéremy Pino.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors could have found themselves 2-0 down when Henderson saved a Timothy Castagne shot from close range, but Mitchell beat Bernd Leno at his near post to equalise against the run of play after being set up by Eddie Nketiah. Palace’s joy was short-lived, however. Chris Richards – being watched by his USA manager Mauricio Pochettino – was fooled by King’s clever dummy and the England Under-21 midfielder accepted the invitation to burst into the box. His cross would have been diverted into his own net by Canvot had it not been for an excellent save from Henderson, but even that only left Palacios with the opportunity, which he accepted, to put the ball into the empty net.

Yet Palace’s fortunes suddenly changed for the better when they scored a comical second equaliser. Mitchell’s initial effort was cleared by Gonzalo García as the striker charged back into the area, but the Palace defender volleyed hopefully towards goal as he fell, and García somehow managed to miss the ball altogether as it trickled over the line.

Fulham seemed to shrink after conceding and Palace sensed an opportunity. The comeback was completed when Chilwell volleyed in after Anan Khalaili’s effort had been blocked, and Fulham were forced to accept their fate once more after their own substitute left-back, Ryan Sessegnon, found the sidenetting in injury time.

Sports.title: Best left-back in Premier League named – and Manchester United have been tipped to sign him
Sports.content:
Best left-back in Premier League named – and Manchester United have been tipped to sign him

Bournemouth star Adrien Truffert has been named the best left-back in the country, with a big move touted for his future.

The 24-year-old has picked up from where he left off last season by starring in each of the Cherries' first three games this campaign.



3 Truffert continues to garner huge praise for his performances Credit: Getty

The Frenchman proved a snip at the £14.4million package Bournemouth agreed to pay Rennes for his signature in June 2025.

Truffert instantly impressed as Milos Kerkez's replacement under Andoni Iraola, who has since followed the latter to Anfield.

The defender, who was part of the France team that won a silver medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics, was named in talkSPORT's pound-for-pound Premier League team of the season in May.



Truffert, who was the only player to make more than 50 overlapping runs in the top-flight last season, scored once and assisted five goals.

He was the only Bournemouth outfield player to start all 38 Premier League matches as they qualified for Europe for the first time ever.



The left-back earned a spot in Opta's team of the season as one of only three players to win possession in the defensive third 100+ times (105), while among full-backs, Truffert also topped the charts for both interceptions (48) and tackles (103).

Only James Garner and Elliot Anderson covered more ground than his 402.59 kilometres during the 2025/26 Premier League season.



Truffert 'the best left-back in the country'

'Have you seen Truffert? We've got the best left-back...' Bournemouth fan Laurent told talkSPORT's GameDay Phone-in while reacting to his side's 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday.

Jason Cundy responded: "You're absolutely right - what a baller he is. I think he could be the best left-back in the country right now."

3 Truffert has been one of Cherries' standout performers since his arrival Credit: Getty

Man United told to sign Truffert

Discussing his competition for that tag with Jamie O'Hara, who put forward England pair Nico O'Reilly and Lewis Hall, Cundy replied: "By the way, struggled a bit today, Lewis Hall, and I'm a big fan.



"Listen, Truffert will get a big move, and do you know who should go for him? Man United.

"I've seen him last season. This is not just me picking up for this season. He is a damn good left-back.

"I've seen enough of Truffert in the Premier League last season since Kerkez has gone to Liverpool, I promise you.

"They [Man United] are after Lewis Hall, but I mean Bournemouth will drive a hard bargain, but Man United need a left-back!"



3 United have held a long-term interest in Hall, who Newcastle are keen to hand a new deal to Credit: Getty

Manchester United left-back options

The Red Devils have been long-term admirers of Hall, who still has three years remaining on his contract at St James' Park.

talkSPORT previously reported that Alejandro Balde and David Raum were left-back alternatives to Newcastle's Hall for the club.

Fulham defender Antonee Robinson was listed as another player United could turn to if they fail to sign their top target, Hall.



Matthias Jaissle shut down the prospect of Michael Carrick's men poaching his left-back after his team's 2-2 draw with Liverpool.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal player set to face FA probe after appearing to throttle fan in EFL chaos
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal player set to face FA probe after appearing to throttle fan in EFL chaos

Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik is expected to face an FA probe into an incident involving a young Portsmouth fan.

talkSPORT understands the FA are 'aware' of the altercation during Cardiff's 2-0 defeat at Fratton Park on Saturday and are awaiting the referee's report.

3 Bielik could land himself in hot water over the incident Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Bielik appears to grab the home supporter around the neck as he went to retrieve the match ball from the crowd.

Pompey boss John Mousinho apologised for the incident after Cardiff counterpart Brian Barry-Murphy claimed Bielik had been slapped in the face during the incident.

The fan involved was later ejected from the ground, much to the fury of Pompey fans on social media

The ex-Arsenal defender's shocking altercation with the supporter in the second half led to a stoppage of around three minutes.

With the Bluebirds 2-0 down and chasing a late comeback, Bielik - a summer arrival from Championship rivals West Brom - lost his cool as he went to retrieve the ball in the 70th minute.

What happened with Bielik and the Portsmouth fan?

Instead of handing it back to the 11-cap Poland international, a young-looking fan proceeded to throw it over his head.

In response, the 28-year-old appears to have grabbed the supporter around his neck.

The fan then pushed the ex-Birmingham man away while appearing to slap him in the face.

Fellow Pompey supporters jumped up in anger, in shock at what they had witnessed.

Camera footage then caught the fan in question gesturing that he had been throttled by Bielik.

A few minutes before the chaos, a separate Pompey fan could also be seen launching a ball off the back of Perry Ng's head.

The officials immediately looked to get the game under control, leading to a break of around three minutes.

Referee Ben Speedie spoke to both captains and managers before allowing the game to resume.

Bielik was already on a yellow card having been cautioned in the ninth minute.

But he faced no extra punishment, as he eventually left the pitch as a substitute in stoppage time.

3 Bielik appeared to grab a Portsmouth fan by the neck Credit: X

3 The Pompey supporter gestured that he had been throttled in the aftermath of the incident Credit: X

Now he could be set for a fine or ban once the FA launches their probe into the event.

It has also been claimed the supporter in question was ejected from the ground before the match finished.

Neither Cardiff nor Portsmouth commented on the incident on social media.

Goals from Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi either side of half-time proved to be the difference for the hosts.

The result lifts Portsmouth up to 13th spot, while Cardiff remain in the relegation zone in 22nd place, having failed to win any of their five league games.

Sports.title: Premier League manager told to immediately resign as winless streak continues
Sports.content:
Unai Emery should step down amid Aston Villa's poor start to the season.

That's the view of one furious fan after Villa were held to a 0-0 draw by Hull on Saturday, leaving them still waiting for their first Premier League win and goal of the campaign.

2 Villa have taken one point from a possible nine at the start of 2026/27 Credit: Getty

Emery 'needs to walk'

Having been thumped 4-0 by Brighton on the opening weekend in disastrous fashion then lost 1-0 to Arsenal, Villa do at least have a point on the board, but supporter Luke, speaking to talkSPORT's Max Scott, is not happy with the situation at the club.

"I'm absolutely furious," he fumed. "Unai Emery needs to leave. He needs to walk.

Asked if he wanted Emery sacked so soon, he emphasised: "No, I think he should walk.

"He's been let down, and PSR [Profit and Sustainability Rules] is to blame as well. He needs to walk because he's been let down massively. He must be sick of it.

"[Goalkeeper Zion] Suzuki, he should be in the No.10. He's the only player we've got who can play a forward ball."

Scott chipped in: "I understand your sentiment. I understand that Unai Emery deserves better. He deserves better than having to reinvent the team every single year because the financial regulations mean that Villa have to sell. I understand that.

"But that would be self-sabotage, wouldn't it, for you, a Villa fan, saying that he needs to walk? Because then you'd be in a world of bother.

"You're [at the] bottom of the table with Unai Emery. It's not going to get much better, is it?"

Villa 'infuriating' to watch

Luke responded: "It's not like we want him to walk, but for his own sanity...

"He looked furious at [Aaron] Wan-Bissaka earlier because he wasn't ready to come on. He must be so peed off about all of it.

2 Emery cut a frustrated figure throughout Villa's draw at Hull Credit: Getty

"And I would be too. Watching as a fan is infuriating. He's not even a fan of the club; he's a manager. He's got to be furious.

"And what we're watching is just abysmal. We don't look like we're going to score again."

A tumultuous summer

Emery might well be furious having seen his Europa League-winning squad ripped up this summer.

Among Villa's departures were Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne – all key figures in their recent success under Emery.

They have all ostensibly been replaced, but Villa have yet to see any major impact from their raft of new signings – while record arrival Johan Manzambi has yet to make his debut due to injury.

But in a more positive omen, this isn't the first time Villa have made such a slow start in the Emery era.

Indeed, last term, they failed to win any of their last six games in all competitions – before winning 17 of their next 20 matches up to the end of 2025.

They went on to finish fourth in the Premier League and end the club's 30-year trophy drought by winning the Europa League, clinching Champions League qualification in the process.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany explains controversial Harry Kane decision as Bayern Munich star is denied history
Sports.content:
Harry Kane was benched by Vincent Kompany for Bayern Munich's stalemate against Schalke as he is still not fully match fit.

That is despite the England skipper starting in the Bavarian outfit's 5-1 opening day victory over Stuttgart last week.



3 Kane missed out on the Bayern starting XI against Schalke Credit: Getty

The 33-year-old striker was introduced against Schalke at the start of the second half in Bayern's 0-0 Bundesliga draw on Saturday evening.

Kane, who has scored 148 goals for Bayern and is now in his fourth season at the club, is still searching for his first league goal contribution this term.

Michael Olise was another surprise inclusion on the bench, and their boss Kompany explained why he dropped the pair from his team.



Why was Harry Kane benched against Schalke?

"That was simply a rational decision," he said when speaking to the media.

"They came back very, very late from vacation. The game against Osnabruck (4-1 win in the DFB-Pokal) cost them a lot of energy.



"The priority was to have them available for that because it was a Pokal game.

"And then I had to make a decision for today.

"They're still not in the right condition to be under full workload. It was a rational decision."



What piece of Bundesliga history is Harry Kane closing in on?

Former Tottenham Hotspur star Kane has been nothing short of a sensation since signing for Bayern in 2023.

He is seventh in their all-time scoring charts, but is closing in on an impressive piece of Bundesliga history.

3 Kompany revealed why he chose not to start the striker Credit: Getty

Kane has 98 goals in 96 German top-flight appearances to date, and is set to hit a century in record time.



As it stands, Dieter Muller is the record holder, having brought up his Bundesliga century in 129 matches in 1977.

And Kane is also poised to smash Robert Lewandowski's record of being the fastest foreign player to score 100 Bundesliga goals.

The Poland international brought up his 100th strike in his 168th appearance in September 2015.

Bayern's 0-0 draw with Schalke saw them miss out on the summit of the Bundesliga.



It was also the first time since February 2025 that they failed to score in a league match, ending a run of 47 fixtures.

3 Kane drew a blank against Schalke, with the striker goalless from his opening two Bundesliga games this season Credit: Getty

And for Kane, Schalke are the first Bundesliga side he has yet to find the back of the net against, having now battled 21 different teams.

Though he will be looking to add Schalke to his long list of victims when Bayern host them later in the season.



As it stands, SC Freiburg sit top of the table after two matches, with Borussia Dortmund and newly-promoted SV Elversberg only behind on goal difference.

Fourth-placed Bayern begin their Champions League campaign on Tuesday night as they take on Bodo/Glimt.

Premier League giants Arsenal and Manchester United are among the eight opponents they have drawn in the league phase.
