Sports.title: Neco Williams takes swipe at VAR as controversial decision leads to unwanted Premier League first for Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Neco Williams takes swipe at VAR as controversial decision leads to unwanted Premier League first for Nottingham Forest

Neco Williams has disputed the VAR decision to rule out what looked like the winner for Nottingham Forest against Tottenham Hotspur.

Forest thought they went ahead against Spurs midway through the second half of their 0-0 draw via the Reds full-back.

3 Williams had his close-range goal ruled out by VAR in the second half Credit: Getty

Morgan Gibbs-White's goalbound shot looked to be heading in as Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke scrambled back to try and clear the ball.

But in crept Williams, who pipped the Spurs duo to the ball where he appeared to have bundled in a close-range header.

However, the goal was controversially ruled out for handball, with neither side able to make a breakthrough following the incident.

With the game ending goalless, Forest hit an unwanted Premier League feat as a result of their disallowed goal.

It's the first time they have not won any of their opening three matches during a Premier League season - and their first time doing so in the top-flight since the 1990/91 campaign.

And Williams, who signed a new deal until 2030 on Friday, expressed his disapproval of the decision to chalk off the goal against Spurs.

He posted a screenshot of the VAR replay on his Instagram and, in the caption, sarcastically said: "Clear and obvious they say."

Why was the Forest goal disallowed?

The Premier League explained why the goal did not stand with a post from their Match Centre on X.

"VAR checked the referee's call of goal to Nottingham Forest – and determined that Williams handled the ball immediately before scoring and recommended that the goal was disallowed."

Referee Craig Pawson also announced: "After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest no. 3 before the goal is scored.

3 Williams posted a still from VAR made a 'clear and obvious' jibe Credit: @necowilliams Instagram

"The final decision is a direct free-kick for Spurs."

Speaking after the match, Forest boss Oliver Glasner claimed that VAR Peter Bankes was 'guessing' when reviewing the goal.

"I watched five or six different angles and, to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt moves a little bit, but it's not clear is it the ball or (Sandro) Tonali on the goalline," he said.

"I think the VAR can't intervene when he is guessing. It was not clear and obvious.

"We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high, which is why this is a wrong intervention.

"If it's not 100 per cent clear, stick to the on-field decisions. This is the inconsistency today.

3 Glasner believes the VAR was guessing when making the controversial decision Credit: Getty

"I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood."

More VAR controversy with Forest

The ruled out goal against Spurs came just a week after Forest were beneficiaries of the rules.

Gibbs-White scored for them in the 2-2 draw at Liverpool with a penalty, which was awarded moments after it appeared that Liam Delap made a foul throw.

It was then revealed that VAR cannot intervene with supposed foul throws, and therefore the penalty was allowed to stand.

Forest are 16th with two draws and one defeat, whilst Spurs sit two spots below them after picking up their first point of the season.

Sports.title: Armando Broja in X-rated blast at Burnley fan as nightmare start to season continues
Sports.content:
Armando Broja in X-rated blast at Burnley fan as nightmare start to season continues

Burnley striker Armando Broja told a fan to 'shut your f****** mouth' as tempers flared after Saturday's 2-1 defeat to Bristol City.

The Clarets threw away three points in the closing stages at Turf Moor and remain winless in England's second tier since their relegation from the Premier League.

3 Broja was involved in a heated conversation with a Burnley fan Credit: Getty

Burnley led via Aaron Ramsey's 56th minute opener, but an 82nd minute equaliser through Rob Dickie and Yu Hirakawa's stoppage time winner ensured it was the Robins who walked away with the victory.

After five games, the Lancashire sit rock-bottom of the Championship on two points and miles off any sort of battle for promotion as it stands.

Broja, who was signed by Burnley in August 2025, was brought on by Nicky Hayen at the start of the second half, but was unable to make an impact for his struggling side.

And the former Chelsea man then seemed to let his frustrations get the better of him after the full-time whistle.

What happened with Armando Broja after Burnley's defeat to Bristol City?

In a video that has widely circulated on social media, Broja looked to be responding to some irritated Burnley fans in a car park amid the club's poor form.

"What have I done?" he appears to ask, as well as: "I've been rubbish for a year?"

Broja then seemingly claimed: "I haven’t played for a year!"

Then, just before he walked away, the 24-year-old says: "Shut your f****** mouth and be respectful."

It remains unclear as to what sparked the tense conversation between him and the fan.

Broja made 26 appearances in all competitions last season, though started on just eight occasions in the top-flight.

3 Bristol City inflicted a third league defeat on Burnley Credit: Getty

He joined in a reported £20million move from Chelsea, where he spent 16 years as a youth and senior player.

Broja, who has made five outings for Burnley this campaign, has also featured 37 times for Albania's national team - scoring six goals.

How have Burnley fared in the Championship this season?

Burnley were amongst the favourites for promotion heading into the new season, but a Premier League return may already be out of reach.

A 2-2 draw at home to fellow relegated side West Ham on the opening weekend was a solid result on the face of it having come from two goals down.

However, this was followed by a 3-1 loss at West Brom before Norwich City thumped then 4-1.

Burnley managed to salvage a 1-1 draw with Middlesbrough during the week, but Saturday's result has further added to their struggles.

3 Burnley are winless at the bottom of the Championship Credit: Getty

Their only victory this season has come in the Carabao Cup as they beat League One side Notts County 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

However, they were knocked out in the second round by Bradford City in a 4-2 shootout defeat.

Boss Hayen will bow be looking for an immediate response when his side travel to Wrexham on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi and Conor Gallagher speak on ‘encouraging signs’ despite unwanted 52-year Tottenham first
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi and Conor Gallagher speak on ‘encouraging signs’ despite unwanted 52-year Tottenham first

Roberto De Zerbi is not sweating over Tottenham's poor start to the season - despite Saturday's 0-0 draw away at Nottingham Forest.

Spurs may have picked up their first point of the season in their third fixture, but they delivered yet another performance void of attacking quality.

3 De Zerbi is remaining calm despite Spurs' winless run extending to three games Credit: AFP

Their afternoon could have even ended in another defeat had Forest not had a goal ruled out for handball from Neco Williams in the second half.

With three games played, Spurs have not scored a single goal in the Premier League this season.

The last time they failed to find the back of the net in their opening three league games of a campaign was the 1974/75 season.

They went on to finish 19th in the First Division and just a point above the relegation zone.

It's also the first time since November 2021 that Spurs have gone three league matches without a goal.

Spurs' draw leaves them in 17th spot in the table - the same position they have finished in each of the two last years.

What has Roberto De Zerbi said about Tottenham's draw?

Having previously lost 3-0 to Brentford and 2-0 against Newcastle United, Spurs will somewhat celebrate the fact they weren't beaten by Forest.

And when asked about the importance of looking for encouraging signs when the team isn't scoring, De Zerbi hinted that they remain a work in progress.

"I think we are working to build a different Tottenham than the last two seasons," he told talkSPORT's Geoff Peters.

"And even (though) we made a great window of the transfer market, we need time.

3 Gallagher senses things are heading in the right direction Credit: Getty

"Because the football team becomes a football team with the time, with the relationship with the players, between the players, the connection between the players to find a balance because it's not so easy to find a balance with a lot of new players.

"I'm excited to work with these players.

"And if you analyse the history of the Premier League in the last ten seasons, ten years, many big clubs, they wanted to rebuild the team.

"Sometimes they finish in a good way, sometimes not, but anyway, they spent the time to become top."

Midfielder Conor Gallagher was given a similar line of questioning and saw enough against Forest to be confident going forward.

He remarked: "We've had a difficult start. We've not played how we would have liked and how we thought we would.

3 Tottenham currently sit 17th in the Premier League table Credit: Getty

"But I'm glad it's happening now so we can sort it out and we can improve and we can work as hard as we can to get better and to get more points and win more games and do everything we need to do.

"Like I said, today was a step in the right direction with a better performance."

Spurs will be desperate to end their goal drought next Saturday when they host Everton at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Sports.title: Man City's former chairman says their £440m transfer spend makes a MOCKERY of the Premier League's regulation amid their 115 charges case - and that 'justice delayed is justice denied'
Sports.content:
Man City's former chairman says their £440m transfer spend makes a MOCKERY of the Premier League's regulation amid their 115 charges case - and that 'justice delayed is justice denied'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City's former chairman David Bernstein says his old club's transfer spending while their 115 charges case continues in silence 'makes a mockery' of the Premier League's regulation of the top division.

Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as Football Association chair 2011-13, today attacked the lack of an outcome and questioned the Premier League's handling of the case.

City, who spent £440million in the transfer window and equalled the British transfer record signing £125m Enzo Fernandez, kicked off this season still without resolution to their infamous financial charges case.

City were charged with 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in February 2023 and a 12-week hearing concluded in December 2024 - but an independent commission is still yet to publish its ruling on the 'hugely complex case'.

The club strenuously deny the allegations. The verdict could see City exonerated or facing historic penalties.

Now Bernstein, 83, has joined the growing chorus of criticism of the delays - after Premier League chief executive Richard Masters admitted a verdict 'has taken longer than expected'.

Erling Haaland celebrates taking Manchester City to the top of the Premier League again

This is the fourth season to begin under the cloud of the City 115 charges announcement.

Writing in the Sunday Times, Bernstein said: 'The fact they have done this (transfer spend) against the background of the 115 Premier League charges is extraordinary and makes a mockery of regulation in England's top division, supposedly the best-run league in the world.

'Why the league decided to prosecute all 115 alleged offences is a mystery to me. Surely common sense (often in short supply) would point to simplifying the process by taking a handful of the bigger, clearer issues and pursuing these as specimen cases.

'Justice delayed is justice denied, and the longer this process is drawn out, the more the resulting implications and challenges are compounded.'

It was a bumper summer for City after the exit of long-serving manager Pep Guardiola. They also signed Elliot Anderson (£116m), Ayyoub Bouaddi (£86m), Iliman Ndiaye (£60m), Allan and Geronimo Rulli.

Masters has claimed that City's ongoing 115 charges saga is 'not necessarily top of the list' when it comes to his conversations with clubs.

David Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as FA chair 2011-13

Four Premier League sides have reserved the right to seek compensation should City be found guilty and it would appear that much of football is desperate for an outcome.

However, Masters suggested that the noise in boardrooms up and down the country is not as loud as one might imagine.

'I obviously speak to clubs all the time,' he said last month. 'It's not necessarily a topic of conversation that is top of the list. (There are) Lots of other things to talk about and do. The Premier League moves on. It's starting (again) on Friday evening.'

Masters has previously admitted to being frustrated by the length of time the independent panel is taking to return its verdict.

'The process is the process,' he said. 'It will resolve itself. But as you know, I literally can't say a thing about it. There's only one available option, which is to allow the process to reach its natural conclusion. I can't talk about the substance of the case. I can't talk about the timing of the case. Our rules are very clear about that. I understand that people are frustrated but it will take as long as it takes.'

The Premier League's latest domestic broadcast deal has seen the amount paid per game fall by around £2.5m.

Some have wondered if that is an indicator that fans are getting fed up of various litigations, with Nottingham Forest, Everton and Leicester City docked points in recent times.

But when asked if the perceived lenient penalty, a £10m fine handed to Chelsea for repeated backhanders, suggested there was a desire to move on from docking points, Masters denied that was the case.

'I don't think litigation and broadcast deals are necessarily associated,' he said. 'I do think litigation is to be avoided.

'It should be a last resort within a league system or generally. I think that is generally the attitude that is taken by stakeholders in the game. Litigation is a last resort.'

City are top of the Premier League, having taken maximum points from their first three matches under the guidance of Enzo Maresca - including a 1-0 victory over promoted Coventry City on Saturday.

Sports.title: Katie Taylor is crowned undisputed champion for a THIRD time with unanimous decision victory over Flora Pili - as Irish boxing icon, 40, enjoys fairytale end to her career in front of 82,000 fans at sold-out Croke Park
Sports.content:
There will never be another night quite like this for Katie Taylor… or, for that matter, for boxing itself.

Under the lights at Croke Park, in front of 82,000 delirious fans, Ireland's greatest fighter walked into the ring for the final time and left it as a three-time undisputed world champion after defeating Flora Pili on points.

Taylor had dreamed of this moment for much of her life. She had spent more than a decade rewriting the history of women's boxing, collecting world titles, conquering America, avenging the only defeat of her professional career and becoming the undisputed champion not once, but twice.

But nothing could have prepared her for this.

The noise inside Croke Park was deafening as Taylor made her final walk to the ring, the 40-year-old receiving a hero's welcome before facing the undefeated Frenchwoman in the last fight of a career that has transformed boxing in Ireland and beyond.

And when the first bell rang, Taylor set about doing exactly what she had come to Croke Park to do.

Katie Taylor celebrated victory on her farewell fight to become a three-time undisputed champion

Taylor overcame the challenge of Flora Pili, who had been unbeaten in 12 fights as a professional

Taylor appeared in the ring with family and friends are wrapping up her career in style

From the opening round, she demonstrated her speed deploying a lightning-quick jab despite being 11 years older than her opponent.

It was in the second round Pili really felt Taylor's power after taking a strong right hand to the temple.

It got the fans excited but the Frenchwoman weathered the storm before receiving a slap across her face from her trainer in the corner as he urged her to 'wake up'.

Knowing she was down heavily on the scorecards Pili showed conviction in the seventh round but it was never going to be enough to topple the Irish champion.

As the tenth and final round rang in, both fighters touched gloves as a sign of respect. The crowd cheered their champion home as she drew the curtain on her career.

Taylor did everything she could to get the stoppage in the dying seconds of the fight but she had to settle for a points victory.

There was a moment after the final bell when Taylor simply stood and took it all in.

The noise, the tears, the Irish flags, the thousands of people on their feet inside Croke Park and the knowledge that this really was the end.

Taylor emerged to a stunning ovation at a sold-out Croke Park, with 82,000 in attendance

Taylor's husband Sean McCavanagh was among those watching on ringside at the venue

Westlife performed in the build-up to Taylor taking to the ring for the last time in her career

Michael Flatley was among the well-known faces in attendance on the historic night

She had wanted one final night. One final fight. One final chance to walk into the ring in front of her home crowd and remind the world exactly who she was.

She got all three.

Taylor leaves boxing as a three-time undisputed world champion, an Olympic gold medallist and one of the most important figures the sport has ever produced.

But her legacy cannot be measured in belts alone.

She changed women's boxing forever. She gave a generation of young girls a reason to believe that they belonged in a boxing gym. She carried Irish boxing on her shoulders for years and became a sporting icon far beyond the ring.

And perhaps most fittingly of all, she signed off where she had always wanted to be.

At Croke Park. In front of her people. With another world title wrapped around her waist.

The final chapter could not have been written any better.

Katie Taylor came home, became undisputed for the third time and walked away on top.

A champion to the very end.

Sports.title: Named: Arsenal's 'TWENTY-ONE summer transfer targets' on remarkable wishlist including Chelsea's Joao Pedro, two Tottenham stars and five £100m+ movers
Sports.content:
Named: Arsenal's 'TWENTY-ONE summer transfer targets' on remarkable wishlist including Chelsea's Joao Pedro, two Tottenham stars and five £100m+ movers

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A list of Arsenal's transfer targets for the summer window has been published - revealing a number of surprise failed moves, including for Chelsea striker Joao Pedro.

The Premier League champions made five major additions in the transfer window, at a cost of almost £200million, while also engaging in a well-publicised failed pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior.

The Brazilian features on a 21-man list of players Arsenal did not sign - but did target - revealed after the closing of the transfer window.

Joao Pedro is among the most eye-catching, among nine Premier League players listed, along with Tottenham centre back duo Micky van der Ven and Cristian Romero. Van der Ven stayed at struggling Spurs and signed a new contract while Romero moved to Atletico Madrid for £34m.

Arsenal have been hunting for a new superstar attacker to boost their bid to win the Champions League for the first time in their history and Julian Alvarez and Vinicius are joined on the list by Bradley Barcola, who Liverpool signed for £123m, and Real Madrid's £120m purchase Yan Diomande.

Sandro Tonali, Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, who signed for Tottenham, Manchester City and Chelsea for £100m, £116m and £117m, are also included.

Morgan Rodgers (centre) and Joao Pedro (right) were both on Arsenal's list of targets

Julian Alvarez was also wanted by Arsenal but a move from Atletico didn't materialise

Arsenal pursued Aston Villa forward Rogers for much of the early summer but were ultimately beaten to him by their London rivals.

The full list, published by the BBC, adds: Kenan Yildiz (Juventus), Nico Paz, Jacobo Ramon (both Como) Malick Fofana (Lyon), Jeremy Monga, Louis Page (both Leicester City), Ivan Fresneda (Sporting Lisbon) and Tarik Muharemovic (Sassuolo).

The remaining names from the Premier League are: Eli Junior Kroupi, Alex Scott (both Bournemouth) and Amadou Onana (Aston Villa).

The inclusion of Joao Pedro will particularly catch the eye ahead of Arsenal's game against Chelsea on Sunday. The Blues were adamant their Brazilian No 9 was not for sale this summer, and the BBC report Arsenal had 'concerns over how he would fit into Mikel Arteta's system'.

Arsenal did recruit from the Premier League, bringing in Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier from Newcastle, Villa and Leeds. Christos Tzolis joined from Club Brugge and Piero Hincapie's loan from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent.

Guimaraes signed ahead of Tonali and Scott due to factors including availability and age and the move by sporting director Andrea Berta is reported to have been 'well recieved' at the Emirates.

Bradley Barcola featured on Arsenal's list but signed for Liverpool instead

Arsenal looked at a number of Premier League names including Eli Junior Kroupi

Arsenal had made it clear from the start that they planned to substantially invest in their squad this summer, after winning the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years in May.

Back then, co-chairman Josh Kroenke said: 'Right now there are other teams that are already trying to strengthen to come at us for next season. So we need to be aware of that.

'We've already had a few conversations about different areas that we think we can improve – both on and off the pitch. We are looking forward to getting that going this summer.'

Last week Daily Mail Sport revealed assistant manager Gabriel Heinze had reached out to Inter Milan's Lautaro Martinez – a fellow Argentine – over a potential move late in the window. Inter refused to engage.

The lack of a superstar attacker has left some Arsenal fans disappointed by manager Arteta insists he is satisfied with their business and their attempts at signings.

Ahead of facing Chelsea, when asked if boxes had been ticked over recruitment, he said: 'Yeah, 100 per cent ticked.

'The outcome after can be different to what you expect, but the intention is certainly there, which is, in my opinion, what I value the most.'

Arsenal's record signing remains the £105m deal to buy Declan Rice from West Ham United in 2023.

Sports.title: US Open fans mock Naomi Osaka's latest bizarre outfit as Japanese star squeezes through in New York thriller
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka wore a different outfit to walk onto Louis Armstrong at the US Open for a third time this tournament on Saturday night, but it did not go down well with fans at home.

Osaka has become known for her bold fashion choices at grand slams in recent years and her outfits in New York this week have been no different.

She stepped out in an all-white ensemble on Thursday, including a long overshirt featuring tennis rackets stitched into the design.

The long tail flowed behind her as she walked onto the court, tripping on the fabric beneath her feet as she walked to the net for the coin toss and to shake hands with her opponent.

The white for the day-time session was a complete contrast to Monday's all-black skirt and tank top promo in the night session on Arthur Ashe.

But Saturday's outfit was completely different again as the Japanese star wore a light-gray zip-up hoodie underneath a tailored gray plaid blazer. On the bottom, Osaka wore a very wide-leg, flowing pair of gray trousers.

Naomi Osaka wore a different outfit to walk onto court at the US Open for a third time

Tthe Japanese star wore a light-gray zip-up hoodie underneath a tailored gray plaid blazer

Osaka then wore an all-black Nike outfit to play in against Elise Mertens on Louis Armstrong

The look did not impress everybody, however, and fans took to social media to give their opinions.

'Nobody cares, it's a tennis court not Paris fashion week ffs,' one commented.

Another posted: 'She's the only one that does this.'

A third responded: 'Always cringe. My favorite tennis player is whoever is playing against Naomi Osaka.

One fan declared Osaka 'looked like a clown', while another insisted they were 'so tired of this'.

The 13th-seeded Osaka progressed to the fourth round by defeating Elise Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5, in a match that lasted two hours, 38 minutes.

The two-time champion put her head on her racket after the final point, stunned at herself at the victory.

'Honestly, I can´t believe I won this match,' Osaka said. 'I´m literally shocked that I won this match.'

Osaka was down 4-2 in the third set and apologized for expressing so much frustration throughout a tough night.

'There was a certain point, I don´t know, I felt like I put my entire heart on the court and then I just kept trying every single point,' Osaka said.

'I didn´t feel like I played amazing, and it was really getting me down. I was very negative on myself.'

Join the discussion Should athletes focus on performance or is making a fashion statement just as important at big events?

The 13th-seeded Osaka progressed to the fourth round by defeating Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5

Earlier in the week, Naomi Osaka was forced to wait until the chair umpire had chided a group of spectators in one of Arthur Ashe's hospitality suites.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

Elsewhere in the stands, another spectator was heard calling out: 'The players are ready!'

When the stadium had stilled somewhat, Osaka returned to her serve but struggled with her ball toss, apologizing as she reset.

Footage captured from another spectator of the group on social media later showed them posing as a group, allegedly during a game, with a person who appeared to be a member of US Open staff holding up a portable light to help them capture the shot.

The social media clip showed another spectator on the same evening posing in front of the court with a portable light, also allegedly during live matchplay.

When contacted by Daily Mail Sport for comment on the incident, Brendan McIntyre, head of US Open communications, said: 'We want our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend the US Open, but we also need to ensure that does not interfere with the action and competition on the court.

'These instances happen infrequently, and similar to when crowd noise reaches a certain level, our chair umpires have the ability to address the crowd when they occur.'

Sports.title: US Open star ripped for 'disgusting' behavior as she's caught appearing to make unsportsmanlike gesture at rival
Sports.content:
A US Open competitor has been accused of poor sportsmanship towards her opponent after she progressed to the fourth round on Saturday.

Russian-born Anastasia Potapova stunned Flushing Meadows when she knocked out American Amanda Anisimova in straight sets.

After shaking hands at the net and celebrating her victory with the crowd, Potapova was caught on camera appearing to sarcastically wave goodbye in the direction of Anisimova.

Seconds later, Anisimova walked past Potapova and off the court and fans took to social media to call her out for her unwanted gesture.

One commented: 'Tell me that Potapova didn't just do what I think I saw her do, that would be a total lack of respect.'

Another added: 'I've rewatched it a few times and can't imagine it being anything other than Potapova rudely waving and saying 'bye bye' to Anisimova.'

Russian-born Anastasia Potapova has been accused of waving sarcastically at her beaten rival

Amanda Anisimova missed repeated chances by converting just three of 16 break-points

Meanwhile, a third added: 'Is this behavior typical of Potapova? I understand the moment getting to you but don't think there's much excuse for this.'

It came at the end of a frustrating day for Anisimova, who missed repeated chances by converting just three of 16 break-point chances before losing 6-2, 7-5.

Potapova, a 25-year-old who was born in Russia but now represents Austria, went six for eight and matched her best showing in a Grand Slam tournament by reaching the fourth round.

Anisimova made the final at both Wimbledon and the US Open in 2025, falling to Aryna Sabalenka in Flushing Meadows.

But after reaching the quarterfinals of the Australian Open, the American was eliminated in the third round of the last three majors this year.

Potapova will play No. 5 seed Mirra Andreeva, the French Open champion.

Sports.title: Chelsea were told to 'respect' the ball by Liam Rosenior and now they are winning by rejecting it - but history tells us Xabi Alonso's side cannot win the Premier League averaging 32% possession, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Chelsea were told to 'respect' the ball by Liam Rosenior and now they are winning by rejecting it - but history tells us Xabi Alonso's side cannot win the Premier League averaging 32% possession, writes KIERAN GILL

Look, it can happen. A team can win the Premier League without the ball. However, it has only happened once in this competition’s 34 seasons, and it was the most spectacular story of them all.

Claudio Ranieri’s Leicester City, the 5,000-1 winners in 2015-16 averaging 42.4 per cent possession per game. It was a time for dilly-ding, dilly-dong. A time for pizza. A time for Jamie Vardy having a party.

Better luck next year to those besotted with the ball. It was a beautiful anomaly, and still the last time a team finished inside the top five while putting up less than 50 per cent possession.

Last season, Sunderland were the highest sub-50 side in seventh. The season before, Nottingham Forest in seventh. Before that, West Ham in ninth. And so on until we find Leicester in first. Save for a footballing fairytale, those at the top get there with the ball, not without it.

We mention all this because as Chelsea travel to Arsenal today – for a showdown which has some wondering whether these two teams will be tussling at the top nearer to May – Xabi Alonso’s side are averaging a mere 32 per cent after their wins over Fulham and Brighton & Hove Albion.

That is more than 10 per cent shy of 2015-16 Leicester, and only Hull City have seen less of the ball than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea have averaged just 32 per cent possession in their first two matches of the season

Chelsea will see more of the ball in time with Xabi Alonso having made possession a focus during his time at Bayer Leverkusen

Granted, a two-game sample size is hardly the greatest, and there is some context which we will cover, but it is still a striking statistical swing for Chelsea. They have gone from ‘respect the ball’ under Liam Rosenior to reject the ball under Alonso – and are winning.

Chelsea are bound to see more of the ball in time, if not today at Arsenal, because this was not exactly expected after how Alonso won his way into the history books with Bayer Leverkusen.

There was a training exercise which Alonso liked using at Leverkusen. It did not have a jazzy name. Just ‘Possession Game’. It involved two eight-a-side teams on a narrow pitch and three neutral players among them in bibs playing for both. There were no goals. The way you scored was by keeping the ball. Ten consecutive passes equalled one point.

Alonso would intervene if he sensed the tempo was too slow, Leverkusen’s metronomic manager playing passes to show the rhythm he wanted. The overall objective was to keep possession, find space, use overloads, become comfortable with the ball and bring control to chaos.

By the end of 2023-24, Alonso’s Leverkusen were the Bundesliga champions for the first time ever, having averaged the highest possession of all the clubs in Germany’s top division at 62.1 per cent.

Which is why the start to Chelsea’s season is so intriguing now. It is something of a phenomenon, though their supporters may not mind it if Alonso persists with this style of play.

They never took to Enzo Maresca, the Pep Guardiola disciple whose methodical football resembled death by a thousand passes. That was too sideways for the liking of a fanbase which fell in love with Jose Mourinho’s pragmatic philosophy, and celebrated Premier League and Champions League triumphs via the back-three systems of Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel respectively.

Chelsea's current style of play might be welcomed by supporters, who did not take to Enzo Maresca's methodical approach

HIGHEST TEAMS WITH LESS THAN 50% POSSESSION PER SEASON 2025-26: Sunderland in 7th (44.8%) 2024-25: Nottm Forest in 7th (40.7%) 2023-24: West Ham in 9th (40.5%) 2022-23: Aston Villa in 7th (49.2%) 2021-22: West Ham in 7th (47.4%) 2020-21: West Ham in 6th (42.5%) 2019-20: Wolves in 7th (48%) 2018-19: Wolves in 7th (46.3%) 2017-18: Burnley in 7th (42.9%) 2016-17: West Brom in 10th (36.7%) **2015-16: Leicester in 1st (42.4%) ** CHELSEA POSSESSIONS THIS SEASON: vs Fulham: 38.1% vs Brighton: 25.9% ARSENAL POSSESSIONS THIS SEASON: vs Coventry: 64.1% vs Aston Villa: 60.8%

When Conte claimed their title in 2016-17, his team averaged 54.8 per cent possession, the second lowest ever put up by an English champion behind Leicester.

Alonso, arguably, is using an approach more suited to this club’s ideology, but as we mentioned, there is some context worth consideration.

Chelsea’s first two fixtures fell against sides that are prioritising possession. First, Fulham, now managed by Alvaro Arbeloa, in a game in which Chelsea led after 31 seconds and won 3-2.

Then Brighton, who crave control under Fabian Hurzeler. Per Opta, Chelsea’s 25.9 per cent possession in that 4-3 victory was their lowest on record in the Premier League.

Yet they were leading 1-0 after four minutes, and 3-0 after 32. They did not need to chase the ball as if it was the last one left on the planet in order to regain possession. They were also without Moises Caicedo, their main ball-winner who has yet to start a game this season because of injury setbacks.

Without Caicedo, Chelsea used Reece James and Romeo Lavia in midfield at Fulham, and Malo Gusto and Lavia against Brighton. Partnered by full backs, Lavia is pushing himself, hopeful of completing his first competitive full 90 for his club soon. Chelsea have shown their vulnerabilities minus Caicedo, conceding five goals in their two games.

Direct football suits Chelsea's front three and Morgan Rogers will be worth watching against Arsenal, who had thought they were poised to sign him this summer

What they have been lacking in defence, they have overcome in attack. Direct football suits Chelsea’s devastatingly talented front three, made up of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro. It is a trident which appears at its best pouncing after transitions, and Rogers will be one worth watching today.

Arsenal spent much of this summer believing Rogers was as good as theirs. Chelsea wanted him, but senior sources are willing to admit they were not overly confident because Mikel Arteta’s side were widely considered favourites. However, those inside Stamford Bridge observed their rivals’ negotiations closely and carefully, and chose their moment to swoop amid the dithering, showing a swift willingness to pay £117million to Aston Villa. Blindsided, Arsenal then claimed they were only willing to go to £80m maximum. Other sources say they were prepared to surpass £100m. Rogers, upon signing for Chelsea, said he had joined ‘the biggest club in London’.

Now he will be a fixture in the Premier League's best attack versus the best defence, seeking to show Arsenal what they missed out on – when Chelsea have the ball, that is.

Sports.title: Why Nottingham Forest are yet to hit their stride under Oliver Glasner: Morgan Gibbs-White has another gear to find - and £50m signing Liam Delap must discover his speciality
Sports.content:
Why Nottingham Forest are yet to hit their stride under Oliver Glasner: Morgan Gibbs-White has another gear to find - and £50m signing Liam Delap must discover his speciality

Without a win or even a goal at the City Ground this season, Nottingham Forest are still to splutter into life.

They look solid enough under Oliver Glasner but the Austrian’s highly-structured training regime and tactical plan is squeezing Forest’s flair players a little.

Glasner is a fine coach and will surely get it right. However, he could do with a victory, ideally at Aston Villa on Saturday.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the challenges facing Glasner after Forest’s slow start.

Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest side have yet to splutter into life this season

Forest’s Delap gamble

There is nothing about Liam Delap that screams ‘£50million centre-forward’. Indeed, the price tag is unfair on the player as it creates a level of expectation that he is unlikely to be able to fulfil.

Delap is a competent No 9. But for that fee – and please ignore the ‘market forces’ justification – a player surely needs to have at least one special quality. What is Delap’s?

He is no slouch but nor is he particularly quick. If he has been bought for his aerial ability, then his lack of impact against Jan Paul van Hecke and Micky van de Ven was worrying. Technically he is OK, nothing more. He’s strong, yes, but so are most Premier League players. His highest goal tally in a league season is 12 for Ipswich in 2024-25.

Delap is probably not as good as Igor Jesus, who cost Forest only £10m from Brazilian club Botafogo a year ago and managed 16 goals in his first campaign in England. Put Delap in Botafogo’s team and there is no guarantee he would reach that tally in his opening season.

More than most, Delap’s valuation reflects the madness of the summer market and if Delap thrives despite it, all credit to him.

Nothing about Liam Delap suggests he is a £50m forward and the price tag has set an unfair expectation on him

Gibbs-White seeking lift-off

Forest’s No 10 was desperately unlucky not to make England’s World Cup squad and the club did well to hang on to him this season. He is their best player and talisman.

Right now, Gibbs-White looks like a player who just needs a spark to bring him to life. He played well at Liverpool last weekend and scored a penalty in the 2-2 draw. He was perfectly good against Tottenham without ever reaching the heights he scaled during last season, especially under Vitor Pereira.

There was an interesting moment after full-time when Gibbs-White shared a warm greeting and a chat with Allan Dixon, the Brad Friedel lookalike who is Tottenham’s long-serving player liaison office.

Spurs came close to signing Gibbs-White last summer when they thought they had triggered a £60m release clause in his contract, only for the 26-year-old to sign a new deal with Forest instead.

Morgan Gibbs-White looks like he needs a spark to bring him to life, as he is so far yet to scale the heights of his form last season

Glasner revealed post-match that Murillo 'did not come back from Brazil in the shape he should come back'

Glasner puts Murillo on notice

One of the joys of covering Glasner’s press conferences is that he will suddenly produce a zinger from nowhere. Delivered in his calm, even tones, it catches the listener by surprise even more.

Asked why his star defender Murillo had come off late in the came, Glasner let slip that the Brazilian – who had been out injured for four months – ‘did not come back from Brazil in the shape he should come back, maybe.’

Pressed on Murillo’s fitness, Glasner understandably decided not to stick the boot in, but spoke more generally about the level of conditioning required to play in his team. But the message was clear.

Murillo has been largely undroppable since he joined Forest three years ago. With Glasner’s signing Ousmane Diomande waiting for his chance, perhaps that is no longer the case.

Sports.title: Serena and Venus Williams implode at the US Open as iconic sisters are knocked out of women's doubles in heartbreaking fashion
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams were sensationally knocked out in the first round of the women's doubles at the US Open on Friday night, blowing a 5-0 lead in the decisive 10-point tiebreaker.

The legendary sisters accepted a wildcard into the women's draw in New York at the eleventh hour after previously partnering up at the Cincinnati Open this summer on the heels of Serena's return to competition.

The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion had previously stepped back from competition four years ago, when she played for what tennis fans believed would be the last time on the US Open's Arthur Ashe show court.

Earlier in the summer, Serena accepted a singles wildcard to Wimbledon, but in a twist of fate was beaten in three competitive sets by Joint, her opponent once again in New York.

Two months later, Serena was unable to get her revenge on the Australian world No. 72, who now holds a surprising 2-0 record against the serial champion, with the American favorites falling 3-6, 7-6(6), 6-7(7).

The Williams sisters received a hero's welcome as they kicked off the night session, with the stadium fast to fill up with fans eager to see the blockbuster siblings back in action for the first time on Arthur Ashe since 2022.

Venus and Serena Williams were dumped out of the US Open women's doubles in round one

Serena and her sister were partnering at the US Open for the first time in four years on Friday

They battled well to win the second set before forcing their higher-ranked opponents to a third

But they could not get the better of Australia's Maya Joint (left) and Taiwan's Chan Hao-ching

While both sisters were laser-focused on their evening's work ahead, Serena let her fashion do the talking, sporting a bomber jacket to walk onto court which listed the years she won singles and doubles titles at the US Open.

And after complaints had been made all week about the noise during play on the over 23,000-capacity stadium, you might have been able to hear a proverbial pin drop as Joint prepared her first serve to kick-off the match.

The Australian must have learned a lot from her match-up this year against Serena, after admitting that she had been 'intimidated' by the 44-year-old due to the iconic position she occupies within the sport. Joint was composed as she held serve, with both the 20-year-old and her partner Chan admirably calm under the lights of Arthur Ashe.

The two pairs passed the opening games between one another, with the occasion perhaps top of mind for all four women on court.

But Serena and Venus had an explosive crowd on their side, who provided an enormous roar at the sight of the first real moment of Serena brilliance - a thunderous backhand which could only force an error.

The Williams sisters indisputably have history, but Chan and Joint are a tested recent pair, in July reaching a final together in Memphis. Their partnership felt sharp and familiar, and it was no surprised when they pinched the early break.

Under the gaze of New York Knicks hero Karl-Anthony Towns and his new wife Jordyn Woods, Williams Squared were full of fight, and strong net play.

A bullish break-back for 2-3 ensued, with the crowd firmly onside. They continued to fend off break points too as Chan and Joint grew into the game - but eventually succumbed at 5-3, with their opponents navigating a tricky service game to pull off the opening set.

They would find the second set far thornier to deal with. Although their games on serve stretched, Venus and Serena were able to knuckle down and hold serve, keeping pace with Chan and Joint all the way to a 4-3 lead.

The sisters blew a 5-0 lead in the 10-point tiebreaker before eventually losing 6-3, 6-7, 7-6

Venus looked a far cry from the singles player who lost her 15th match in a row this week

The thousands of fans on Arthur Ashe were raucous in their support of the sisters

Among the stars in attendance were newly married Jordyn Woods and Karl-Anthony Towns

Their run continued. 5-4 up, Serena's excellent backhand down-the-line won the sisters the opening point. Joint's serving, which was capable of causing a lot of problems for Serena and Williams, had to be pinpoint-accurate.

But Joint and Chan tightened up, a fine return from Serena brought up deuce, and advantage - it was set point Williams. They had two, and were even assisted by a rare Joint double fault, but they could not convert, and somehow, their opponents clung on.

A strong serving game from Serena, as expected, steadied the ship for 6-5, and after Joint and Chan did the same for a tiebreak. As the stakes rose, so did the Williamses levels, and it was the sibling duo who had the lead, handing Serena the opportunity to serve out the set. She double-faulted the first time, but as Joint hit wildly out into the stands, Serena and Venus took it to the decider.

This was the last time that Serena and Venus would lead. A particularly strong bit of net play from Chan in the third game helped hand their opponents the early break. But the Williams sisters broke back to make it 4-3 in the third and confirmed it with a confident hold that had Chan flinging her racquet on the court in frustration.

In a third set filled with vintage shot making, Venus and Serena wrenched momentum from their rivals with the older Williams sister in particular looking a far cry from the singles player who lost her 15th match in a row at the beginning of this tournament.

Another tiebreak beckoned. The result, however, looked a little different, with the sisters building a strong early lead, only for Joint and Chan to pull off an almighty comeback.

All in, the match lasted just over three hours. Venus and Serena more than proved that they can be competitive against doubles players on the tour in 2026. But their wait for a win this year goes on.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
