World.title: Mnangagwa pays tribute to Zim founding father Robert Mugabe
World.content:
The late former Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe with President Emmerson Mnangagwa. Images via X@matinyarare

President Emmerson Mnangagwa has paid tribute to Zimbabwe’s founding leader, the late Robert Mugabe, describing him as a revolutionary whose contribution to the liberation and development of the country continues to shape Zimbabwe’s future.

Mnangagwa made the remarks in a commemorative statement on Sunday, 6 September 2026, marking the seventh anniversary of Mugabe’s death.

“Today, 6th September 2026, our nation joins the Mugabe family in commemorating the passing on of Cde Robert Gabriel Mugabe, the founding leader of the Republic of Zimbabwe,” Mnangagwa said.



Mnangagwa hails Mugabe’s liberation struggle

The President described Mugabe as a revolutionary who led Zimbabwe through the armed struggle against colonial rule, culminating in independence on 18 April 1980.

He said Mugabe’s political journey reflected sacrifice, resilience and an unwavering commitment to the liberation of Zimbabwe and the wider African continent.

Mugabe spent 11 years in prison under the colonial government before his release in 1974. He later crossed into Mozambique in 1975, where he played a leading role in the final phase of the armed liberation struggle.

That struggle eventually led to the Lancaster House Conference in 1979 and Zimbabwe’s independence the following year.

Mugabe’s Pan-African legacy

Mnangagwa also highlighted Mugabe’s wider Pan-African outlook, saying the former leader worked alongside other African liberation leaders to end colonialism and apartheid across the continent.

Among those leaders were former Tanzanian President Julius Nyerere, Zambia’s Kenneth Kaunda, Angola’s Agostinho Neto, Mozambique’s Samora Machel and Botswana’s Seretse Khama.



Mnangagwa said Mugabe remained committed to the liberation of the African continent even after Zimbabwe gained independence.

Mnangagwa highlights Mugabe’s land reform legacy

However, Mnangagwa said Mugabe’s contribution went beyond political independence.

He singled out the Land Reform Programme, which Mugabe’s government launched at the turn of the millennium, as one of the former leader’s most significant legacies.

“Never to be satisfied with titular political independence, the founding father of our nation led the Third Chimurenga for the recovery of our birthright, land, through the Land Reform Programme,” Mnangagwa said.

The President described the programme as an “epochal transformation of property relations” that placed Zimbabwe at the forefront of post-colonial Africa’s efforts to address land ownership.

He said the programme, together with investments in education and skills development, created a foundation for economic empowerment and contributed to Zimbabwe’s long-term development ambitions under Vision 2030.

Zimbabwe remembers its founding leader

Mnangagwa said Zimbabweans would continue to honour Mugabe’s contribution and preserve the values associated with the liberation struggle.

“As a people and a nation, we continue to pay tribute to him, and to cherish the rich and priceless legacy he bequeathed to our nation, and which is sure to inspire generations to come,” he said.

He also reaffirmed Zimbabwe’s commitment to independence, unity, peace and freedom, ideals that Mugabe and other liberation leaders championed during the struggle against colonial rule.

World.title: Emirates is trending in SA: What travellers need to know
World.content:
Emirates has been all over South African headlines lately, and it’s not hard to see why. Between an expanded local partnership, a beefed-up insurance offering, and a steady stream of new aircraft touching down, the Dubai-based carrier has been quietly reshaping what flying out of South Africa looks like.

A BIGGER PARTNERSHIP WITH SAA

At the centre of the latest buzz is an expanded codeshare partnership between Emirates and South African Airways (SAA), which now covers nine additional cities. The deal includes three domestic South African routes, connecting Johannesburg with Cape Town, Durban and Port Elizabeth, along with six regional routes linking Johannesburg to Kinshasa, Gaborone, Windhoek, Lusaka, Harare and Victoria Falls.

For travellers, that means easier one-ticket bookings and smoother connections across southern and central Africa, whether you’re departing from a smaller domestic hub or connecting onward through Dubai. The two airlines have partnered for close to three decades, and this expansion marks the start of what’s now a fully reciprocal codeshare agreement.



MORE SEATS, NEWER PLANES

South Africa has also been getting a noticeable capacity boost this year. In July, Emirates introduced its next-generation Airbus A350 on a new third daily Dubai–Cape Town service, marking the aircraft’s first-ever deployment anywhere in Southern Africa. The new route also brought Premium Economy seating to the Cape Town corridor for the first time.

Johannesburg hasn’t been left out either. Emirates restored a fourth daily service to OR Tambo International around the same time, lifting the airline’s total weekly capacity to and from South Africa’s three gateways to 56 flights.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR YOUR WALLET AND YOUR TRIP

More capacity generally works in travellers’ favour. Additional daily flights and a wider codeshare network typically mean more schedule flexibility, better connection options, and increased competition on pricing, particularly on the Johannesburg and Cape Town routes to Dubai and beyond.



If you’re booking Premium Economy, the new A350s flying into Cape Town are worth looking out for specifically, since not every Emirates aircraft on the route offers that cabin yet.

Emirates has also rolled out an enhanced travel insurance offering for customers, which the airline says makes it the first in the world to provide this level of built-in cover. It includes conflict-related medical expense protection, a complimentary 30-day trip extension, airline-managed hotel stays during disruptions, and complimentary rebooking on other airlines if a conflict-related cancellation affects your journey.

For South African travellers heading to destinations where situations can shift quickly, that additional layer of protection, bundled in rather than bought separately, is a meaningful shift in what “standard” airline cover looks like.



Whether you’re booking a quick domestic hop, a regional trip into Southern Africa, or a long-haul journey via Dubai, Emirates’ recent moves add up to more choice and more flexibility for South African travellers. If you’ve got a trip on the horizon, it’s worth checking whether the new codeshare routes, aircraft types, or insurance benefits could work in your favour before you book.

World.title: What you need to earn to live in Cape Town’s most expensive suburb
World.content:
You see them driving supercars, wearing designer brands, and casually soaking up the sun during working hours.

You may be curious: how much do Cape Town’s wealthiest residents earn?

Well, if they live in the city’s most expensive suburb (Clifton), now you’ll know.



To become one of them, this is what you’ll need to earn, win, or inherit.

Cape Town’s Most Expensive Suburb

On the Atlantic Seaboard, Clifton is home to multimillionaires and a handful of billionaires.

Christo Weise, the founder of what we know today as Shoprite, has mentioned owning a home there.

The average sale price in the area is R33 million as of September 2026.

But you can find a more reasonably priced flat for R9.5 million.

If you’re looking for a hillside house, you can buy a four-bedroom property overlooking Clifton 4th for just under R50 million.



To buy the cheapest home on Clifton’s limited property market, you’ll need to earn R316 000 a month.

To purchase the average home, you’ll need a minimum monthly gross of R1.1 million.

That’s without a deposit.

If you have a R3.3 million deposit, you’ll only need a gross income of R989 000 a month.

Property Type Average Asking Price Minimum Gross Income (Monthly) 1 Bedroom R9.5 million R284 538 2 Bedroom R15.5 million R464 246 3 Bedroom R44.5 million R1.32 million 4 Bedroom R59.2 million R1.77 million

Renting in Clifton

But you don’t have to buy to become one of Clifton’s 507 residents.

You can rent.

To rent in Clifton, agents and landlords require you to earn at least 3 times the rent.

On the rental market, there’s a furnished studio flat for R22 000 a month.

You’ll need to earn at least R66 000 a month. But if you’re renting with a partner, that’s only R33 000 each.

Your other choices are a furnished 1-bedroom for R35 000 or a 2-bedroom for R95 000.

You could get an unfurnished 3-bedroom flat for R100 000 a month.

But unlike most rentals, this 3-bedroom has a 24-month lease period.

If you don’t mind a very brief experience of how the wealthy live, you can pay R5 000 a night to rent a 3-bedroom beachfront bungalow.

Daily rentals like this typically don’t require a payslip or bank statements.

A furnished four-bedroom bungalow is available for R185 000 a month.

On a single salary, you’d need to earn R555 000 a month.

But if you attempt to split it with seven other people (two bodies to a room), you’d only need to contribute R23 125 a month.

Property Type Average Rental Minimum Gross Income Studio R29 500 R88 500 1 Bedroom R35 000 R105 000 2 Bedroom R95 000 R285 000 3 Bedroom R130 500 R391 500 4 Bedroom R138 750 R416 250

Clifton’s Residents

According to census data from 2011, the last census in which data was reported on a suburb-by-suburb basis, most Clifton residents earned over R51 280 a month.

If these salaries kept up with inflation, that starting salary would be R106 209 today.

At the time, most residents either owned and had fully paid off their home (33.3%) or were renting (32.6%).

A handful (7.6%) owned but hadn’t paid off their bond.

Some (21%) adults even resided in these sought-after homes rent-free.

World.title: Popcru wants cop killers charged with treason
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Twelve SAPS members were killed in the line of duty between April 2025 and March 2026.

Those fallen heroes were remembered in Pretoria on Sunday.

Popcru’s Mosadiwamaje Mokokong said an attack on a police officer is an attack on the state.

“This is a crisis. Hence, as a union coming from our recent Central Executive Committee, we again reaffirmed our long-standing resolution that says the government must declare a deliberate killing of a police officer as treason.

“We cannot afford to have the criminals that goes out and kill law enforcement officers because in our view, when you attack and kill a police officer you are not just killing an individual employee, but this according to us, is an attack on the authority and the capacity of a democratic state so hence we have made that call to say can we declare this is a treason those that are killing the police officers.”

World.title: 20 cop killers arrested in past year – Dimpane
World.content:
PRETORIA - Twelve South African Police Service members lost their lives in the line of duty between April 2025 and March 2026.

Their sacrifice was remembered as President Cyril Ramaphosa joined the families, friends and colleagues at a memorial service in Pretoria.

The ceremony took place at the SAPS Memorial Site at the Union Buildings.

Acting Police Commissioner, Puleng Dimpane, said 11 of them have already been convicted.

"This is a priority crime for us. It is investigated by the DPCI over the past 12 months. Over 20 suspects were arrested and over 11 actually were convicted. So indeed, and they do get a harsher sentence. And we pray that as and when we convict them, they get the harshest punishment in this regard because it is unacceptable that our police are being murdered while they protect the society.

“We have four provinces that are actually very problematic when it comes to highest levels of crimes tells us that there is so much criminality in Gauteng. It tells us that we need to revisit our plans, our strategies when it comes to Gauteng, but not only in Gauteng.

“So it tells us that we have problems and it tells us that our members in Gauteng must be vigilant, but not only in Gauteng but across the country, they must look after each other and ensure that they are vigilant at all times."
