World.title: ‘We’re praying for a miracle’ - KZN mother searching for missing daughter in Nepal
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A Durban family is racing against time to find their daughter in Nepal.

Terricia Govender, 33, is among 5,000 missing after devastating flash floods almost two weeks ago.

She was part of a pilgrimage group.

Her mother, Linda and friend Sashin are on the ground searching.

“We have not heard any information from anyone. All families are in the same boat as we are. We are also not getting assistance from the foundation she traveled with."

Linda said she is willing to physically search for her daughter in the debris.

“We cannot sit back and wait. We are praying for a miracle,” she said.

World.title: Nepali rescuers buoyed by miracle finds but tough conditions persist
World.content:
NEPAL - Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations after catastrophic floods entered a 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescues of four survivors.

The glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,384 people and left more than 5,500 missing across the two countries.

Rescuers found two more people alive on Saturday, joining two saved the day before in what have been described as miraculous tales of survival.

Three of those have been found in hydropower tunnels where the government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive.

"Search and rescue is going on at the tunnels despite geography, adverse weather and lack of connectivity," Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha told AFP.

Rescue workers were experiencing "multiple challenges", he said.

The wall of icy water and debris tore through mountain districts on August 26, destroying roads, bridges and other infrastructure.

On Saturday, rescuers pulled a Chinese man alive from deep inside a hydropower tunnel, and a 64-year-old Nepali woman, Chandrika Shrestha, from her mud-covered home.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the latter rescue had "given hope to the entire nation".

A day earlier, two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continue alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects affected.

Other examples of remarkable fortitude have emerged from Nepal, including Rajendra Dawadi, a school principal who quickly ordered an evacuation as the torrent approached, saving hundreds of students' lives.

"If the information was wrong, we would lose a day of schooling," he told AFP.

"But if it was true, we were going to lose our lives."

- Tolls rise in China -

Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said work was continuing to restore electricity in several areas.

World.title: Indonesia's main airport suspends operations after volcanic eruption
World.content:
JAKARTA - Indonesia halted operations at its main international airport outside Jakarta on Sunday after ash spewed from the Anak Krakatoa volcano more than 150 kilometres away, impacting thousands of passengers.

Mount Anak Krakatoa erupted on Saturday, producing a fountain of lava and booming sounds that could be heard up to a few hundred kilometres away, the geology agency said in a statement.

Two new eruptions were recorded on Sunday, the volcanology agency warned.

Ash from the volcano was detected in the airspace surrounding Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, prompting authorities to initially suspend operations from 1:30 am Sunday (Saturday 1830 GMT) to 5:30 am.

The suspension was extended three times, with the latest ending at 5:30 pm Sunday "due to increased eruptive activity," the airport said in a social media post.

Operations have been suspended at six airports including the Hussein Sastranegara airport in Bandung and Radin Inten II airport near Bandar Lampung on Sumatra, the country's Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.

Several airports in cities, including Semarang and Surabaya, have been prepared as "alternatives for landing" Dudy added.

- Passengers scrambling -

The disruption left some passengers scrambling to find alternative flights.

Henny Yensan, 44, who had hoped to go back to her hometown with her mother, said "everybody was disappointed".

World.title: IEC officials have nothing to worry about – elections analyst
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Elections analyst Terry Tselane is confident that the IEC has nothing to worry about with a pending legal challenge.

The ANC is considering approaching the Electoral Court, over missing Friday’s deadline to nominate some candidates.

The party cited technical glitches on the electoral commission's website.

“I think it's going to be extremely difficult for any of the political parties that feels that the so-called glitches that may have happened would actually act in their favor.

“Absolutely nothing that would allow the Commission to do so. And I think the Commission is actually protected by those two judgments, the Electoral Court judgment as well as the Constitutional Court.

“I think it's officials really can sleep at night knowing that whatever decision that they're taking is consistent with the decisions that have already been made by both the Electoral Court and the Constitutional Court.

“And besides, they are protected also by the legislation. So they should not actually be having sleepless nights on this issue because as I've indicated, they're protected by the legislation as well as the judgments of the Electoral Court as well as the Constitutional Court.”

World.title: 'The flood is coming': How a Nepal principal saved 900 students
World.content:
NEPAL - Rajendra Dawadi was inside his school near Nepal's Trishuli River with around 900 students last week when a colleague delivered an urgent warning.

"My accountant came to the school and said, 'The flood is coming, the flood is coming'," the school principal told AFP in a recent interview.

Dawadi quickly ordered an evacuation, and teachers hurried hundreds of students from classrooms to higher ground.

Minutes later, the 47-year-old watched the Trishuli Bazaar Secondary School he had run for years collapse into a raging torrent.

World.title: How Ndindi Nyoro's rise could unsettle Gachagua's Mt Kenya grip
World.content:
Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro. [Edward Kiplimo, Standard]

The political landscape of Mount Kenya is entering an intriguing phase, with Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro increasingly emerging as a figure capable of disrupting established political calculations in the region.

For months, Nyoro has been dismissed by some political actors as a “mole” serving interests beyond his own political project, while his People's Party of Kenya has been portrayed by critics as a small political vehicle with limited influence.

World.title: Sifuna condemns abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Busia County Senator Okiya Omtata, Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Bumula MP Jack Wamboka during the burial service of Mary Gorreti Okiya at Kabula, in Bumula on September 5,2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has declared that the fight to restore democracy, media freedom and the rule of law following the abduction of Standard Group Senior Editor will form the centrepiece of the Linda Mwananchi government vowing to defeat President William Ruto in the 2027 General Election.

Sifuna accused President Ruto’s administration of undermining constitutional freedoms and creating an atmosphere of fear, saying the country must be returned to what he described as “the rail of the six important values” enshrined in the Constitution.

Speaking in Bumula Constituency, Kakamega County during the burial of Mary Goreti, the sister of Busia Senator Okiya Omtatah, Sifuna strongly condemned the abduction and arrest of a Standard Group Associate Editor, Alex Kiprotich, arguing that journalists must be protected if Kenya is to remain a democratic country.

“It is impossible that you are driving on the road and you are taken away the way the way the Standard Group Journaliat and Editor Alex Kiprotich was taken. Kenyans want to live in a free country. We do not want to live in fear,” said Sifuna.

He questioned the circumstances surrounding the incident and accused the Government of failing to protect media freedom, adding that the Linda Mwananchi movement would seek to restore institutions and constitutional safeguards if elected to power, arguing that democracy could not survive where citizens, journalists and political opponents lived in fear.

"You cannot just arrest a senior journalist in the middle of the road with police carrying firearms, then you dump him some 500kilometres near the dam, a country cannot have democracy if media is not being respected and allowed to do it's work as per the constitution," said Sifuna.

He said the movement’s agenda was not merely about removing the current administration from power but it's main plan is rebuilding systems of governance around constitutionalism, democracy, individual freedoms and the rule of law.

“With less than 11 months remaining, we want to tell Kenyans that our entire plan is to return this country to the rails of the six important values contained in our Constitution, including democracy, freedom of citizens and the rule of law,” said Sifuna.

Sifuna also accused the Government of using threats against political opponents, saying leaders should not threaten citizens with arrest, expulsion or other forms of intimidation.

He challenged religious leaders to remind politicians that the power to determine the length of a person's life belongs to God.

Sifuna further linked the rule of law to economic growth, warning that investors would be reluctant to establish businesses in Kenya if government could arbitrarily order them to leave.

He said Kenya could not rely on government alone to create employment for millions of young people, arguing that the country needed both local and foreign investors.

“No investor can bring his project to a country where he can wake up one day and the President tells him, ‘Pack and go.’ It is impossible,” Sifuna said.

He argued that investor confidence was also affected by the possibility of commercial disputes being referred to foreign jurisdictions because investors lacked confidence in Kenya’s legal system.

Sifuna also criticised the government over the ongoing nurses and midwives strike, saying the rule of law required the State to honour agreements signed with workers.

World.title: Murkomen reaffirms IG Kanja's command of National Police Service
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has reaffirmed that the Inspector General of Police retains constitutional command of the National Police Service, saying the government will continue to respect the independence of the office.

Speaking during the passing-out parade of new Administration Police recruits in Nairobi, Murkomen said the Inspector General has authority over key operational matters within the service, including investigations, promotions and deployment of officers.

“Your Excellency, the Inspector General of Police retains the command of the National Police Service, especially on matters of investigation, promotion and deployment of officers without interference from anyone, including the Cabinet Secretary. We will continue respecting Article 245 of the Constitution,” Murkomen said.

His remarks come amid public debate over the relationship between the Interior Ministry and the National Police Service, particularly allegations that political leaders sometimes issue direct instructions to police officers.

Murkomen dismissed criticism directed at the office of the Inspector General, describing some of its proponents as tribalists and propagandists. He maintained that the Inspector General is carrying out his responsibilities and said he had confidence in the leadership of the police service.

“I have full faith in the IG and believe that every act that is done by the National Police Service is guided by the Constitution,” he said.

The Cabinet Secretary also addressed concerns over his role in directing the police, saying that his responsibility is primarily to provide policy direction rather than interfere with the operational command of the service.

“When required to give policy direction, I always give it in writing and we will continue to support the independence of the National Police Service from external interference,” Murkomen said.

During the ceremony, Murkomen also cautioned the newly graduated officers against corruption, excessive alcohol consumption and conduct that could undermine the reputation of the police service.

He urged the recruits to uphold discipline and protect the dignity of the police uniform, noting that the respect they receive from members of the public would depend largely on their conduct.

The Cabinet Secretary encouraged the officers to understand the responsibility that comes with joining the National Police Service and to discharge their duties within the confines of the Constitution and the law.

The passing-out ceremony marked the entry of the new recruits into the police service that made the CS use the occasion to emphasize professional conduct and respect for the constitutional framework governing policing in Kenya.

World.title: Ruto assures Kajiado residents of full control of Amboseli National Park
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto inspects the Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project in Kajiado County on September 3, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

President William Ruto has assured Kajiado residents that they will soon have full control of the management of Amboseli National Park, following his decision to return the park to the county in November 2025.

However, he said the transfer has been temporarily halted by the court.

The President hit out at those he accused of frustrating the move, saying they will be in for a rude shock.

“They took us to court over the Social Health Authority and the Affordable Housing Programme, but these programmes are progressing well. Similarly, I want to assure the people of Kajiado that, before the end of this year, Amboseli will be fully in the hands of Kajiado County,” he said.

Speaking in Kajiado County on Thursday during his development tour, President Ruto reiterated that he will not relent in his pursuit of equity and inclusive development across Kenya, saying that longstanding inequalities have unduly benefited certain regions at the expense of others.

He revealed that the securitisation of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund and the Sports Fund has enabled the Government to clear pending bills in the roads sector and construct 6,000km of new roads, and accelerate the construction of 32 new stadia across the country.

"The Road Maintenance Levy Fund was misused to only build roads in some parts of the country. Those opposing securitisation are unhappy that we are advancing equity," he said.

The President began his tour at Oloirien in Kajiado South Constituency by inspecting progress of the 67km Illasit-Rombo-Chala-Njukini-Taveta road, which is 48 per cent completed.

The Sh9.4 billion project will cut travel time between Kajiado and Taita-Taveta counties from two hours to just 40 minutes, thus easing the movement of goods and people.

The Head of State announced that eight new roads of 220km are being built across Kajiado County at a cost of Sh13 billion to open up the region and improve transport.

The President commissioned Sh221 million Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project, which is expected to enhance livelihoods and boost irrigation in the area.

He also inspected progress of the Sh2.2 billion Loitoktok Affordable Housing Project, and laid the foundation stone for the Sh220 million Loitoktok Kenya Medical Training College student hostels with a 580-bed capacity.

At Kimana, in Kajiado South Constituency, President Ruto commissioned the Sh2.7 billion Sultan Hamud-Loitoktok 132kV Transmission Line and Loitoktok Sub-Station, which will serve the residents of Kajiado South and parts of Makueni County.

He inspected construction of the Kimana modern market, which is aimed at giving traders dignified working environment.

At Namanga, Kajiado Central Constituency, the President commissioned the Namanga Sub-Station, a project of the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO), which is part of the 132KV Machakos- Konza-Isinya-Namanga Transmission Project.

Namanga Modern Market, which is under construction at a cost of Sh50 million, will benefit 120 traders at the border town.

In Kajiado town, the President toured the construction of the Kajiado Affordable Housing Project, a Sh473 million investment that will deliver 196 housing units, as well as the 100-unit police housing project at a cost of Sh137 million.

He also inspected the progress of the 580-bed student hostels at Maasai National Polytechnic, which is being built at a cost of KSh216 million.

Ruto ordered the closer of Tata Chemicals, saying the government will identify a new and responsible investor to take over soda ash mining operations at Lake Magadi.

The President said Tata Chemicals had failed to adequately modernise the plant, create sufficient employment opportunities for residents, and deliver meaningful economic benefits to the people of Kenya.

“It is unfair for one company to dominate the ownership and operations of Magadi Soda for years, yet it has done little to improve the factory or create employment opportunities for our youth,” he said at Rombo in Kajiado South Constituency.

He added: “Because they have been unable to do anything meaningful with the plant for more than 100 years, I have directed them to pack up and go.”

The Ministry of Mining suspended the company’s mining operations in July 2026 over concerns relating to regulatory compliance, value addition and licensing.

The ministry also ordered the closure of the company’s depot in Kajiado Town for contravening environmental regulations.

In addition, the company has been unable to reach an agreement with the Kajiado County Government over a land rates dispute following the expiry of its operating licence in 2023.

The plant produces soda ash, or sodium carbonate, a key industrial mineral used in the manufacture of glass, soap and laundry detergents, among other products.

Despite being Africa’s largest soda ash producer, President Ruto noted that the operation had not delivered commensurate benefits to Kenyans over its more than 100-year history, particularly because much of the soda ash produced is exported for processing and consumption in overseas markets.

The Government, the President said, would therefore prioritise an investor capable of modernising the facility, expanding local value addition, creating jobs for young people, and ensuring that Kenya derives greater economic value from its natural resources.

World.title: IG Kanja orders probe into abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Standard Group PLC Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered immediate and transparent investigations into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.

The National Police Service (NPS) said it had taken note of reports that Kiprotich was allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday and had moved swiftly to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said the police service treats kidnapping and abduction with the utmost seriousness, describing the offences as a threat to the lives, liberty and security of Kenyans.

“The Inspector General of Police has accordingly ordered immediate investigations to determine what transpired, including the identity of the heavily armed individuals reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle,” Nyaga said in a statement.

The NPS said its Anti-Abduction Unit, established to investigate abductions and disappearances, had taken up the matter and would work to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“We unequivocally condemn any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation intended to interfere with press freedom or any other constitutional right,” Nyaga said.

The police service assured the public that the investigation into the Gilgil incident would be conducted transparently, stressing that no one was above the law.

The development comes amid growing condemnation of Kiprotich’s alleged abduction, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also calling for an immediate investigation.

CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a “shameful indictment” of the Kenya Kwanza administration, raising concerns over the safety of journalists and press freedom in the country.

“The attempt to forcibly disappear Alex Kiprotich, three days after President William Ruto railed against The Standard Group, reflects the growing dangers that journalists face in Kenya, despite the president’s earlier promise to allow the press to work freely,” Quintal said.

The New York-based press freedom organisation further expressed concern over what it described as an escalation in cases of abductions and enforced disappearances in Kenya.

World.title: Trumpets of reforms blow louder as Kenya marks 16 years under 2010 Constitution
World.content:
The Constitution, Kenyan flag and the National anthem. [PCS]

On Thursday, August 27, a group of people largely composed of the youth gathered under some trees at Jeevanjee Gardens in Nairobi, carrying Kenyans flag, and banners and placards inscribed with "implement the constitution. Kenyans first" words.

These were in protests against what they believed is deliberate failure of those in authority to fully implement the 2010 Constitution.

World.title: Ruto allies hit back at Gachagua over IEBC tender concerns
World.content:
The Kenya Integrated Elections Management System (KIEMS) kit. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto’s allies led by National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula have launched a scathing attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and the Opposition over their criticism of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), citing blackmail by the Opposition.

The leaders warned that attempts by politicians to dictate how the electoral agency procures technology and other election materials could undermine public confidence in the 2027 General Election.

World.title: IEBC rejects Gachagua's claims, defends 2027 polls preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC dismissed Gachagua's claims of political interference, graft and voter suppression in 2027 polls.

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has dismissed allegations of political interference, corruption and voter suppression surrounding preparations for the 2027 General Election, terming the claims false, unsubstantiated and aimed at undermining public confidence in the electoral body.

In a statement issued on Thursday, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the allegations followed statements made by Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a press briefing on Wednesday.

The commission specifically rejected claims that politicians had purchased a house for its chairperson to influence him, saying the allegation had changed from an alleged Sh80 million property to one worth Sh200 million.

"The allegations that a house has been purchased for the Chairperson of IEBC by some politicians for purposes of influencing him are unfortunate, unfair and unsubstantiated to date," Ethekon stated.

The commission also challenged Gachagua to provide evidence, including the location of the property, sale and transfer documents, payment receipts and details of the parties involved, and submit them to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission for investigation.

The electoral body also dismissed claims of improper staff changes, saying deployment and redeployment of employees was part of its normal administrative functions and was guided by its human resource policies and public service regulations.

"The Commission complies with its Human Resource policies, guidelines and other relevant instruments under the larger public service when engaging employees," the statement read in part.

It further denied allegations of malpractice against the chairperson and vice-chairperson, describing them as fabricated claims intended to damage the reputation of the commissioners and the commission.

Magarini by-election

On the Magarini by-election, IEBC said the poll was conducted in a free, fair and credible manner and was not challenged through an election petition. The commission added that it had successfully conducted several by-elections and was prepared to oversee the 2027 General Election.

At the same time, IEBC also defended its procurement process for election technology and ballot papers, saying all tenders were being conducted in accordance with Chapter 12 of the Constitution and the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015.

"Two key tenders, one for the Integrated Elections Management System, hardware and accessories, and another for ballot papers and other election materials, have temporarily been halted following a request for review filed before the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board," IEBC stated.

According to IEBC, documents for the technology tender were uploaded on its website and the Public Procurement Information Portal on August 11, 2026.

The commission said the technical specifications were generic and performance-based and open to all qualified suppliers. It stressed that the procurement process was still at its initial stages and that no company had been awarded the tender.

Voter register protected

The commission also dismissed claims that voter registration data could be manipulated or shared with external parties, insisting that the Register of Voters remained under its exclusive custody.

"Voter registration involves several stages, including in-person registration, verification of identity, collection of biometric and biographical data, transmission to a central database and automated biometric deduplication," IEBC added.

Flagged records are subjected to data cleaning, validation and adjudication before valid records are incorporated into the register.

The register will subsequently undergo a 30-day biometric verification exercise, followed by an independent audit before it is finalised and certified for use in an election.

IEBC said allegations of bribery, predetermined tender awards and voter suppression were false and potentially harmful to public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: When will autumn 2026 begin astronomically?
World.content:
Approximately 18 days remain until the start of autumn in 2026.

The autumnal equinox will occur on Wednesday, September 23, marking the end of summer and the beginning of a new season during which the weather will gradually improve, particularly with a decrease in temperatures and humidity levels.

Summer began astronomically on Sunday, June 21, ending with the start of autumn on September 23.

Autumn’s duration

Astronomical calculations for the seasons of 2026 reveal a difference in the duration of each season.

Spring began on Friday, March 20, and lasted 92 days and 17 hours, while summer began on Sunday, June 21st, and will last 93 days and 15 hours.

Autumn begins astronomically on Wednesday, September 23, and lasts for 89 days and 20 hours, while the winter season begins on Monday, December 21, and lasts for 88 days and 23 hours.

As autumn approaches, Egypt will gradually enters a transitional phase during which temperatures decrease.

However, this does not mean the sudden disappearance of summer weather, as some summer-like characteristics are expected to persist during the first half of September, particularly high temperatures and humidity levels.

Autumnal Equinox

The autumnal equinox occurs when the sun’s rays are almost perpendicular to the equator, resulting in approximately equal day and night lengths across most of the world.

Following the autumnal equinox, daylight hours gradually decrease while nighttime hours increase in the Northern Hemisphere, leading to a gradual change in weather patterns as autumn progresses.

Summer Solstice

The summer solstice occurred on Sunday, June 21, 2026, when the sun reached its northernmost point in the sky, coinciding with the Earth’s North Pole reaching its maximum tilt of approximately 23.5 degrees towards the sun.

This resulted in the longest day and shortest night of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

The sun rose from its northernmost point in the northeast, and shadows cast at midday were the shortest of the year.

On the summer solstice, the sun appears to reach its highest and longest point in the sky as seen from the Northern Hemisphere, resulting in longer days than nights.

Daylight hours then gradually decrease as the autumnal equinox approaches.

Gradual Weather Change

With the arrival of autumn, a transitional phase begins.

Temperatures continue to decline gradually, while humidity levels decrease compared to the peak of summer, leading to increasingly mild weather as winter approaches.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Lawsuit to place Nawal al-Degwy’s assets under guardianship adjourned to November 4
World.content:
The New Cairo Family Court on Saturday adjourned the hearing for the lawsuit filed by Nawal al-Degwy’s grandson, Amr al-Degwy —in which he seeks to place her assets under legal guardianship— to November 4.

This postponement allows for the submission of documents withdrawing the motion to recuse the presiding judges.

The decision follows the withdrawal by Degwy’s defense team of their motion to recuse the panel of the court hearing the case.

At the previous hearing, the court had decided to adjourn proceedings to allow the litigants time to submit documents, reports, and legal memoranda supporting their respective positions.

The lawsuit comes amid escalating family disputes within the Degwy family, following accusations by Nawal al-Degwy that several family members misappropriated funds and gold jewelry valued at over a quarter of a billion Egyptian pounds.

One of Degwy’s grandchildren filed a guardianship suit, arguing that her continued management of her own finances could lead to ruin.

Her defense team maintains that the suit should be dismissed, asserting that she possesses full legal capacity and is capable of managing her affairs and finances without guardianship.

World.title: EgyptAir launches direct flights from Cairo to Zanzibar
World.content:
EgyptAir has launched direct flights from Cairo to Zanzibar, Tanzania, as the Egyptian flag carrier continues to expand its network across Africa.

The airline will operate two flights a week on Fridays and Sundays using Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft.

EgyptAir Airlines Chairman Mohamed Alyan said the inaugural flight recorded a load factor of more than 90%. The airline has also introduced promotional fares in economy and business class for the new route.

EgyptAir Holding Company Chairman Ahmed Adel said that the service is part of the airline’s plans to add more destinations across Africa and provide passengers with additional travel options.

The new route provides a direct connection between Cairo and Zanzibar, one of East Africa’s major tourist destinations, and is expected to support travel and tourism between Egypt and Tanzania.

Tickets are available through EgyptAir’s website, offices and travel agencies.

World.title: NCW launches new agricultural waste recycling phase
World.content:
The National Council for Women (NCW) has launched a new phase of its agricultural waste recycling project to produce compost, which is organic fertilizer, in Giza Governorate.

The initiative aims to support the economic empowerment of rural women and convert agricultural waste into high-value products, thereby enhancing their participation in the green economy.

Project experts explained that compost production contributes to improving soil quality and agricultural products, reducing reliance on chemical fertilizers and mitigating the negative environmental impacts resulting from the unsafe disposal of agricultural waste.

World.title: Grand Mufti reaffirms strong support for Palestinian Cause
World.content:
The Grand Mufti Nazir Ayyad said the Palestinian Cause remains deeply rooted in Egypt’s national consciousness, stressing the religious and humanitarian responsibility to support the Palestinian people.

Ayyad made the remarks during a meeting with Palestinian Chief Justice Mahmoud Al-Habbash on the sidelines of the 11th international fatwa conference in Cairo. They discussed developments in the Palestinian issue and the role of religious institutions in raising awareness, preserving Palestinian identity and countering attempts to distort its history.

Al-Habbash praised Egypt’s longstanding support for the Palestinian cause and its religious institutions’ efforts to promote awareness of its importance, describing Egypt as a key Arab and Islamic pillar of support for Palestine.

World.title: Petroleum Minister highlights refining, transport upgrades to secure energy supplies
World.content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi affirmed that upgrading infrastructure in the petroleum sector represents a key pillar to bolster energy security and support Egyptian economic competitiveness, noting that upgrading refineries, improving crude and petroleum product transport networks, and expanding storage capacities top sector priorities in the coming period.

Badawi spoke during the meetings of the general assembly of the Petroleum Pipelines Company and Assiut Oil Refining Company to approve financial results for fiscal year 2025/2026. The meeting was attended by Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Esmat, Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid, and Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem via videoconference, alongside sector officials.

The minister stressed that these efforts maximize the value of Egypt’s petroleum resources, increase added value for crude, and raise distribution efficiency, reinforcing Egypt’s position as a regional energy hub leveraging its prime geography and integrated infrastructure.

Badawi highlighted the coordination between the petroleum and electricity ministries in securing fuel supplies for power stations, which preserved grid stability during peak summer demand.

He noted that both companies play an essential role in securing national energy supplies by refining crude, transporting products nationwide, and fueling power stations to sustain operations.

The minister reaffirmed that enhancing refineries is a strategic priority alongside ongoing expansion projects to optimize growing crude production and produce higher-value petroleum products.

He urged accelerating refinery expansions to supply local markets, narrow the production-consumption gap, and fulfill domestic demand.

Badawi underscored that occupational health and safety is a shared responsibility across all staff and leadership, stressing compliance with safety rules and expanding training programs to protect personnel.

For his part, Minister of Electricity Mahmoud Esmat praised the petroleum sector’s efforts in supplying power generation plants, noting sustained coordination stabilized the grid during peak loads exceeding 40,000 MW.

During the Petroleum Pipelines Company meeting, company Chairman Haggag Rabie Keilany reviewed fiscal year 2025/2026 results, stating the company met Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation transport plans and secured power plant fuel needs.

He noted the firm operates 6,300 km of pipelines that transported over 8.2 billion ton-km, alongside 155 storage depots holding 2.5 million cubic meters.

Keilany added that ongoing strategic projects include expanding the Sokhna terminal over 19 feddans to raise storage capacity from 300,000 to 460,000 cubic meters.

Projects also encompass renewing the 135-km Port Said-Abu Sultan-Suez pipeline and building the 140-km MIDOR-Hamra line to support Hamra port expansions and supply New Alamein refining projects.

Badawi directed company leaders to draft an integrated five-year plan to upgrade crude and product transport infrastructure and maximize operational efficiency.

The minister highlighted leveraging Egypt’s assets to advance its role as a regional trade hub, citing the establishment of Fujairah-Alamein Oil and Gas and SUMED’s expanding operations between the Red Sea and Mediterranean.

At the Assiut Oil Refining Company assembly, Chairman Issa Abdel Aal reported output valued at nearly 3 billion dollars, refining 3.314 million tons of crude with high-value products representing 57% of output.

He explained that building the third distillation unit will double refining capacity from 4.5 to 9.5 million tons annually, securing local fuel supplies and providing mazut for the ANOPC complex.

Abdel Aal indicated that operations maximized middle distillates, with LPG reaching 62,000 tons, 80-octane gasoline at 366,000 tons, 92-octane gasoline at 419,000 tons, jet fuel at 115,000 tons, and diesel rising 20% to 911,000 tons.

Badawi commended the company for employing Upper Egypt residents across 95% of its workforce, emphasizing its role in regional development and local job creation.

On social responsibility, Abdel Aal noted qualifying 400 university students and graduates in Assiut for freelance digital work, alongside equipping a bone marrow transplant unit, blood bank, and physical therapy wing at Sohag Oncology Center.

World.title: Masked men block traffic to UK’s Port of Dover in apparent anti-immigrant protest
World.content:
London Associated Press — A group of masked men blocked roads leading to Britain’s busiest ferry port on Saturday in what officials said appeared to be an anti-immigration protest.

The Port of Dover said all traffic in and out was “stopped due to an ongoing public order incident,” and police said they were “engaging with the protesters.”

Video posted on social media showed several dozen men in black, their faces covered, standing across a major road near the port. One clip showed demonstrators linking arms across a main road and shouting “stop the boats.”

Chris Vinson, a Conservative Party local councilor, said the protest appeared to be “illegal migration-related.”

“I’m not aware that there’s been any violence, although clearly, having the path of your vehicle blocked by men wearing black paramilitary gear and balaclavas is extremely intimidating,” he said.

The National Highways agency said the protest blocked routes to the port and caused a 4-mile (6.4-kilometer) traffic jam on Saturday morning. The Port of Dover said one road to the port had reopened by late morning.

P&O Ferries, which runs services between Dover and Calais in France, said passengers who missed their ferry would be offered the next available crossing.

Dover, about 70 miles (110 kilometers) southeast of London, dealt with more than 9 million passengers and 2 million freight vehicles in 2025, according to the port’s website.

A general view of the port of Dover with the coastguard station, top left, in Dover, England, on February 26, 2025. Kin Cheung/AP

The town has been the site of previous anti-immigrant protests focused on migrants who cross the Channel from France in small boats. Some politicians, including Nigel Farage of hard-right party Reform UK, have seized on the issue. He branded the asylum seekers “an invasion” in a Friday speech.

The Labour Party government says stepped-up law enforcement cooperation between Britain and France has helped reduce the number of people making the crossing this year by more than 40 percent compared to 2025.

Mike Tapp, a Labour lawmaker who represents Dover in Parliament, criticized “idiots coming to Dover to cause disruption.”

“I bet if you asked any one of those ‘protesters’ they wouldn’t know small boat crossing are down by 40 percent and we are working hard to fix the mess,” he wrote on Facebook on Saturday. “Go home, enjoy your weekend/get a job.”

World.title: US military strikes three Iranian tankers in retaliation for missile attacks
World.content:
The United States military said Saturday its forces struck three Iranian crude oil carriers after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships.

The fresh exchanges threaten to heighten a shipping war in and beyond the Persian Gulf, as Iran seeks to prevent shipping transiting the Strait of Hormuz without its consent and the US steps up targeting of Iranian shipping.

The two sides traded strikes earlier this week for the first time in over a month, and the new attacks risk another retaliatory cycle.

“A U.S. aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer successfully evaded multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks,” US Central Command said in a statement Saturday.

In response, US forces “permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask.”

Outside the Persian Gulf, according to CENTCOM, an unladen crude tanker called the M/T Kylo was “completely destroyed” after being hit multiple times to render it inoperable.

CENTCOM said the ships “are part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies.”

“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” said Adm. Brad Cooper, the CENTCOM commander.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote Saturday on X, “It’s simple: if Iran shoots at U.S. ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers. All they have to do is stop shooting at @USNavy.”

Hegseth added that the US could strike Iran’s oil tanker fleet in the Middle East or in the Indo-Pacific region, writing, “Iran’s oil tanker fleet is defenseless — Iran has no navy or air force.”

Iran’s foreign affairs ministry strongly condemned the US actions in a statement Saturday, calling the attacks “illegal and aggressive” and an “overt threat to international peace and the security of commercial shipping.”

The attacks constitute a “clear violation” of the UN Charter, the ministry said.

Iran’s state-run Islamic Republic News Agency reported the statement by US Central Command, adding that “Iranian officials emphasized that they would respond strongly to any attack.”

Earlier Saturday, Iranian news agencies said a tanker came under missile attack by US forces near Kharg Island. The tanker was hit by four projectiles fired by US forces, Tasnim reported. There were no casualties, the agency added.

Audio confirmed by CNN showed that a US military aircraft issued warnings to the ship via an emergency channel. In one, an American-accented voice says: “Motor Tanker STARK 1, this is the United States military aircraft. I am preparing to fire at your stern. You have 10 minutes to clear the crew from the stern of your ship. Over.”

In a later exchange, the ship is warned: “This was your final warning … get into your lifeboats and abandon the ship immediately.”

The conflict between Iran and the United States is in a volatile limbo, with both battling for control over the vital Strait of Hormuz, which is critical for global oil supplies.

Kharg Island, a coral outcrop off Iran’s coast, has typically handled roughly 90% of the country’s crude oil exports. The island has been attacked throughout the conflict, and US President Donald Trump has previously threatened to capture it.

Shipping data and satellite imagery indicate there are nearly 20 Iranian tankers at anchor near Kharg, unable to exit the Gulf because of the US naval blockade but in many cases fully laden.

In the Gulf as a whole and just beyond, in the Gulf of Oman, there are more than 50 Iranian tankers, according to ship tracking services.

On Thursday, US Vice President JD Vance denied the conflict should even be described as a “war,” adding that despite the recent flare-up there was “no active shooting.”

He also refused to lay out a timetable for ending the conflict, suggesting instead it was up to Iran to conclude the war that began with joint US-Israeli airstrikes six months ago.

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: Liberia: CDC Debunks NPP Chairman Mulbah, Says NPP Was Never Invited to Opposition Roundtable
World.content:
Monrovia — The opposition Congress for Democratic Change has rejected claims by National Patriotic Party Chairman George Mulbah that his party declined an invitation to participate in a proposed opposition roundtable, insisting that no such invitation was extended to the NPP as an institution.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

CDC Secretary-General Jefferson Koijee said the record must be set straight, arguing that the NPP and its national leadership were never formally invited to the planned engagement.

“At no time and at no point did the Congress for Democratic Change extend an invitation to the National Patriotic Party or its national leadership to participate in the proposed opposition roundtable discussion,” Koijee said.

His comments followed an announcement by Mulbah that the NPP would not participate in the planned opposition meeting.

Koijee said while a number of “outstanding, uncompromising” members of the NPP were invited, they were invited in their individual capacities and not as representatives of the party.

“Neither the NPP as an institution nor its National Chairman, Mr. George Mulbah, was invited,” he said.

He accused Mulbah of creating the impression that the CDC had sought the institutional participation of the NPP and was subsequently rejected.

“The National Chairman should therefore immediately cease and desist from creating the impression that the CDC sought the institutional participation of the NPP and was subsequently rejected,” Koijee added.

The dispute comes against the backdrop of the two parties’ political history. The NPP was a key component of the Coalition for Democratic Change during the 2017 presidential and legislative elections. The coalition brought together the CDC, which produced then-presidential candidate George Manneh Weah, and the NPP, which produced then-Vice Standard Bearer Jewel Howard-Taylor.

The CDC-led coalition won the 2017 presidential election and subsequently governed Liberia from 2018 to 2024.

Koijee also questioned the political circumstances surrounding Mulbah’s statement, particularly his reported employment within the Office of Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung.

He said the relationship raises questions about the “independence, timing and motivation” of statements directed at opposition cooperation.

Koijee further criticized what he described as the NPP leadership’s weak response when its standard bearer and former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor faced criminal allegations and incarceration.

“At that defining moment, the statement attributed to the party leadership was, in our view, one of the weakest responses in the history of a party once renowned for its fighting spirit, political potency and revolutionary character,” he said.

The CDC Secretary-General maintained that his party would not allow what he described as political distractions and manufactured controversies to undermine cooperation among opposition forces.

“The mighty Congress for Democratic Change has no room for political distractions, manufactured controversies or attempts to fracture genuine opposition solidarity,” Koijee said.

He pledged that the CDC would remain “vigilant” and respond to what it considers efforts to undermine democratic cooperation among opposition groups.

Koijee concluded by thanking individuals and institutions that were formally invited to the roundtable and accepted the invitation, saying their participation demonstrated that the broader democratic conversation would continue.

“The democratic conversation continues, and no political grandstanding will derail it,” he said.

World.title: Co-Defendant Challenges Judge’s Ruling Granting Ex-VP Taylor House Arrest, Calls It Unlawful
World.content:
MONROVIA — A day after Criminal Court “C” ordered former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor moved from Monrovia Central Prison to guarded house detention on medical grounds, a co-defendant in the same narcotics case has formally challenged the ruling, arguing that Judge Ousman F. Feika had no legal authority to grant it and asking him to reverse himself.



In a filing captio ned “Exceptions to His Honor Ousman F. Feika’s Ruling in Granting Co-Defendant Jewel Howard Taylor Compassionate Release,” Garpue K. Wonlue takes issue with the September 4 order on six separate grounds, most of them turning on a single argument: that the law Judge Feika relied on does not apply to someone in Taylor’s position.



The Case So Far



Taylor, Liberia’s vice president from 2018 to 2024, was arrested at Roberts International Airport on August 19 in connection with what officials have described as a transnational narcotics trafficking investigation tied to a record cocaine seizure earlier this year.

She was formally charged over eight counts, including unlicensed importation, unlicensed sale and trading, and illicit trafficking of drugs, along with money laundering and abuse-of-office allegations.



Her lawyers spent the following weeks trying, without success, to keep her out of the general prison population.

A Monrovia City Court magistrate denied an initial request for compassionate detention, ruling that granting it fell within the authority of the Ministry of Justice rather than the judiciary the defense’s follow-up appeal to the Supreme Court challenging that denial did not stop Taylor from being remanded to Monrovia Central Prison. She entered custody on September 2.



The case then moved to Criminal Court “C,” the circuit with jurisdiction over major drug offenses, where Judge Feika ordered Taylor’s immediate transfer from prison to 24-hour guarded house detention at her residence, converting her pre-trial custody into house arrest pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

Feika was explicit that the order rested solely on medical grounds and carried no bearing on guilt, writing that the release “shall therefore not constitute dismissal, acquittal, pardon, immunity, or termination of the criminal proceedings.

The judge also noted that the State itself had not opposed the request.



The Challenge



Wonlue’s filing does not dispute that Taylor has a medical condition. Instead, it argues that the court used the wrong statute to address it — and in doing so, exceeded its authority. The exceptions raise six points:



1. Jurisdiction: The filing argues that Chapter 34, Section 34.20 of the Criminal Procedure Law — the provision Judge Feika relied on — applies only to people who have already been indicted, tried, convicted, sentenced and committed to prison. Taylor, still awaiting trial, doesn’t fit that description, the filing contends, and Wonlue asks the court to rescind the ruling and have her returned to custody at Monrovia Central Prison.



2. No such remedy exists: The Criminal Procedure Law provides for bail under Chapter 13 for the accused, and for commitment under Chapter 34 for the convicted, the filing says — but nothing in between for a pre-trial detainee seeking release on medical grounds. Granting “compassionate leave” from pre-trial detention, it argues, is a remedy the court created rather than one the statute authorizes.



3. Consent doesn’t create jurisdiction: The fact that the State did not oppose Taylor’s request doesn’t change the analysis, the filing argues — parties cannot agree to give a court power the statute doesn’t grant it.



4. Equal treatment. This is the filing’s broadest argument: that granting one high-profile, pre-trial detainee a form of release unavailable to others sets up a two-tier system, at odds with the fairness-in-administration standard in Section 1.2 of the Criminal Procedure Law and Article 11 of the 1986 Constitution. The filing points out that many pre-trial detainees at Monrovia Central Prison have untreated medical conditions of their own, and argues the proper remedy was to order the Bureau of Corrections to provide adequate care in custody — not to release one defendant from it.



5. The nature of the charges and the cost of enforcement: Given that Taylor faces serious felony charges — importation of controlled drugs, money laundering and abuse of office, as the filing describes them — Wonlue argues the release conditions impose an unfunded, unauthorized burden on the State, which must now provide round-the-clock security at her residence. Surrendering travel documents, the filing adds, doesn’t eliminate flight risk on its own.



6. The inquiry should have ended sooner: Once the court determined that Section 34.20 doesn’t apply to pre-trial detainees, the filing argues, that finding should have ended the motion rather than being followed by relief anyway. It maintains the appropriate avenue for a detainee with medical concerns is a bail motion under Chapter 13 — with bond, sureties and monitoring conditions — not compassionate leave.



What’s Being Asked



The filing asks Judge Feika to reverse course: to rule that Section 34.20 doesn’t apply to pre-trial detainees, to direct the Bureau of Corrections and Ministry of Health to provide Taylor medical treatment at JFK Medical Center or another approved facility while she remains in custody, and — if release is warranted at all — to take it up as a bail application under Chapter 13, with a substantial bond and formal sureties, rather than as compassionate leave.



Judge Feika has not yet ruled on the exceptions. Taylor remains under house arrest at her residence pending the outcome. All defendants in the case, including Taylor, are presumed innocent, and the charges against them remain allegations that have not been tested at trial.

World.title: Liberia Champions Key Discussions on Preventive Diplomacy and a Robust E10 Voice at the 9th E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue in Panama
World.content:
Panama – Liberia’s Political Coordinator to the United Nations Security Council, Cllr. Aloysius Jappah assumed an active role in the 9th E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue, hosted by the Republic of Panama in Panama City from 1 to 2 September 2026, delivering substantive interventions on preventive diplomacy, Council effectiveness, and the responsibilities that come with elected membership of the UN Security Council.

Since 2019, the Dialogue has convened annually to unite the ten elected members of the Council (the E10) with the five incoming members (the I5) to enhance institutional memory, coordinate priorities, and bolster the Council’s ability to uphold international peace and security.

This year’s event was inaugurated and concluded by Panama’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Javier Eduardo Martínez-Acha Vásquez, and honored at its closing by former President H.E. Mireya Moscoso.

The current E10 for 2026 includes Bahrain, Colombia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Liberia, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia.

Starting on 1 January 2027, the newly elected I5 will consist of Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, and Zimbabwe, replacing Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia as their mandates end on 31 December 2026.

Speaking during the session on “Preventive Diplomacy in Action,” moderated with the support of the Dag Hammarskjöld Foundation and its presenters Sigrid and Henrik, Cllr. Jappah anchored Liberia’s contribution in the letter of the United Nations Charter — Chapter VI (Articles 33–38) on the pacific settlement of disputes, Chapter VIII (Article 52) on regional arrangements, and Article 99 on the Secretary-General’s early-warning authority.

“The best Council intervention is a crisis that diplomacy prevents,” Cllr. Jappah affirmed, adding that “the Charter calls on us to extinguish the spark of conflict before it becomes a blaze. When we subscribed to this organization, we pledged to fulfill that obligation.”

Commenting on the operational challenge of moving from early warning to early action, the Political Coordinator emphasized what he called the prevention paradox — that when preventive diplomacy succeeds, the crisis does not occur, and success is therefore less visible than failure.

He cautioned that sovereignty concerns and geopolitical divisions frequently delay Council action, resulting in inaction until violence erupts. He warned that “Early warning without early action,” he warned, “is only a forecast of failure.”

Drawing on Liberia’s own post-conflict experience, Cllr. Jappah stressed that peace agreements close a chapter but do not, by themselves, remove the grievances, institutional weaknesses, or local tensions that can reignite conflict.

He called for the sustained deployment of good offices, mediation support, regional engagement, inclusive dialogue, confidence-building measures, early-warning capacity, and local peace infrastructures — with the consent and ownership of the country concerned.

“Peace agreements close a chapter; preventive diplomacy helps keep the next chapter from reopening the war,” he said, noting that sustained international, regional, and national engagement has been decisive in consolidating and protecting Liberia’s hard-won peace.

Contributing to Session V on reinvigorating the Council’s role in preventive diplomacy, Cllr. Jappah observed that the Dialogue offered members a valuable opportunity to internalize how a hasty drawdown of peacekeeping operations can leave a country vulnerable.

He was speaking in response to interventions on how transnational organized crime — including transcontinental drug trafficking — can undermine governance in states just emerging from conflict, where institutions remain fragile.

On the question of how the E10 should engage the incoming Secretary-General, Cllr. Jappah urged elected members to first conduct an honest internal assessment and to invest deliberately in strengthening themselves as a caucus.

He proposed that the E10 build the discipline and coordination required to create what he described as a collective “veto,” together with the guardrails to use that leverage responsibly. He observed that, over a two-year tenure, “before an elected member really gets to understand the Council and its dynamics, it is time to exit,” and he called on the E10 to systematically leverage the institutional memory of what he termed the “Farewell Five” — the five outgoing members concluding their terms each year — so that hard-earned experience is transferred rather than lost.

He further cautioned that the Council too frequently holds briefings and open meetings at which statements are made that contain useful antidotes but are followed by no concrete action.

He urged that the traditional E10 luncheons move beyond merely setting the agenda for the Secretary-General’s luncheon with Permanent Representatives, and instead become a forum in which elected members act with one voice on decisive issues before the Council.

Cllr. Jappah welcomed the newly elected members—Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, and Zimbabwe—emphasizing the importance of continuity in preventive practice, disciplined coordination among members, and adherence to the Charter as the Council’s composition changes.

“Prevention is not an abstract ideal,” he concluded. “It is the disciplined practice of acting before choices disappear.”

The E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue, established in 2019, gathers incoming, serving, and outgoing UN Security Council members to enhance institutional memory and align objectives. Panama, holding a non-permanent seat, hosted the 9th edition during its term, ending on December 31, 2026.

World.title: Liberia Elevates Diplomatic Standing as August E10 UN Security Council Coordinator
World.content:
NEW YORK — Liberia has successfully concluded its leadership as Coordinator of the Ten Elected Members (E10) of the United Nations Security Council for August 2026, marking a historic milestone in its global diplomatic resurgence.

Stepping into the helm of the E10 alongside Bahrain, Colombia, DRC, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Panama, Somalia, and Pakistan, Liberia strategically projected African leadership, unified non-permanent members, and shaped critical debate on pressing global peace and security files.

Key Achievements and Diplomatic Interventions

High-Level Security Council Diplomacy: Hosted UN Secretary-General António Guterres and E10 Ambassadors for a strategic luncheon centered on accelerating humanitarian interventions in Gaza and the West Bank.

Regional & Crisis Resolution:

Chaired the Political Coordinators’ Meeting to align consensus on the Libyan political process, security dynamics across West Africa and the Sahel, and the E10 Joint Statement on Security Council Working Methods.

International Judicial Oversight: Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary Lewis G. Brown II convened high-level negotiations with International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) President Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, driving resolution terms on judicial archives, institutional downsizing, and UN oversight sensitivities involving Rwanda and Tanzania.

🇹🇿 Humanitarian Advocacy & International Law: Spearheaded expert briefings on the Ukraine humanitarian crisis and led targeted press interventions demanding the immediate release of illegally detained UN and aid personnel in Yemen.

Council Reform & Strategic Alignment: Championed reform of Security Council Subsidiary Bodies to streamline operations and ensure unified diplomatic alignment between the E10 and the Permanent Five (P5).

A Lasting Legacy on the World Stage

Liberia’s month-long tenure as Coordinator demonstrated strategic leadership, robust policy alignment, and an elevated ability to forge consensus among diverse international partners. Upon concluding its leadership, the E10 alliance formally commended Liberia for its decisive steering of the Council’s thematic priorities throughout August.

Meanwhile, Pakistan has assumed the E10 Coordination role for September, while Liberia remains positioned as an influential, principled voice on the Security Council, committed to driving international peace, stability, and multilateral cooperation.

World.title: Liberia: Ex-Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor to Receive Medical Care at Residence Under Restrictions as Drug Case Continues
World.content:
MONROVIA — Former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor is set to receive medical attention outside detention under strict conditions imposed by Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika amid ongoing concerns about her health.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The court’s decision comes after Howard-Taylor’s lawyers raised medical concerns and sought her release from detention to allow her to receive treatment.

Under the court’s directive, Howard-Taylor is required to surrender all travel documents, effectively restricting her ability to leave the country while the case remains pending.

The former vice president will also be subject to limitations on visitors at her residence, with access restricted to a family member and her physician or physician’s assistant.

Howard-Taylor remains entangled in an ongoing investigation and prosecution involving allegations connected to an alleged transnational cocaine-trafficking operation.

Her legal team has maintained that her medical condition requires appropriate care, while the case continues to attract public attention because of the seriousness of the allegations.

The court’s latest action provides for medical considerations while maintaining judicial controls over Howard-Taylor as proceedings continue.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Feika Grants Jewel Howard-Taylor Compassionate Release
World.content:
Monrovia — Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika has granted former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor’s request for compassionate release from detention on medical grounds.

The ruling follows concerns raised by Howard-Taylor’s legal team about her medical condition and their request that she be permitted to receive medical care outside detention.

Under the court’s ruling, Howard-Taylor is required to surrender all travel documents to the court as part of the conditions of her release.

The court also ordered that visits to her residence be limited to a family member and her physician or physician’s assistant.

Howard-Taylor is facing criminal charges in connection with an ongoing narcotics investigation. She has denied the allegations.

The court’s decision allows her to leave detention while the legal proceedings continue.

This is a developing story.

World.title: Liberia: LIS Officer Thomas Kesselly Reportedly Shot in Foya
World.content:
MONROVIA — Thomas Kesselly, a member of the Liberia Immigration Service (LIS), was reportedly shot on Thursday, September 3, 2026, with conflicting accounts emerging over the incident.

Kesselley was reportedly shot at the LIS Academy in Foya.

While initial reports said Kesselly was shot, another account claims he shot himself.

However, family sources have expressed doubts about the self-inflicted shooting claim and are seeking clarity on what happened.

Kesselly’s condition and the circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear as authorities have yet to provide a definitive account.

World.title: Liberia: Witness Alleges Howard-Taylor Link to Cocaine Trafficking Investigation and Political Plot
World.content:
Monrovia — A police investigator has testified in court about an alleged cocaine-trafficking operation in Liberia, telling the court that former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor was allegedly approached over a proposed protection arrangement and that discussions also involved an alleged plan targeting the administration of former President George Weah.

The testimony was given by Raphael Wilson, Acting Commissioner of Police for the Crimes Services Division, who said he supervised the investigative team that conducted the probe.

Wilson told the court that investigators traced the alleged network to meetings involving Liberians and foreign nationals in Dubai and Liberia, beginning around 2021.

According to his testimony, a Liberian identified as Sheikh Bashir Kanti met individuals in Dubai who expressed interest in returning to Liberia to resume business activities.

Wilson alleged that the individuals later disclosed plans to establish a cocaine-trafficking operation, with Liberia allegedly intended to serve as a transit point.

The witness further testified that the foreign nationals sought protection from a senior government official to facilitate their activities in Liberia.

According to Wilson, meetings were subsequently arranged in Liberia involving Bashir, the foreign nationals and individuals identified in the investigation as Tony and Maga.

He said investigators secretly recorded at least one of the meetings using cameras and written notes as part of their investigation.

Wilson testified that cocaine trafficking and the use of Liberia as a transit route were discussed during the meeting.

The witness further alleged that participants wanted assurances that their activities would receive protection from influential government officials.

According to Wilson, Jewel Howard-Taylor agreed to provide the requested protection but indicated that she would first return to Liberia and discuss the matter with her superior.

The testimony forms part of the prosecution’s effort to establish Howard-Taylor’s alleged connection to the broader investigation.

Alleged Political Plot

Wilson also testified about discussions that, according to the prosecution, involved an alleged plan directed against the government of former President George Weah.

The witness said the discussions surrounding the alleged protection arrangement were connected to a broader political plan involving senior political figures and an alleged attempt to undermine or overthrow the government.

However, Wilson’s testimony did not establish in court who allegedly initiated the plan, the specific actions contemplated or the precise role Howard-Taylor allegedly played.

Those matters remain subject to further evidence and examination by both the prosecution and defense.

Wilson said the alleged operation continued during the Weah administration and that investigators expanded their inquiry after some of the individuals involved returned to the region.

Foundation Mentioned in Testimony

The court also heard testimony concerning an alleged connection between some of the individuals under investigation and the Jewel Starfish Foundation, an organization associated with Howard-Taylor.

Wilson said one of the participants mentioned that Howard-Taylor operated the foundation.

The witness further testified that an individual identified as Nicholas expressed willingness to assist with the foundation.

The prosecution is presenting the alleged connection as part of the broader relationship it says existed between political figures and individuals under investigation.

US$45,000 Allegedly Delivered

Wilson also testified about an alleged cash delivery during one of the meetings.

According to the witness, a shopping bag was handed over during the meeting, and investigators later received information that approximately US$45,000 had been placed inside the bag.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged payment, including its intended recipient, purpose and connection to the alleged drug-trafficking operation, remain issues for the court to determine.

Investigation Continued After Weah Presidency

Wilson told the court that the investigation continued after the conclusion of the Weah administration in 2024.

He said investigators later determined that some of the individuals under investigation had returned to the region in 2025, prompting further investigative activity.

According to the witness, intelligence officers subsequently identified additional individuals allegedly connected to the investigation.

Wilson maintained that the investigation relied on intelligence gathering, recorded meetings and information obtained during the probe.

The testimony places several issues before the court, including the alleged cocaine-trafficking operation, claims of political protection, financial transactions and an alleged plan targeting the former Weah administration.

However, the allegations remain matters to be tested through evidence and cross-examination.

Howard-Taylor’s alleged involvement has not been established merely by Wilson’s testimony. She remains entitled to the presumption of innocence unless and until a competent court determines otherwise.

The defense is expected to challenge aspects of the investigation, including the credibility and interpretation of the witness’s account, the alleged recordings, meetings, financial transactions and claims concerning the political plan.

The court will ultimately determine whether the prosecution has produced sufficient admissible and credible evidence to establish the charges against Howard-Taylor and the other defendants.

World.title: SADC Troika Considers Zambia’s Post-Electoral Crisis
World.content:
SADC Troika Considers Zambia’s Post-Electoral Crisis

The Southern African Development Community’s security organ is preparing to take up Zambia’s post-election crisis, after receiving a preliminary report from its election observer mission.

King Mswati III of Eswatini, who took over the chairmanship of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation Troika last month, is expected to convene member states to consider the situation. Zambia’s main opposition leader remains in jail, and a former Cabinet minister is dead following a military raid conducted during the vote count.

Zambia held its general election on August 13. Voting passed off peacefully, but the aftermath brought allegations of vote manipulation and result tampering, including claims that the Zambia Army was deployed inside counting centres and that results were altered under military supervision.

On August 14, a military raid on the Lusaka home of opposition leader Brian Mundubile left former Minister of Transport and Communications Mutotwe Kafwaya dead. Several of Mundubile’s colleagues were arrested in the same operation, among them UNIP president and former Botswana bishop Trevor Mwamba, and former Law Association of Zambia president George Chisanga.

Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, took refuge inside the United Nations building in Lusaka after the raid. UN Secretary-General António Guterres sent a Special Envoy from New York to negotiate a resolution.

The UN sought safe passage for the two men, or their transfer to a third-party embassy in Lusaka. President Hakainde Hichilema rejected both options, demanding they surrender to police, who were investigating alleged security breaches and claims that the opposition had formed a militia.

Five days after the raid, Secretary to Cabinet Patrick Kangwa confirmed Kafwaya’s death. He said Mundubile had formed a militia intending to seize power illegally.

Mundubile and Zulu were handed over on August 27 to the Eight Church Mother Bodies at the Anglican Cathedral of the Holy Cross in Lusaka, who surrendered them to police. Both now face treason charges and are held at Mukobeko Maximum Correctional Facility in Kabwe, roughly 200km from Lusaka, awaiting trial.

Soldiers sealed Zambia’s courts during the constitutional window for filing election challenges, blocking Mundubile and civil society groups from lodging a petition through normal channels.

Chief Justice Mumba Malila later disclosed that a petition had reached him regardless, filed by private mail. He named former Law Association of Zambia president Linda Kasonde and civil society leader Brebner Changala as the petitioners. Malila said the filing method was unusual but that he would use his constitutional powers to refer the matter to the Constitutional Court.

The Constitution requires election challenges to be resolved before a new president is inaugurated. Government proceeded with the inauguration regardless. Hichilema was sworn in for a second term on September 1 at National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka, with the Kasonde-Changala petition still before the Constitutional Court.

World.title: From Civil Servant to Stateless: Mukandila’s Citizenship Ordeal
World.content:
A man does not need to lose his freedom and his nationality on the same day, yet that is precisely the position in which incarcerated Lusaka lawyer Celestine Mukandila now finds himself, after the state moved to cancel his National Registration Card and passport while he remains in custody, effectively declaring him stateless at the very moment he is least able to contest it in the ordinary course of civic life.

Mukandila, secretary general of the Tonse Pamodzi Alliance, says he is a Zambian citizen by descent and has challenged the cancellation of his documents, arguing that citizenship cannot be revoked through administrative action without following the law.

His position rests on a specific constitutional provision. Mukandila says he acquired Zambian citizenship at birth through his mother, who was a Zambian citizen at the time of his birth in 1990 in Lubumbashi, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. He explained that his mother was Ushi by origin, from Matanda Village in Mansa, Luapula Province, and that his maternal family had deep roots in the province.

Being born outside Zambia did not, in his account, make him a foreigner, because Article 36 of the Constitution provides for citizenship by descent where, at the time of birth, at least one parent was a Zambian citizen by birth or descent.

“My position is therefore straightforward: I acquired Zambian citizenship by descent at birth through my Zambian mother. I did not apply to become Zambian as an adult, nor did I obtain my citizenship through naturalisation,” Mukandila said.

He said he was approximately 16 years old when he became eligible for national registration, and therefore could not be personally held responsible for any alleged irregularities surrounding the acquisition of his NRC, since he was still a minor navigating a process his family, not he alone, would have managed.

“If the State alleges that fraud was committed in the acquisition of my NRC, then it must identify the alleged fraudulent representation, identify who made it, and establish who had the legal responsibility for making the relevant declarations at the time,” Mukandila said.

He said his family returned to Zambia in 1999, although his mother continued spending periods in the DRC because of her employment. Mukandila also questioned why his nationality was only being challenged now, when he had previously served as a civil servant and had undergone State verification processes without issue.

“The National Registration authorities themselves have previously recognised me and issued me with national documentation,” he said.

He has also demanded that authorities explain the legal basis for cancelling his NRC and passport, including identifying the alleged fraud, the authority that made the decision, and the procedure followed before the cancellation was carried out.

Mukandila said a Gazette notice could not substitute the law, arguing that public officers must exercise statutory power within the limits prescribed by law.

He said the matter was bigger than him personally, because citizenship should not be used as a political weapon against citizens holding views different from those in government.

“I demand only what every citizen is entitled to demand. Let the law be followed. Let the evidence be produced. Let due process be respected. And let the rule of law prevail over political expediency,” Mukandila said.

The case adds to a growing list of disputes in which opposition-aligned figures have found their legal standing, whether through citizenship, bail, or access to counsel, challenged through administrative or security channels rather than tested first through ordinary judicial process, a pattern that has drawn concern from legal commentators and civil society figures in the weeks following the general election.
