World.title: Experiment: How easy is it to buy a research paper on the black market?
World.content:
Paper mills are making it easier than ever for researchers to buy authorship of bogus academic papers, fueling concerns that mounting pressure to publish is undermining research integrity.

In today's world of research, publications are the main currency. Amid fierce academic competition, a researcher's salary, position and entire future career depend on the number and success of their published papers. But the constant pressure to publish an ever-growing number of influential research papers has created the perfect environment for a murky business.

This has given rise to a black market flourishing primarily on social media where so-called paper mills operate. Rather than conducting actual research, they mass-produce texts designed to appear credible. For a moderate fee, researchers can buy authorship of such a bogus paper to boost their standing in academic databases. Those selling academic fraud also do everything they can to ensure the paper is actually published in an established academic journal.

To find out just how easy it is to buy authorship of a research paper, we conducted a journalistic experiment and contacted a handful of paper mills.

Let it be said that ERR's editorial team does not advocate using the services of paper mills. Paper mills are fraudulent operations that are wholly at odds with the principles of research ethics and using their services can, in the worst case, result in criminal penalties. Our sole aim was to demonstrate just how absurdly easy it is to get in touch with a paper mill.

A scientist in 20 days and for $800

Paper mills openly market their services on social media. In Facebook communities with seemingly innocuous names such as "Free Scopus publication and research help," various services are advertised using information-packed, AI-generated posters. On the surface, they appear to offer consulting services, but in reality, it is clear they are advertising something else.

We collected contact details for seven of the most active sellers in the groups and messaged them directly on WhatsApp, as instructed in the ads. In the exchanges, we posed as a fictional computer scientist named John Robert Steezy and asked directly about the possibility of buying authorship of a research paper.

Screenshot of a message sent to paper mills. Source: ERR

We did not have to wait long for help. Of the seven contacts, most of whom had Indian names, five responded within the next half-hour, with WhatsApp notifications constantly lighting up the phone screen.

The offers varied widely. The most expensive paper cost $800 and would have been published in a journal titled the Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science. According to the seller, publication would have taken just 20 days. Compared with a conventional research paper, which can take months to undergo peer review and editing, this was a ridiculously short period.

The cheapest offer, meanwhile, was just $200, for which the computer scientist was offered co-authorship of a paper in a fisheries journal. Aside from a couple of stranger offers, the paper mills were fairly consistent in quality. At first glance, all the sample papers looked like genuine research papers and only closer examination revealed that some of the figures were illogical or the references arbitrary.

Within the first half-hour, the fictitious researcher's WhatsApp account created by the newsroom received more than 20 papers offering authorship for between $200 and $800. Screenshot of WhatsApp notifications. Source: ERR

The paper mills' customer service was no less polished. We managed to speak with one seller by phone and a man with an Indian accent explained the publication process and pricing in fluent English. Notably, this particular seller required payment only after the journal's editors had accepted the paper.

Within a few hours, every conversation had reached the point where a single email would have been enough to send the paper off to journals under the fictitious researcher's name. To avoid burdening the research world with even more junk, however, we ended the conversations there. The relentless salespeople continued bombarding the newsroom with WhatsApp messages for days afterward.

Stolen research

Where do paper mills get the seemingly genuine material they sell? This is where an arguably even more dishonest side of this dirty business comes into play: stealing the work of real researchers.

While, as might be expected today, some of the papers offered for sale are generated using artificial intelligence, the information often comes from previously published research. In such cases, paper mills select lesser-known or foreign-language papers, run them through machine translation and alter the wording, tables and graphs to evade plagiarism detection. The aim is to make the paper look genuine at first glance.

That appears to be exactly what happened to Lauri Laanisto, a tenure-track professor of macroecology at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, who discovered last spring that an attempt had been made to republish a study he had worked on in a slightly altered form and under someone else's name. Laanisto first described what happened on his blog.

"It was a lucky coincidence," Laanisto recalled. "Just a couple of months earlier, I had attended a joint meeting in Poland with the editor-in-chief of a journal where I presented those same results and figures. So we were simply lucky that, as editor-in-chief, he happened to scroll through this resubmitted manuscript and noticed that everything looked suspiciously similar," he said.

According to Laanisto, it was an unequivocal case of plagiarism: The title and wording had been changed and a color figure converted to black and white, but the substance of the study remained the same. The paper listed as its author a person purportedly affiliated with a Chinese university, but that person could not be found on the university's website or in academic databases.

Laanisto said the perpetrator's ultimate goal may not even have been to get the paper published. "Perhaps it was a doctoral student who needed to show their supervisor that they had submitted a manuscript somewhere by a certain deadline in order to pass an evaluation. Simply submitting the paper may have been enough," he said.

It could also have been a researcher under pressure who was trying to keep their job. "There are a lot of researchers, competition for funding is fierce and the requirements for keeping an academic position are becoming increasingly demanding. Using paper mills may be the easiest way to build up academic credit. Just as the number of votes is a form of currency for politicians in an election, the equivalent for researchers is the number of papers they have published or their overall body of published research," Laanisto added.

But how do fraudsters get around peer review? As a cornerstone of the modern research system, peer review is supposed to ensure that independent experts scrutinize a study before it is published. Paper mills have their own tricks for circumventing the process.

The most brazen method involves fake peer reviewers. A paper mill recommends fictitious researchers to a journal as potential reviewers, providing email addresses that route the publisher's messages directly to the mill's employees. They then use fake accounts to approve their own work. Another method is to bribe journal editors or create an entire sham journal themselves.

An extensive analysis published in the journal PNAS found nearly 30,000 suspicious paper mill articles in the academic databases examined. Worse still, researchers estimate that around 75 percent of this junk will remain in academic databases permanently. That means future studies or even medical treatment guidelines could end up being based on completely false information.

Mounting pressure to publish

According to Lauri Laanisto, selling co-authorship is nothing new in research, with such fraud having existed for at least 20 years. What has changed, however, is the scale and accessibility of the business. In the past, co-authorship slots were sold during a narrow window after a genuine paper had passed its first round of peer review but before it was published. "But the experiment showed that now the store is essentially open 24/7 — things have changed," he added.

Laanisto pointed to the root of the problem: ever-increasing pressure to publish. "You can be a good researcher, but if you don't publish enough, you aren't successful. At the same time, we've reached a point where you can be a successful researcher without necessarily being a real researcher," he said.

Researchers' working environment has changed dramatically over time. "When I started my master's degree, my supervisor told me that an ecologist's year went like this: You plan an experiment in the spring, carry it out in the summer, analyze the data come fall, write up the paper in the winter and start again in the spring. That gives you one paper a year," Laanisto said.

Today, however, competition is so intense that, for example, an ecologist who publishes fewer than 10 papers a year can no longer maintain a sufficiently high profile, he said. Such pressure inevitably affects the quality of research. "It's obvious that if you've always published one paper a year, you don't suddenly jump to a level where you have 10 times as much new knowledge or 10 times as many results. That can clearly only come from spreading the substance more thinly across papers," Laanisto said.

At the same time, Laanisto noted that while pressure to publish is also a problem for researchers in Estonia, he is not aware of any researchers in the country who use paper mill services. For now, such fraud is predominantly associated with countries that offer state-funded bonuses for published papers, such as China.

Laanisto said pressure to publish could be reduced by placing greater value on qualitative skills in assessing researchers' work, such as good teaching. "Within universities, they probably know better how to distribute that money among people who are actually doing something, such as those who do a good job supervising bachelor's students." In his view, this would ease the pressure created by evaluating researchers solely on the number of their publications.

When it comes to curbing the paper mills' murky business, however, Laanisto believes the most sensible approach would be to impose real consequences for breaches of research ethics. "If you're caught, for example, buying from a paper mill, duplicating data or publishing stolen results, there generally isn't any kind of formal punishment," Laanisto said, describing a situation in which a researcher caught engaging in misconduct can often simply move to another university.

"But if getting caught resulted in an official ban on receiving research funding, that would make people less willing to risk committing fraud," Laanisto said.

World.title: Lavly Perling: Let's not live in dreams
World.content:
The lives of Estonian people will not be improved by Kristen Michal's sugar‑coating nor by Urmas Reinsalu's populism, writes Lavly Perling.

Parliamentary parties are living in their own dreams. The Reform Party dreams that everything is fine with the economy and that no more decisions need to be made. Isamaa and the Center Party, however, hope to escape responsibility.

Such political games only harm the Estonian state. Bold reforms are postponed, and the debt we pass on to our children grows by more than a hundred million euros every month.

The situation is not improved by the fact that the Reform Party government recently transferred 70 million euros of national defense money to an Indian company with a dubious background, now mocked by the biggest Putin trolls on social media. In addition to the Reform Party's failure to balance the budget, the honest use of Estonia's defense funds and our international defense reputation have been called into question. It is simply embarrassing. The Reform Party is no longer reliable in national defense or public finances.

This is precisely why the board of Parempoolsed has proposed to the Reform Party board that Kristen Michal — who absolutely does not grasp political responsibility — be recalled from the prime minister's seat and replaced until the elections with an interim prime minister whose task would be to stop the budget that is steering us toward bankruptcy and to lead the country to the elections without additional scandals.

Why do we think so, besides the mess created in national defense?

The private sector does not believe in Estonia

Yes, Estonia's economy cannot be viewed only in dark tones. Since Sweden and Finland have begun to do better, we have benefited as well. The economy is cyclical, and every downturn is followed at some point by an upswing. We are seeing that now: in the previous quarter, the economy grew by 1.8 percent.

But let's not be fooled by the prime minister's sugar‑coated talk about how everything is fine, even though investments continue to bypass us, people's confidence is low, and most employers see the biggest future risk as an unpredictable economic and tax environment.

"The Reform Party is no longer reliable in national defense or public finances."

Moreover, if the prime minister truly believes that things are now good, then the question arises: why have you not used this growth in a statesmanlike manner to fix public finances? The reality is that we are far from the kind of economic growth that would improve people's standard of living — growth that is stable, long‑term, and faster than that of our neighbors.

Current economic growth is fragile. Especially when you look inside the numbers. Our growth is based on large state investments. As the Ministry of Finance's economic forecast pointed out, public‑sector investments are at a historic peak. The private sector last invested such a small share of GDP in Estonia during the recession at the end of the first decade of the century. And the situation is not improving — the economic forecast does not foresee growth in business investments.

State expenditures keep growing, and the government neither knows nor wants to apply brakes. This increases and prolongs the period of uncertainty. Entrepreneurs do not want to invest in Estonia because they are rational. They understand that a yeast‑like swelling national debt will eventually bring tax increases that will sink their plans again.

For foreign investment to return, the government must acknowledge its mistakes. We cannot change the geopolitical situation ourselves, but we can and must start fixing our public finances here, by ourselves, and immediately. Right now, the statesmanlike thing would be to focus on the state budget and steer it toward balance. Only then do we restore investment confidence, which will eventually bring better jobs, wage growth, and improved living standards for Estonians.

This is also pointed out in the fresh employers' manifesto. Public‑sector overspending is not sustainable — it artificially inflates economic growth, but at some point the myth collapses, because real prosperity is created only by the private sector.

Let's not be fooled by statistical adjustments

What does not help us? Claims that the past few years have not actually been so bad because statistics have been adjusted. This is simply a political talking point, because such adjustments are routine and have no real impact on the economy.

Everyone has felt the decline in purchasing power, rising prices, climbing inflation, and the taking away of earned money through constant tax increases. These feelings, perceptions, and experiences have been real for people — statistical adjustments do not make anyone's life better.

In reality, state expenditures are still growing, there is no plan to ease the debt burden, and by 2027 interest costs may reach 320 million euros — 0.7 percent of GDP. As large as the amount Estonia gives each year to our national culture.

This shows that current state leaders continue living at the expense of the future. Yet this is exactly what we must stop if we want a better Estonia for future generations and confidence and hope for a brighter future for Estonian people.

All parliamentary parties share responsibility for the disorder in public finances, because it has lasted longer than the current coalition. At the same time, instead of focusing on the past, it is important to focus on the future and seek solutions there. This is how the opposition should think as well, if they had a sense of responsibility and statesmanship.

Reinsalu and Kõlvart offer only populism

The leader of the largest opposition party, instead of focusing on the state budget, proposes a plan for extraordinary elections — something belonging to the realm of utopia. Extraordinary elections are neither possible nor necessary.

"All parliamentary parties share responsibility for the disorder in public finances."

Of course, the leaders of Isamaa and the Center Party know this, but since Reform Party chairman Kristen Michal and Isamaa chairman Urmas Reinsalu are competing for the title of best political gamer, the fairy tale of extraordinary elections serves nicely as a smokescreen to hide the fear of Isamaa and the Center Party — who have tied themselves together neatly in the capital — that the government might actually fall and they would have to govern themselves. Then their myth of raising benefits while lowering taxes would collapse.

Until now, the fairy tale of extraordinary elections has mostly been told to voters by the Helme family leading EKRE, who are used to living in a parallel reality. It is very strange why opposition leader Reinsalu has fallen for the same trick. By going along with such ridiculous populism, he harms the entire opposition and makes the Reform Party's election campaign easier.

A large part of Estonians reasonably want a change of government and the Reform Party sent to the waiting bench, but many of these people also want a return to sensible politics and avoidance of populism. Reinsalu and Centre Party chairman Mihhail Kõlvart, however, have decided to offer populism and unrealistic substitute activities.

Let's start deciding

The statesmanlike thing would be to resist the temptation to extort promises from a minority government through deals and instead help compile a responsible state budget. I admit this is difficult, and even with the best effort it may not succeed.

Therefore, the other alternative is not to allow the adoption of an irresponsible budget and to enter the next year without a state budget, using the constitutional option that in the first months one may spend as much as at the beginning of 2026. In March, a new government can adopt a budget that moves toward balance.

What would help us now is a decision to freeze state expenditures at the 2026 level. After that, we can discuss starting tax cuts that stimulate the economy. This would restore confidence for entrepreneurs and give people hope for a better future.

True, even these two steps are not enough, because they only illustrate the general path. How do we move the budget toward balance? Very simple: we must start reforms in the education, social, and healthcare systems to detach ourselves from the outdated welfare‑state model, giving people back the freedom and responsibility to make more choices themselves and giving the private sector greater opportunities to operate in these fields.

Education must be tied to the labor market. In healthcare, the availability of medical care must be maintained under the conditions of an aging and shrinking population through greater co‑payment and broader involvement of the private sector.

Reducing bureaucracy and administrative burden must happen in deeds, not words as before. We also need modernization of labor relations, because they inevitably rely more on flexibility and mutual agreements, where trade unions, as historical phenomena, should no longer have a role.

These are the steps that help change the direction of the state and lead us toward a free and prosperous Estonia. Therefore, I recommend that state leaders not engage in substitute activities during the last half‑year before the elections, but rather find the statesmanship within themselves and make at least some difficult decisions for a better future.

World.title: Being transferred from one hospital to another restarts inpatient fee count
World.content:
Under Estonian law, a hospital may charge a patient an inpatient fee for a maximum of 10 days per case. However, if the patient is transferred from one hospital to another, the 10-day period starts over.

The Health Insurance Act states that an insured patient may be charged an inpatient fee for a hospital stay, but for no more than 10 calendar days per case.

In practice, however, a concern has arisen when a patient is initially treated at one hospital but is then transferred to another to continue treatment, for example to a hospital closer to home. Even though the patient's health issue remains the same, the second hospital may start charging the inpatient fee again for up to 10 days.

Siiri Lahe, chair of the Health Insurance Fund's management board, therefore contacted Social Affairs Minister Karmen Joller, pointing out that the meaning of a single case or course of treatment differs from the perspective of hospitals and patients. Hospitals also have no system for tracking or exchanging information on whether and how much a patient paid in inpatient fees at the previous hospital.

"Each hospital uses its own information system and information about inpatient fees is not transferred to the nationwide digital health record," Lahe said.

She compared this with specialist doctor appointment fees where the law does not allow another fee to be charged for a follow-up appointment for the same service. Against that background, she noted, charging inpatient fees again can strike patients as unfair and cause confusion.

The Health Insurance Fund chief asked the Ministry of Social Affairs for its position on whether the term "single case" means, for the purposes of the law, only the period spent at the same hospital. She also pointed out that, to the Health Insurance Fund's knowledge, Estonian law contains no separate definition of the term "case."

Heli Paluste, a healthcare network expert at the Ministry of Social Affairs, told ERR that from the patient's perspective, it is indeed a single course of treatment and having to pay another inpatient fee when moving between hospitals can raise questions.

"Unlike appointment fees, for which the law sets out specific exemptions governing when a patient moving between institutions may not be charged another appointment fee, no similar exemption applying across hospitals has been established for inpatient fees. Hospitals are independent institutions and when a patient is transferred and admitted to another hospital, that hospital considers it a new case," Paluste said.

She added that the Health Insurance Fund likewise treats and funds such cases as separate hospital-specific courses of treatment under its contracts with hospitals.

According to the Ministry of Social Affairs expert, the Health Insurance Fund's observation is entirely understandable from the patient's perspective.

"Since the current Health Insurance Act does not explicitly define a case across hospitals, it will probably be necessary to discuss separately with hospitals and the Health Insurance Fund whether the rules and practices governing inpatient fees need to be clarified to ensure that patients' cost-sharing is calculated clearly and fairly," Paluste said.

World.title: Dog Pennu finds a home after 1,497 days in Tartu shelter
World.content:
This spring, the dog Pennu, who had lived for more than four years at the Tartu shelter for homeless animals, found his real home.

"Just like with people, some simply don't get lucky in life — the right one just doesn't come," shelter director Annika Mölder said, explaining why Pennu spent so many years waiting for a home.

In the end, he was taken home by shelter volunteer Elisabeth Kaldvee. Kaldvee has been a volunteer at the shelter for seven years, but with Pennu it was not love at first sight at all. At first, her heart was won by the dog boy living next to Pennu.

"Pennu kept jumping like a bat onto the fence and waited for scratches under the arm. Then I just tossed treats to him, but didn't pay much attention. He wasn't my main dog to work with. I went walking with him for the first time about three years ago," Kaldvee recalled.

Dog arrived after bite incident

Pennu arrived at the shelter from a home where he had bitten another dog and a child. "Right now it seems impossible," said Mölder. "The situation was probably such that the child was with the dog, and the dogs got into a conflict with each other, and maybe the child ended up in between. The owner then decided that he did not want to keep such an aggressive dog — too big a responsibility, which is also true."

Kaldvee recalled that when Pennu arrived at the shelter, it was clear that not much work had been done with him, because he had no habit of walking on a leash, he didn't know tricks, and contact with people was minimal. He was also very reactive toward other dogs. "A lot of work and training has been done."

Kaldvee has loved dogs her whole life. As a child, she constantly asked her parents to get her a dog, but it never happened. Now she sees that her parents acted correctly, because at that time it wasn't the right moment and she didn't know enough about dogs.

Volunteer becomes owner

"But the interest has always been there. A classmate invited me to the shelter when I was 18. We went together. For her it was the last time, I kept going. Especially when you choose one dog there to focus on, it's a bit like cheating, because you start feeling like you have your own dog," Kaldvee smiled.

Becoming attached to an animal waiting for a home at the shelter can also bring great heartbreak.

"I always like to say that my first heartbreak was at the shelter, when the first dog I seriously fell in love with was adopted. His name is Bruno. I mourned him for three months and took a break from the shelter. It's a bittersweet moment, because you're happy, but on the other hand he was a dog I invested so much in. It's hard to accept that he's no longer at the shelter," Kaldvee admitted.

Years of attachment grow

Why no one wanted Pennu, Kaldvee has thought about for years. At one point she even began to hope a little that no one would take Pennu, so she could adopt him herself at the right moment.

"He is such a cool‑natured dog. He is super friendly," the owner praised. "He is the first shelter dog I have seriously trained. It was a bit sad to think that all the work I had done would go to waste and I'd have to start from scratch with another dog. And also, when you work with a dog for three years straight, you grow together. He became my dog some time ago already. The shelter workers had long been asking when I would take Pennu home."

Pennu has accepted his new home very well.

Kaldvee encourages others to adopt older dogs too, because then you don't have to worry about puppy‑like mischief. "Once they get used to the home environment, they practically sleep the whole day."

World.title: Al Zaidi rejects dragging Iraq into U.S. sanctions against Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s governing State Administration Coalition convened its 38th regular session at the Government Palace on Sunday, September 6, 2026, issuing a strong warning on the necessity of insulating Iraq from the repercussions of U.S. sanctions imposed on regional states, emphasizing that the country’s tight fiscal situation leaves zero margin for geopolitical risk.

During the meeting, Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi announced an immediate moratorium on the demolition of informal settlements until the distribution of the sovereign one-million residential plot initiative is completed. The premier also confirmed the imminent release of a fresh liquidity tranche to clear long-standing state arrears owed to local farmers and private contracting firms.

Key Outcomes & Policy Directives

Insulating Against Regional Sanctions: The coalition explicitly stressed shielding Iraq from secondary impacts of Washington’s sanctions targeting regional neighbors (chiefly Iran). Political leaders warned that ongoing liquidity shortages and mounting fiscal pressures mean Iraq cannot endure financial isolation or retaliatory banking measures.

Moratorium on Slum Demolitions: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi ordered municipal authorities to halt all eviction and demolition campaigns targeting informal housing until eligible, propertyless families receive deeds under the one-million serviced plot program.

Liquidity Injections for Farmers & Contractors: A new sovereign funding disbursement will be released shortly to settle dues for domestic grain producers and infrastructure contractors, easing liquidity bottlenecks across the real economy.

Oil & Gas Draft Law Progress: The coalition reviewed an updated draft of the federal Oil and Gas Law, finalizing consensus terms before its formal transmission to the Council of Representatives (parliament).

Cabinet Completion Dialogues: Political blocs agreed to launch direct negotiations next week to fill remaining vacant ministerial portfolios.

Anti-Corruption & Institutional Reform: Leaders reaffirmed unanimous political backing for Al-Zaidi’s anti-graft drive and judicial referrals, while reviewing the draft Federal Internal Oversight Authority Law.

Major Policy Decisions at the 38th Coalition Meeting

Policy File Direct Executive Action Strategic Significance Regional Geopolitics & Sanctions Strict neutrality; protecting banking and oil flows from U.S. sanctions Preserves dollar-clearing access and safeguards fragile financial stability. Housing & Informal Settlements Halt on property demolitions pending plot allocation Prevents social displacement; aligns urban clearance with the 1M land initiative. Public Dues & Arrears Imminent payment tranche for farmers and commercial contractors Injects state liquidity directly into the agricultural and construction sectors. Hydrocarbon Legislation Finalizing the Federal Oil & Gas Law draft Creates a binding statutory formula between Baghdad, Erbil, and producing provinces. Government Formation Dialogues with entitled parliamentary blocs begin next week Resolves vacant cabinet seats to strengthen executive decision-making. Institutional Accountability Advancing the Federal Internal Oversight Authority bill Reinforces internal audit mechanics across ministries and state-owned banks.

The coalition’s explicit warning regarding U.S. sanctions highlights heightened sensitivity within Baghdad’s ruling elite over banking compliance, correspondent account access, and external financial exposure.

With public debt climbing and mandatory spending on civil salaries and social programs averaging over 7.4 trillion IQD per month, preserving open financial channels with Western institutions is viewed by the coalition as an essential safeguard for national economic solvency.

World.title: Integrity probes liquidity drain and 1B+ dinar loans at Rafidain and Rasheed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Federal Commission of Integrity and specialized judicial oversight bodies have launched a comprehensive financial audit and investigative probe into liquidity depletion, high-value commercial loans, and discretionary financing waivers across Iraq’s state-owned banking sector on Saturday, September 5, 2026.

The investigation centers on operational practices at Rafidain Bank and Rasheed Bank—the country’s two dominant state lenders—examining major credit facilities exceeding 1 billion IQD (approximately $763,000) granted through non-standard channels or exceptional exemptions.

According to sources close to the regulatory authorities, forensic teams are cross-referencing credit files against statutory central bank lending guidelines to determine civil and administrative culpability:

High-Value Credit Facilities:Scrutinizing loans and investment financing packages valued from 1 billion IQD upward, assessing whether underwriting criteria and collateral coverage adhered to regulatory standards.

Beneficiary Audits:Examining corporate structures, political affiliations, and corporate vehicles granted special exemptions, verifying whether funds were directed toward actual commercial assets or converted into speculative cash holdings.

Historical Policy Tracing: Multiple files under scrutiny date back to policies and executive administrative approvals issued under the previous cabinet and Ministry of Finance administration.

Misleading Administrative Disclosures: Following up on reports from late August indicating that some bank boards submitted inaccurate or misleading liquidity statements to senior government leadership amid delays in civil service payroll allocations.

Core Areas of the Banking Investigation

Audit Focus Investigation Target Regulatory Objective Credit Packages ≥ 1B IQD Commercial facilities, corporate overdrafts, and project finance Confirm collateral solvency and compliance with statutory lending ceilings. Special Clearances Ministerial waivers and board-level discretionary exemptions Identify irregular approvals granted outside standard central bank risk frameworks. World.title: Iraq achieves wheat and date self-sufficiency for 2026: Agriculture Ministry
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture announced on Friday, September 4, 2026, that Iraq has achieved full self-sufficiency in its strategic wheat harvest for the third consecutive season, while also securing complete domestic self-sufficiency in date production.

Ministry Spokesperson Qusay Al-Hattab stated that targeted state interventions—combining climate-resilient crop genetics, subsidized modern sprinkler systems, and a data-backed agricultural calendar—have decoupled key food staples from volatile international import markets.

Core Pillars of Agricultural Self-Sufficiency

Three Consecutive Seasons of Wheat Sufficiency: The 2026 winter harvest solidified a three-year streak of domestic grain self-reliance, with the ministry already preparing its winter crop plan to maintain full coverage into 2027.

Climate-Adaptive Seed Cultivars: Agricultural research divisions successfully introduced proprietary wheat seed strains engineered to withstand high soil salinity, prolonged drought, and extreme climatic volatility.

Subsidized Irrigation Upgrades (Austrian Loan Facility): To combat persistent water scarcity across the Tigris and Euphrates basins, modern pivot and localized sprinkler systems are distributed under a 33% state subsidy. Pivot systems valued at 70 million IQD are provided to registered farmers for 49 million IQD, financed through a 10-year installment plan with a one-year grace period.

Date Palm Sector Expansion: Iraq’s date palm population expanded from roughly 12 million trees in 2003 to 22 million trees in 2026, driven by replanting campaigns and commercial orchard developments, with Zahdi dates comprising the largest share of national yield.

Agricultural Policy Framework: Modernization and Trade Protections

World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: 19 lakh lives impacted as Ganga breaches flood mark in Patna
World.content:
NEW DELHI: More than 19.57 lakh people have been affected by floods across 11 districts of Bihar as of Sunday, with authorities putting downstream areas on high alert. This comes after the Ganga, following heavy rain, crossed its previous highest flood level at Gandhi Ghat in Patna.

The Ganga was flowing at 50.57 metres at Gandhi Ghat at 6am on Sunday, 0.05 metres above its previous highest flood level (HFL) of 50.52 metres recorded on August 21, 2016. While the trend was stable at Gandhi Ghat, authorities warned that Hathidah and subsequent gauge stations could be affected over the next one to three days.

The rising water levels have prompted heightened vigilance across several downstream districts, with officials monitoring river levels, embankments, vulnerable locations and low-lying areas and keeping rescue machinery ready.

19.57 lakh people affected across 11 districts

According to officials, flooding has affected around 19.57 lakh people in 330 gram panchayats across Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar and Araria.

The latest figures indicate a worsening impact compared with earlier assessments, when around 16.85 lakh people across 61 blocks and 300 gram panchayats had been reported affected.

With several rivers continuing to flow above danger levels, authorities have intensified relief and rescue operations in the affected districts.





The Water Resources Department has warned that the Ganga at Hathidah may also cross its previous HFL, increasing the risk for Begusarai, Lakhisarai, Munger, Bhagalpur and Katihar.

âOfficials and field-level authorities have been directed to remain alert and continuously monitor water levels, embankments, vulnerable locations and low-lying areas, while taking precautionary measures as required.

âEngineers have been asked to keep flood-control resources and machinery ready.

People in affected areas have been advised to avoid going near the river and remain cautious,â the advisory stated.

Local administrations have also been asked to keep a close watch on boat operations, prevent overloading and ensure residents receive regular updates about the flood situation.

Ganga breaches danger levels at several locations

The Ganga is above the danger mark at several locations in Bihar.

At Buxar, the river was 0.08 metres above the danger mark, although its level was declining.

At Dighaghat in Patna, it was 1.54 metres above the danger mark, while at Gandhi Ghat it stood 1.96 metres above it.

At Hathidah, the Ganga was 1.74 metres above the danger mark and continued to rise. Munger recorded a level 0.51 metres above the danger mark, with the river showing a rising trend.

The river was also 2.01 metres above the danger mark at Sultanganj and 0.65 metres above it at Bhagalpur. The Ganga remained above the danger mark at Kahalgaon as well.

At Pandarak in Patna, the river was flowing at 43.92 metres at 6 am, 0.19 metres above its previous HFL of 43.73 metres recorded on August 16, 2021.

In contrast, the Ganga remained below the warning level in Prayagraj and Varanasi. Its level was rising in Prayagraj but declining in Varanasi.

Several rivers remain above danger levels

The flood threat is not confined to the Ganga. Several other rivers in Bihar are also flowing above their respective danger levels.

The Gandak is above the danger mark at Dumariaghat and Hajipur, while the Kosi has crossed the mark at Baltara and Kursela. The Budhi Gandak is above the danger level at Khagaria.

The Punpun is above the danger mark at Sripalpur, while the Bagmati has crossed it at Benibad. The Ghaghra is also flowing above the danger level at Darauli.

The combination of rising river levels and further rainfall has kept authorities on alert, particularly in downstream and low-lying areas.

Relief operations expanded across flood-hit districts

The administration has deployed significant resources to assist people affected by the floods.

A total of 110 community kitchens are currently operating in various districts to provide food to affected residents. Earlier official figures had put the number of operational community kitchens at 80, with around 1.21 lakh people receiving meals through them.

One relief camp is also operational, providing accommodation, food, medical assistance and other essential facilities to 326 flood-affected people.

Authorities have distributed around 45,900 polythene sheets and 11,700 dry ration packets as part of relief efforts.

Boats are being used extensively to evacuate residents and maintain movement in areas affected by rising waters. The latest deployment stands at 1,345 boats across the state, compared with 1,158 reported earlier.

SDRF, NDRF teams deployed

With the possibility of further flooding, 27 State Disaster Response Force teams and 10 National Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed across different districts.

The teams have been tasked with undertaking rapid relief and rescue operations, while district administrations continue to monitor vulnerable areas and river embankments.

Officials have also been instructed to ensure that flood-control equipment and machinery remain ready for deployment as required.

Rain forecast raises concern over further rise

The flood situation could remain challenging over the coming days as the Bihar Meteorological Service Centre has forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places across the state over the next two days.

Heavy rainfall is also possible at some locations.

Authorities are therefore preparing for the possibility of further increases in river levels, particularly in areas already affected by flooding. The state government and district administrations are continuing to monitor the situation and deploy relief materials, boats and rescue teams according to local requirements.

Rail services affected on Patna-Gaya section

The flooding has also disrupted railway operations in parts of the state.

The East Central Railway said on Sunday that some trains had been cancelled or diverted because of the âalarmingly high water level at bridge number 21" connecting Punpun and Parsa Bazar stations on the Patna-Gaya section.

The development adds to the disruption caused by rising waters as authorities continue to focus on evacuation, relief and the safety of residents in flood-affected areas.

Barrage discharge levels

Barrage discharge data recorded at 9 am on Sunday showed that the Sone Barrage at Indrapuri was releasing 2,27,739 cusecs of water, although the flow was declining.

The Kosi Barrage at Birpur was releasing 1,68,400 cusecs, with the discharge remaining stable. The Gandak Barrage at Valmikinagar was releasing 1,29,000 cusecs, also with a stable trend.

With multiple rivers remaining above danger levels, further rainfall forecast over the next two days and the Ganga already having crossed its previous HFL at Gandhi Ghat, authorities have urged residents in vulnerable areas to remain cautious and avoid approaching swollen rivers.

World.title: 'Contributed to population control': Former CEC Quraishi says EC 'eliminated' 15 cr voters through SIR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Chief Election Commissioner SY Quraishi on Sunday criticised the Election Commission over its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, claiming that the exercise had effectively removed around 14-15 crore people from the country's voter lists.

Speaking to news agency ANI, Quraishi urged the poll panel to disclose the number of voters deleted, describing the exercise as a "great success" in achieving something the National Population Commission could not.

"I would like to compliment the Election Commission for completing a very difficult mission of eliminating about 14-15 crore population of India through this exercise. I don't know how many illegal immigrants they have found, which was the main purpose of this exercise.

It's a pity they have not disclosed this figure," Quraishi said.

"I would request them to please come out with this figure, so that we know what a great success you have been, and also that you have achieved something that the National Population Commission could not do. You have contributed a lot to population control by eliminating about 15% of India's population," he added.

Quraishi also questioned the intent behind the SIR exercise, arguing that voting is a constitutional right and not something to be granted by the Election Commission.





"I think the entire SIR exercise is not well-intentioned. The way it has deleted crores of voters is tinkering with democracy. You are a citizen of India. I'm a citizen of India. Voting is our constitutional right," he said.

"Article 326 says that everyone shall be registered. So it is not a charity from the Election Commission that they will give you that," he added.

The Election Commission is conducting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in several states to ensure that voter lists are accurate, updated and free of ineligible or duplicate entries, while ensuring that no eligible voter is left out.

The nationwide SIR was announced in October 2025 by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The poll panel cited migration, voters being registered at multiple places, failure to remove deceased voters and the inclusion of foreign nationals in electoral rolls as factors behind the exercise.

World.title: ‘Bye-bye, papa’: What 21-year-old told father before jumping into Chenab
World.content:
NEW DEHI: A 21-year-old woman allegedly jumped into the Chenab River in Doda district on Saturday after speaking to her father over the phone and telling him, "This is my life," before saying, "Bye-bye, papa.

" A joint rescue operation was launched soon after the incident, but there was no immediate trace of her.

The incident took place around 2 pm at the Shiva Dal bridge near Prem Nagar. Police, personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and local volunteers joined the search operation in the river after the woman, identified as Payal Devi, reportedly jumped from the bridge.

A video purportedly recorded by passersby who attempted to discourage her from taking the step shows Devi saying "bye-bye" before jumping into the Chenab.

The video subsequently went viral on social media.

Officials said the circumstances that led to Devi taking the extreme step were not immediately known.

âThis is my own lifeâ

The final conversation between Devi and her father, Krishan Lal, came shortly before she disappeared into the river.

According to Lal, Devi had gone to a mela earlier in the day. She later called him and said that she was feeling unwell and intended to consult a doctor.





When the doctor was reportedly unavailable, Devi began making her way back. At some point, she apparently got onto a motorcycle.

Lal said he subsequently received a call from a person who was accompanying his daughter. The person told him that Devi had run towards the river.

The development prompted Lal to speak to his daughter over the phone. He said he repeatedly asked her what had happened and whether somebody had said or done anything to her.

Lal recalled Devi telling him, "Nobody should come near me."

He continued trying to understand what had happened and urged her to explain why she was behaving that way.

According to Lal, Devi responded, "No, papa. This is my own life. My heart tells me that I should go this way."

She then told her father, "Bye-bye, papa," before the call ended, he said.

Passersby tried to stop her

The moments before Devi jumped were also reportedly captured on video.

The video, which was said to have been recorded by passersby at the bridge, shows people attempting to discourage her. Despite their efforts, she reportedly jumped into the Chenab.

The footage later circulated widely on social media, drawing attention to the incident and the efforts of those present to prevent her from taking the step.

NEW DELHI: India and China are set to hold the first Corps Commander-level talks in the eastern sector on Sunday, with military officers from both sides meeting at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh amid unresolved issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), ANI reported citing sources.The meeting, scheduled for September 6, is expected to provide a platform to address the ongoing issues in the area. The talks will be held at Wacha on the Indian side, with India represented by 3 Corps Commander Lt Gen Girish Kalia, according to the report by ANI.The Indian Army's 3 Corps, based at Rangapahar, and 4 Corps, headquartered in Tezpur, are responsible for the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh.India and China have differing perceptions of the LAC, which has periodically led to face-offs and other issues on the ground. Until now, Corps Commander-level talks between the two sides have largely been held at the Chusul-Moldo border meeting point in Ladakh following the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes, in which soldiers from both countries were killed.The latest talks come after National Security Adviser Ajit Doval's visit to China for the 25th round of India-China Special Representatives' talks on the boundary question. Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed maintaining peace and tranquillity along the border and advancing bilateral ties.The engagement is part of a gradual improvement in India-China relations following a series of high-level meetings between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The two leaders have stressed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences should not be allowed to become disputes.Recently, Army Chief Gen Dhiraj Seth also visited the 3 Corps headquarters, where he was briefed on operational readiness and measures to strengthen the formation's combat capabilities.

World.title: India supplied 60% of diesel to Europe in August as Russian, US supplies plunge: Report
World.content:
Â Â Â Â India emerges as key diesel supplier to Europe

India supplied about 60 per cent of the diesel transiting through the Bab-el-Mandeb towards Europe in August, strengthening its role as a key source of refined fuel as Russian exports remain depressed and US shipments begin to decline, according to a report.Around 2,00,000 barrels per day of diesel, or gasoil, crossed the strategic shipping route for Europe last month, close to year-earlier levels after flows nearly stalled in March and April. Indian refiners accounted for roughly 60 per cent of that volume, energy analytics firm Vortexa said in a report.India, the worldâs fourth-largest refiner, has 258.1 million tonnes per annum of installed capacity, above domestic fuel demand. It exported 61.5 million tonnes of petroleum products in 2025-26, making it a major global supplier, PTI reported.However, sustaining these flows could become difficult. Indiaâs crude and condensate imports fell to about 3.8 million barrels per day in August from 4.8 million barrels per day a year earlier, data showed.Russian diesel exports averaged only around 1,50,000 barrels per day during the first 25 days of August, down about 6,10,000 barrels per day year-on-year and 81 per cent below the five-year seasonal average.The scheduled easing of Russiaâs diesel export ban from September 1 may not quickly restore supplies, with Ukrainian drone strikes continuing to disrupt refineries and export infrastructure. Vortexa recorded 32 refinery attacks across July and August.The Perm refinery, with capacity of 2,60,000 barrels per day, was left operating at only about 28 per cent of its crude distillation capacity after an attack, while no diesel cargoes have left Tuapse since a May strike.The US supplied about half of Europeâs seaborne diesel imports from outside the region in August, at around 5,20,000 barrels per day. But shipments fell from nearly 5,40,000 barrels per day in the first half of August to about 3,50,000 barrels per day in the second half.

World.title: IIT Mandi probes ‘Shudras serve higher classes’ poster; director blames some students’ interpretation
World.content:
IIT Mandi has ordered an inquiry into a controversial Bhagavad Gita-themed poster on its campus that said Shudras should “serve higher classes”, with Director Laxmidhar Behera attributing it to students’ interpretation of the scripture and distancing the institute from its contents.

Mr. Behera himself has a longstanding association with the teaching of the Bhagavad Gita and the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON). He teaches a three-credit Gita course at IIT Mandi and is the founder of the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, which describes itself as an ISKCON initiative.

“Some students have interpreted the Gita in some way. I have instituted an enquiry committee. It was a student-based event,” Mr. Behera told PTI on Sunday (September 6, 2026), asserting that he and the institute stood against caste discrimination.

In an email to the IIT Mandi community on Sunday (September 6, 2026), titled “Outright condemnation of recent poster display within campus”, Mr. Behera said he was “shocked” to learn about the poster displayed during Janmashtami celebrations on September 4 and stressed that it had not been endorsed by the institute “in any manner”.

“I have personally fought against caste-based discrimination in any form in every forum. I have instituted an enquiry committee in this matter such that the institute campus is never used for any such violation of social harmony. I fully empathise with members of our community who have been hurt by this incident,” he wrote.

Mr. Behera said the institute was committed to upholding “the values of equality, social justice, scientific temper” and other principles enshrined in the Constitution.

“The institute strongly condemns any form of caste-based discrimination,” he said in the email, seeking cooperation from the campus community to “stand together against such biases/discrimination in any form”.

Mr. Behera told PTI that the poster was prepared as part of a student-led event and that a committee comprising faculty members and representatives from different social categories, including Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes, has been constituted to look into the matter.

The controversy erupted over a poster titled “Bhagavad Gita - The Timeless Wisdom”, which was displayed outside the institute’s auditorium and divided society into Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras.

It described the role of Brahmanas as to “spread God’s message” and Kshatriyas as to “protect society and spirituality”. Vaishyas as to “drive economy, support others” and Shudras as to “serve higher classes”.

The poster also carried a verse from the Bhagavad Gita which said the four divisions of human society were created according to the “three modes of material nature and the work associated with them”.

Mr. Behera said he had been away from the campus and returned only on Saturday (September 5, 2026) and came to know about the controversy on Sunday morning (September 6, 2026).

“I have not seen the poster. I don’t want to take a side here and let the panel decide,” he told PTI.

Mr. Behera’s official IIT Mandi profile says he has taught the “universal principles of peace through the Bhagavad Gita” to young people for 27 years. Also identified as “HG Lila Purushottam Das”, he is the founder of the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, which its website describes as an ISKCON initiative.

The IIT director said ISKCON strongly opposes caste discrimination and teaches equality.

“ISKCON is the only organisation that strictly and strongly speaks against caste-based discrimination. In ISKCON, pujaris are also from the Shudra community. Muslims are also pujaris,” he claimed.

“We are against casteism in all forms. All occupational duties are according to guna and karma,” he added.

Mr. Behera also pointed to the representation of marginalised communities at IIT Mandi during his tenure, claiming that when he joined the institute, there were no faculty members from the OBC, SC and ST communities and that their numbers had since increased substantially.

An electrical engineering professor whose areas of specialisation include robotics and artificial intelligence, Behera has courted controversy over his views in the past.

In 2023, he asked students to pledge not to eat meat while claiming that landslides and cloudbursts in Himachal Pradesh were occurring because of cruelty to animals. A year earlier, soon after his appointment as IIT Mandi director, a video surfaced in which Mr. Behera claimed to have helped rid a friend’s family of “evil spirits” by chanting holy mantras.

IIT Mandi’s Indian Knowledge System and Mental Health Applications Centre also organised a conference in June featuring sessions on the Bhagavad Gita, Ayurveda and reincarnation, among other subjects. Behera, who was one of the general chairs of the conference, was also a co-organiser of a session titled “Reincarnation, OBEs and afterlife communication”.

World.title: CPI(M) area committee member Anas Ali accuses G. Sudhakaran of wilfully targeting him
World.content:
An area committee member of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] in Alappuzha has accused CPI(M) dissident turned Independent MLA G. Sudhakaran of wilfully targeting him to tarnish his reputation. Demanding the MLA to withdraw his comments linking him to drug rackets, M.M. Anas Ali, Haripad CPI(M) area committee member as well as vice-president of Haripad block panchayat, said he would file a defamation case if Mr. Sudhakaran refused to do so.

On Saturday (September 5, 2026), he broke down at a press conference in Alappuzha he had convened to respond to Mr. Sudhakaran’s allegations. Speaking to The Hindu on Sunday (September 6, 2026), Mr. Ali said he had shared a close relationship with Mr. Sudhakaran for a long time. However, things soured from the time Mr. Ali was appointed by the party to coordinate the Assembly election campaign in the Ambalappuzha constituency.

“I became part of the leadership of the Balasangam, Students' Federation of India (SFI), Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), and Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) when the party in the district was firmly under Mr. Sudhakaran’s control. For my wedding ceremony, he was the one who handed me the ‘Thaali’. Even the day before he decided to leave the party, we had gone to his house to convince him to stay. He had agreed also. These baseless allegations have come out of the blue,” said Mr. Ali.

‘Family affected’

He said that the allegations have affected his family members, who have not stepped outside the house in the past few days. “My wife has not gone to work for the past three days. Neither has my child gone to school nor has my father gone to the mosque on Friday,” he said.

In the press conference, he cautioned Mr. Sudhakaran that he will have to make certain revelations if the MLA continued to target him. This includes a fake social media post on a woman politician that Mr. Sudhakaran had allegedly sent him as well as an alleged attempt to suppress an issue related to the death by suicide of a girl in Thottappally.

He said he had sent a notice to Mr. Sudhakaran seeking ₹1 in damages, as a token amount to establish his integrity.

World.title: Delhi building collapse: Four rescued, several feared trapped
World.content:
A house collapse was reported near Shiv Mandir at Satya Niketan in South West Delhi at 01:33 p.m on Sunday (September 6, 2026).

Also read | Falling walls: On building collapses

According to the Delhi Fire Service, six people have been rescued so far, although the exact number of people feared to be trapped could not be ascertained.

The rescue operations are under way. JCBs have been called in to remove the debris.

The police are clearing the way and are asking people to move away from the site. Student volunteers from DU are helping in the rescue operations.

Eight fire tenders and multiple rescue teams of various departments were rushed to the spot, a Delhi Fire Service official said.

Police teams also arrived at the site and cordoned off the area as emergency personnel launched a search and rescue operation.

According to the locals, the building was five-storeyed and was used as a hostel for students from the nearby South campus. It is said that at least least 30 students were residing in the building.

A few workers who were working in the basement had left for lunch when the collapse occurred.

Visuals from the incident spot also showed a leg trapped under the debris, and fire officials are removing the rubble to rescue the person.

As of now, the Delhi Police have not issued a statement regarding the incident or the circumstances that led to the collapse.

The fire department is also working to determine whether anyone else remains trapped inside. Further details are awaited.

Police are repeatedly advising locals and onlookers to stay away from the site.

(With inputs from PTI.)

World.title: Tamil Nadu government mulling over abolition of State Planning Commission
World.content:
It is likely to be curtains for the Tamil Nadu State Planning Commission (SPC), a body formed 55 years ago.

The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government has not filled the posts of Vice-Chairperson and full-time members of the SPC after the resignation of the team appointed by the previous DMK government. By convention, the incumbent Chief Minister, C. Joseph Vijay, is the ex-officio Chairperson of the SPC. The Chief Secretary (M. Sai Kumar) and the Finance Secretary (M. A. Siddique) are ex-officio members. At present, the body has only an IAS officer as the Member-Secretary.

The idea is “to abolish” the concept of the Planning Commission, says a senior official. As its “only contribution” is to provide policy inputs, the government is considering subject-specific committees of experts, he says.

To cite an example, the government has put in place a committee, chaired by former Deputy Chairman of the now-abolished Union Planning Commission Montek Singh Ahluwalia, to recommend measures to strengthen own-tax and non-tax revenues; improve buoyancy; plug leakages; and increase fiscal self-reliance. Instead of having a standing body of experts, the TVK government hopes to derive more benefits by tapping, through different committees, into the services of various experts, according to sources.

The plan to do away with the SPC was first announced by the AIADMK government in March 2017. It was stated then that the SPC would be replaced with the State Development Policy Council (SDPC) to advise the government on policy coherence and formulation of programmes to guide the development of the State. The SDPC came into being in April 2020. Three months after the DMK returned to power in May 2021, the SDPC was rechristened as the SPC.

The content posted on the SPC website reveals that the SPC serves “as an apex advisory body which provides evidence-based policy guidance to promote holistic growth and development in the State”. In addition to the SPC, the services of the Department of Economics and Statistics (DoES) and the Department of Evaluation and Applied Research (DEAR) are utilised by the government for policy advice.

When the SPC was conceived in the early 1970s, the country was in the mode of planned development. Then, the new body’s brief was to assess the State’s resources and formulate a plan for their most effective and balanced utilisation, as reported by The Hindu on April 7, 1971. E.P. Royappa was made the Vice-Chairman after he was ousted from the post of Chief Secretary. After one more transfer, Royappa challenged the validity of his transfer in the Supreme Court, but lost his case.

There had been instances of civil servants heading the SPC: V. Karthikeyan in 1983 and C.V.R. Panikar in 1985. However, after M. Karunanidhi of the DMK came back to power in January 1989, the practice of naming the incumbent Chief Minister as the ex-officio head was revived. This has been the practice since then. Several leaders such as K.A. Mathiazhagan (1974), V. Ramaiah (1976), Kovai Chezhian (1978), M. Muthuswami (1983), V. R. Nedunchezhian (1992-the then Finance Minister too), and C. Ponnaiyan (2020) were made Vice-Chairpersons. In 2011, it was the turn of veteran civil servant Santha Sheela Nair to hold the post of Vice-Chairperson.

World.title: Ten dead after consuming spurious liquor in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar
World.content:
At least 10 people have died after consuming spurious liquor in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district, with authorities swinging into action and police launching an investigation, officials said Sunday (September 6, 2026).

Three Excise officials have been suspended and one line-attached by the Madhya Pradesh Government in connection with the incident.

Kirti Dubey, Assistant Commissioner (Excise), Sagar; Dilip Khandate, Assistant District Excise Officer; Proshni Ureti, Excise Sub-Inspector, Banda Circle have been suspended by the State Excise Commissioner.

Neerja Srivastava, Deputy Commissioner and in-charge of the Divisional Flying Squad, has been attached to the Gwalior headquarters, a government official said.

Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal said that cases of methyl alcohol consumption have been reported from two villages — Nauroja and Dogra — under Banda police station limits and that the matter came to light around 4.30 a.m. on Sunday (September 6, 2026).

“10 people have been identified as deceased. The post-mortem examinations and other procedures related to the deceased are being carried out,” Ms. Pal said, adding that the focus at present is on whether any more people are affected or are showing any symptoms in the two villages.

“A doctor's team is screening for such people, and officials like the SDM are on the spot. We are trying to identify anyone with such symptoms and send them to the Bundelkhand Medical College for observation,” she said.

“Interactions with locals have indicated that the deaths occurred after they consumed illegal, spurious liquor. Screening has already begun in the two villages,” Ms. Pal added.

Ms. Pal said that prima facie, based on the few postmortem examinations conducted, it appears to be a case of methyl alcohol consumption, and the connection of a spurious liquor supply gang from Uttar Pradesh’s Lalitpur has surfaced in the preliminary investigation.

“There is a gang from Lalitpur, U.P., which is involved in supplying methyl alcohol, and since we share a border with Lalitpur, we have received information that their chain in our area has also come to notice. Further investigation is underway,” she added.

Superintendent of Police (SP) Anurag Sujaniya said that about 12 suspects have been detained and are currently being questioned.

He also said that the source of the liquor is suspected to be in U.P.’s Lalitpur.

“Such activities have been found there even in the past. So, we are working in the same direction and will reach its main source soon. We have detained 10-12 people so far and are trying to establish a link through a systematic interrogation. We are also trying to curtail its movement, if it is anywhere else, to prevent anymore loss of life,” he said.

The incident comes after 13 people died last month due to the consumption of spurious liquor in the Bhavnagar district of Gujarat, a ‘dry’ State where the manufacture, sale and consumption of alcohol are banned.

Madhya Pradesh Congress leader Jitu Patwari said that this incident exposes the true nature of this government.

“This is not the first time this has happened. Madhya Pradesh has been taken over by liquor mafias. With great sorrow, I say that such incidents have occurred in Sagar before as well. I myself went there and met with the victims,” he said.

“Parents in every household are shedding tears of blood because of this addiction, and the government remains silent. I believe there should be a judicial inquiry into this, and the mafias should be behind bars within 24 hours,” he added.

World.title: Upper Bhadra Project: Trial run to Chitradurga branch canal begins
World.content:
The trial release of water from the Bhadra reservoir into the Chitradurga Branch Canal, under the Upper Bhadra Project, began on Sunday (September 6, 2026) — a moment elected representatives described as historic given a decades-long struggle of people of Chitradurga district.

Three TMC of water is being released as part of the trial run, launched at the project’s intake point on the Bhadra reservoir. The larger project is designed to supply water to 12 taluks across four districts — Chitradurga, Tumakuru, Chikkamagaluru and Davanagere.

Minister for Scheduled Tribes Welfare and Chitradurga district in-charge Minister, who visited the reservoir to witness the occasion, said the fruition of the project, after a struggle spanning six to seven decades, was a matter of great satisfaction.

He paid tribute to the individuals, associations and farmers’ groups who had campaigned for the project over the decades — several of whom, he said, were no longer alive to see it realised — and thanked successive Chief Ministers, from S.M. Krishna to incumbent Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, along with former Chief Ministers and district in-charge Ministers, for advancing the project.

Under the project, 17.4 TMC of water is lifted from the Tunga river into the Bhadra reservoir, and a further 12.5 TMC is drawn from the reservoir itself — together making up the 29.9 TMC that is lifted to the tunnel near Ajjampura. From there, the water is distributed through the Chitradurga Branch Canal and the Tumakuru Branch Canal.

The project envisages filling 367 tanks and providing drip irrigation to 2.25 lakh hectares. However, since the drip irrigation infrastructure and the tank-filling works are yet to be completed, the release has for now been restricted to 3 TMC on a trial basis. Mr. Raghumurthy said the arrangement would become permanent once the pending works were finished, and appealed to the public to cooperate without creating confusion until then.

MLAs K. Veerendra Pappi (Chitradurga), M. Chandranna (Holalkere), T.B. Jayachandra (Sira, and a former Minister), G.H. Srinivas (Tarikere) and B.G. Govindappa (Hosadurga), along with other elected representatives and officials, were present.

World.title: Migrant worker killed in Nolambur
World.content:
A 62-year-old migrant worker was killed after he was assaulted by a gang of four persons in Nolambur on Saturday (September 5, 2026) night.

City police said N. Abjith Mondal, a native of West Bengal, was working at a construction site in Gajalakshmi Nagar of Nolambur. Four persons from the same locality, who were in an inebriated condition, approached Mondal on Saturday night at about 10.15 p.m. and demanded a cigarette.

When he refused, an argument ensued, and the assailants picked up a wooden log from the ground and attacked him. He sustained severe head and body injuries in the attack and was admitted to Government Kilpauk Medical College Hospital by the residents of the locality. However, he died in the early morning on Sunday (September 5, 2026).

The Nolambur police arrested four persons - V. Vaseegaran (18), R. Ajay (18), S. Gokul Raj (18) and R. Sabari, for the murder.

World.title: Prohibited lands, KCR’s absence set to dominate Telangana Assembly proceedings
World.content:
The stage is set for the commencement of the monsoon session of the Telangana legislature on Monday (September 7, 2026).

The monsoon session, coming after the budget session which ended on March 30, is expected to witness heated debates on various issues, prime among them being the controversy over the inclusion of several private lands in the prohibited list (Section 22A of the Registration Act) that created consternation among house/land owners.

The main Opposition BRS, as well as the BJP, have asserted that they will “expose” the double standards of the Government, which was doling out land to private individuals and eyeing private individuals' land during the session.

While the Opposition members are gearing up to corner the ruling party on the furore raised by the affected landowners, the ruling Congress is gearing up to release a factual picture relating to the problems that cropped up with the introduction of the Dharani portal, which pushed many a landowner into crisis due to its inherent technical and updating of details

The Treasury Benches are preparing to highlight the inclusion of lands on the prohibited list under the previous BRS rule, the number of registrations carried out by relaxing the rule to benefit “those close to powers that be,” and related issues.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s challenge to Opposition leader K. Chandrasekhar Rao to attend the assembly proceedings or resign from the post is another major issue that is expected to dominate the proceedings.

The Chief Minister has been mentioning the absence of the Opposition leader from the House for a major part of the last three years, at a time when the Government had spent over ₹22.38 crore on his salary, security and other facilities.

“Employees will be dismissed if they fail to attend duties for a year or more. Why should Mr. KCR continue in the post when he is not attending the proceedings?” he asked, adding that the Government had spent ₹22.24 crore tax payers money towards salaries, security and other facilities that are being provided to the Opposition leader in the 1,000 days since the Congress took over the reins.

The Chief Minister’s assertion assumes significance in light of the reported claims of the BRS top leaders that Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao would return to the assembly as the Chief Minister after the party secures a full majority in the next elections. The BRS has decided to corner the Government on the implementation of the six guarantees, promises made to unemployed, youth and students during the session.

The session will see extensive debates on the proposed changes in the polytechnic courses, fee reimbursement to students, Kalyana Laksmhi/Shaadi Mubarak and other issues.

Meanwhile, Assembly Speaker G. Prasad Kumar and Council chairman G. Sukhender Reddy reviewed the arrangements being made for the session with senior officials on Saturday (September 5). They directed the officials to be prepared with answers to the questions likely to be raised by the Opposition members, and the Home Department has been directed to tighten security around the legislature premises without giving scope for staging dharnas or protests.

World.title: PM, president highlight Pakistan's growing role in regional security as nation observes Defence Day
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Zardari highlighted Pakistan’s growing role in regional security on Sunday as the nation observed its 61st Defence and Martyrs’ Day.

The day began with a 31-gun salute in Islamabad and a 21-gun salute in the provincial capitals, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported.

A change of guards was also held at the Quaid’s mausoleum in Karachi. A contingent of 64 male and eight female cadets from the Pakistan Air Force Academy participated in the guard-changing ceremony with Asghar Khan assuming guard duties.

Defence Day is observed every year on September 6 to commemorate the legacy of the 1965 war, which began after India launched an attack across the international border. The war ended with a ceasefire on September 22, and peace between the two countries was negotiated under Soviet auspices in Tashkent on January 10, 1966.

During this war, 1617 square miles of territory was occupied by Pakistan as compared to 446 square miles of Pakistan’s open and undefended territory occupied by India. The Pakistan Army had captured 20 Indian officers, 19 junior Indian commissioned officers and 569 other ranks.

PM’s message

PM Shehbaz paid tribute to the martyrs and veterans of the armed forces and their families on behalf of the entire nation in a Defence Day message issued by his office.

“September 6 is a glorious chapter in our national history, reminding us of the unparalleled resolve, unity and sacrifices demonstrated by our armed forces and the nation in defence of our beloved homeland.

“This day provides us with an opportunity to pay tribute to the martyrs and veterans who made immense sacrifices to safeguard Pakistan’s security, sovereignty and independence. Despite the enemy’s undeclared aggression and numerical superiority on September 6 1965, the professionalism and operational preparedness of Pakistan’s armed forces inflicted a humiliating and resounding defeat upon it on all fronts,” he recalled.

The prime minister added, “History bears witness that during the 1965 war, our armed forces displayed exceptional professionalism and courage, while the Pakistani nation demonstrated remarkable unity, resilience and steadfastness. Together they created a proud and enduring legacy in our national history.”

The prime minister also commended the armed forces’ response to India during last year’s four-day military conflict, Marka-i-Haq.

“In line with the glorious tradition of valiance, our armed forces, under the excellent professional strategy of Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmad Babar Sidhu and Naval Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf, delivered a response to our age-old adversary that will be remembered for generations.

“The entire nation is proud of our brave Pakistan Army, Pakistan Air Force and Pakistan Navy,” he said.

Referring to Bunyanum Marsoos —Pakistan’s military operation in response to India’s attack in the episode — the premier said its success added another “glorious chapter to our military history”.

“Our armed forces have once again demonstrated that the spirit and fervour of September 6 remain as strong as ever.”

He added that the challenges confronting Pakistan today demanded greater national unity and solidarity.

“Our traditional adversary, along with Fitna-al-Khawarij and Fitna-al-Hindustan, continues to pursue its nefarious designs against Pakistan, but these hostile forces are facing successive and decisive defeats. The sinister designs of hostile forces seeking to destabilise Pakistan through hybrid warfare shall be resolutely defeated,” he said.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.
